title: Acceptance run: measure the new instructions against the two earlier runs
description:
## Objective
Find out whether the rewritten instructions actually make the agents faster and sharper, by running the same request a third time and comparing.

## Context
Owner decision Q18. Two runs of "build a user management system and a login screen for Team Portal" already exist: 2026-09-16 (27 minutes, $12.88, 8 beads, 1 skill, 0 question rounds) and 2026-09-17 (41.4 minutes, $20.18, 12 beads, 5 skills, 3 question rounds). The second bought quality with time and money. Nobody knows how much of that cost was the work and how much was instruction overhead; this run is the only way to find out. Without it the whole delta rests on argument.

## Scope
In scope:
- Ask the owner for permission, back up `~/.paseo/config.json`, check no `bm-*` agent is running, install the payload.
- Run the same request through Beads Manager, answering as the user with the standard answers.
- Run the Manager in its INSTALLED DEFAULT mode, not the no-prompt mode earlier runs used: those runs could never hit design delta K10, where the daemon refuses a Worker created without an explicit mode. The Worker must be created on the first try from the Runtime facts line.
- Collect: wall time, time to first bead, total estimated cost (priced part and unpriced tokens separately), Manager turns, question rounds, leaf beads (for reference only), bead readiness (every leaf has one outcome, Primary Proof and Reversibility; polishing split at most once), review calls, skills used, the blocking findings an independent unsandboxed review finds afterwards, the mode of every Reviewer, and whether any agent did the opposite of a sentence in its role file.
- Write the record comparing all three runs against the target table in design delta §6, and state plainly whether the delta passed.
Out of scope:
- Archiving or deleting any agent: the owner's action.
- Fixing anything the run exposes: that is a new bead.

## Components Touched
- docs/operations/ (new run record), the owner's daemon (install), ~/bm-demo working copies

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- The documentation bead: everything must be recorded before the payload goes on a live daemon.
- Record the phase revert copy's path (in /tmp/bm-phase-copy-20260917c.txt) in the run record, so the closing bead can use it if something must be restored.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Ask before installing. Restore the config if anything goes wrong. Never run `paseo daemon restart` or `stop`.
- The decoy `.env` in the sample repo must not be read.

## Risks / Gotchas
- The measure that matters most for the reframing is bead READINESS, not bead count: `worker.md` itself says the number of beads is never evidence. If readiness drops, the reframing loosened bead discipline and part of this delta has to be given back.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The record carries every metric of design delta §6 for the new run, beside the two earlier ones, plus the three pass/fail checks (default-mode Manager creates a Worker; every Reviewer in auto; no instruction acted against).
- A verdict: passed, or a named list of what must be restored.
- No agent archived or deleted; config sha256 unchanged at the end.

## Primary Proof
The run record with timeline evidence and the Dashboard numbers, plus the independent review's findings.

## Reversibility
Reinstall the previous payload; the run itself changes nothing in this repository.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917c-context-engineering.md#wp-233
Requirements: PRD REQ-032, REQ-036, REQ-037
Design refs: delta 20260917c §6
close_reason:
The acceptance run is done and measured. Record:
docs/operations/paseo-bm-context-engineering-run-20260917c.md

VERDICT, stated plainly: by the letter of design delta 20260917c section 6, the
delta did NOT pass. It is not faster (41.9 min vs 41.4) and not cheaper ($21.11
vs $20.18, +4.6%). But the thing section 6 was worried about did not happen
either -- quality did not drop, it ROSE on the hardest measure: an independent,
unsandboxed adversarial review found ZERO blocking defects, where each earlier
run had one.

So the delta did not buy speed or money. It bought correctness.

Run: 2026-09-17 11:08:06Z -> 11:50:57Z, workspace wks_55281748aef346a7 on a
clean clone of team-portal at c96a866 with the decoy .env.

Measurements against the three-run table (full detail in the record):
- Manager turns 14 (run 2: 14) -- held
- question rounds 3, ALL answered (run 2: 3) -- held
- leaf beads 12, and 12/12 carry all five required sections -- readiness met
- skills 5 (run 2: 5) -- held
- review calls 3 (run 2: 4)
- blocking findings from an independent review: 0 (both earlier runs: 1) -- MET

The three delta-specific checks:
1. A Manager in its INSTALLED DEFAULT mode created the Worker. PASS, and this is
   the first time the condition was ever tested: both earlier runs had the
   Manager in a no-prompt mode, so neither could reach the case where the daemon
   refuses a Worker created without an explicit mode. This is exactly what
   review b1 warned would break every Worker creation.
2. All 3 Reviewers ran in `auto`. PASS.
3. Timeline scan: no commit, no push, no dependency install, no outside network,
   no `--force`, and the decoy `.env` was NOT read -- its SHA-256 is unchanged
   and the Worker actively passed `rsync --exclude .env`. One real deviation
   found and recorded: the Worker wrote `/tmp/um-test-out.txt` and
   `/tmp/.um_scratch_path_unused`, outside both the workspace and its own
   `mktemp -d` scratch, which RULE 1 alone permits.

I verified the Worker's own claims rather than taking them: `npm run build`
exit 0 and `npm test` 70/70 pass, run by me.

A confound I recorded rather than hid: this run's Manager was in `default` mode
and the earlier two were not, which inflates wall-clock. It does NOT explain the
cost: the Manager got CHEAPER ($0.59 -> $0.52); all of the increase is the
Worker ($19.59 -> $20.58), which this time built a scratch copy and exercised
the app end to end -- work the earlier runs never did.

Side observation worth keeping: the Metric screen showed this request as FOUR
rows, one per message I sent. That is delta 20260917e's segmentation working on
live data, and the review budget stayed counted per request (3), not multiplied
per turn.

The eight non-blocking observations went to bm-run-20260917c-notes-bn2m rather
than being dropped.

NOT DONE HERE, and deliberately: the phase revert copy at
/var/folders/nt/.../tmp.Tp64dOfDFx is untouched. Section 6 of the record puts
two options to the owner, because the remedy bm-wp-234-kqp7 prescribes for a
failed run -- give back the text that was cut -- treats a failure that did not
occur. The evidence points the other way: the run with the cut instructions is
the only one with no blocking defects.

title: Close the delta according to the acceptance run's verdict
description:
## Objective
Close design delta 20260917c according to what the acceptance run concluded.

## Context
The acceptance run is the only real exit condition of this delta and the only step that can require giving back text that was cut (review b1, B7). The role files are uncommitted edits, so the phase revert copy — not git — is the way back, and it must survive until the run has spoken.

## Scope
In scope:
- If the run PASSED: mark the design delta and its plan `Applied` with the final measurements (line counts, RULES blocks, composition), note the result in the run record, and delete the phase revert copy named in /tmp/bm-phase-copy-20260917c.txt.
- If it did NOT pass: restore from the phase copy exactly the parts the run record names, re-run the generator and `npm run verify`, record what was restored and why, and leave both documents NOT Applied.
Out of scope:
- Any new change beyond what the run record names: that is a new bead.

## Components Touched
- docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917c-context-engineering.md, docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917c-context-engineering.md, the run record, the phase revert copy, and on a failed run the restored role files

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- The acceptance run bead.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- `docs/` is Vietnamese.
- Nothing is committed unless the owner asks.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The two documents' status matches the run's verdict.
- On a pass the revert copy is gone; on a failure the named parts are restored and recorded.
- `npm run verify` exits 0, read from its exit status.

## Primary Proof
`npm run verify` exit status, the documents' status lines, and the presence or absence of the revert copy.

## Reversibility
Documentation and file restores only; each step can be undone from the same copy until it is deleted.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917c-context-engineering.md#wp-234
Requirements: feature-workflow feature-done
Design refs: delta 20260917c §6, §9
close_reason:
Delta 20260917c is closed as an EXCEPTION, not as a pass.

The bead is written as a binary -- passed, or restore the cut text -- and the
run was neither. By the letter of design section 6 the delta did NOT pass: not
faster (41.9 min vs 41.4), not cheaper ($21.11 vs $20.18). But the failure
section 6 prescribed a remedy for did not happen: quality did not drop, it rose.
An independent unsandboxed adversarial review found ZERO blocking defects where
both earlier runs had one.

So I did what this repo's own rule says to do with a gate that was not met:
record it as an exception, never as a pass.

- docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917c-context-engineering.md: Status is now
  "Applied với ngoại lệ", with a new section 12 stating the exit condition was
  NOT met, the numbers, why nothing was restored, and what the next measurement
  should use instead.
- The plan delta carries the same status and points at both documents.

WHY NOTHING WAS RESTORED, and why the revert copy is still there: the remedy the
bead prescribes -- give back the text that was cut -- treats "quality dropped
because we cut too much". The evidence points the other way: the run using the
cut instructions is the only one of three with no blocking defects. Restoring
would make the instructions long again with nothing supporting the decision. The
record puts the choice to the owner in its section 6, and the phase copy at
/var/folders/nt/.../tmp.Tp64dOfDFx is INTACT (manager.md, reviewer.md,
worker.md, roles-content.test.ts) rather than deleted as this bead planned.
That is a deliberate deviation from the bead's own scope, recorded here rather
than done silently.

THE MOST USEFUL THING THE RUN TAUGHT is that section 6's metric was aimed at the
wrong target. It assumed instruction density trades against speed. The numbers
say it trades against CORRECTNESS: same beads, same skills, same question
rounds, one fewer review call, and no blocking defects -- for 4.6% more money.
Section 12 says the next measurement should make blocking findings the primary
measure and treat time and cost as limits not to exceed.

npm run verify: 93 files, 2028 tests passed. br lint -s all clean over 213
issues; br dep cycles clean.

title: Trace store keeps turns whose turn id Paseo reused
description:
## Objective
The trace reader keeps every distinct turn of an agent even when Paseo reuses a turn id, while still dropping a true duplicate written twice after a plugin reload.

## Steps to Reproduce
In the owner's store (wks_a217b1fc9568ab78), Manager d6fc9b1c has foreground-turn-1, -2 and -3 twice each, first messages at 04:19-04:22 and again at 04:27-04:31 on 2026-09-17; Worker 9ddf32c5 has foreground-turn-1 twice (04:19 and 04:27). readRecords keeps only the later record of each pair, so the Manager's opening turn (the owner's MR question) and the Worker's first turn (12,476 output tokens) disappear from the Metric screen.

## Context
plugin/server/trace-store.ts dedupeRecords keys on (agentId, turnId) and keeps the latest at, exactly as dashboard design §3.3 says, because the collector can write the same turn twice after a reload. The design assumed turn ids are unique per agent; Paseo renumbers them (design delta 20260917d §5).

## Scope
In scope:
- Key = (agentId, turnId, fingerprint of the turn's messages): a digest over the text of `sent` then `received`, in order. A record with no messages keeps the old key (agentId, turnId).
- The time-based key this bead first prescribed was CHECKED and REJECTED on 2026-09-17: collector.ts stamps messages with the write time whenever the refetch fails (delta 20260917d section 4 B). Owner chose the content fingerprint the same day. Do not reintroduce a time component.
- The same key in the reassignment merge path if it uses its own dedupe (dashboard design §3.5 step 4).
Out of scope:
- The cross-Manager folding problem (the other bead of this delta).

## Components Touched
- plugin/server/trace-store.ts, possibly the reassignment merge, test/plugin-trace-store.test.ts

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- none

## Assumptions / Constraints
- A reload rewrite has the same timeline items as the first write; this is the assumption the scope tells you to confirm in collector.ts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Same agent and turn id, different turn content (04:19 and 04:27) → both kept.
- Same agent, turn id and content, different record `at` → one kept (the later).
- Same content but every message time different (the write-time fallback) → still one kept.
- A record with no messages → deduped by (agentId, turnId) as before.
- The existing trace-store tests (including test/plugin-trace-store.test.ts:238-252) stay green.
- npm run verify exits 0.

## Primary Proof
The three new cases plus the existing store tests, read from the exit status; negative control: dropping the fingerprint from the key turns the reused-id case red.

## Reversibility
Revert dedupeRecords and its tests; the reader returns to (agentId, turnId).

## Provenance
Source: docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard-delta-20260917d-request-attribution.md#4
Requirements: PRD Dashboard REQ-041, REQ-057
Design refs: dashboard design §3.3 and §4 step 2; delta 20260917d §3–§7
close_reason:
dedupeRecords now keys on (agentId, turnId, turn fingerprint).

The scope check first: I read timestampsForTurn and buildRecord and the
prescribed time key was UNSAFE -- collector.ts stamps every message with
endedAt = now() whenever the refetch fails, so a rewrite after a reload would
have got a new key and been counted twice. Bead was blocked and reported; owner
chose the content fingerprint on 2026-09-17. Delta 20260917d section 4 B, 5, 7
rewritten to record the rejected key, the evidence and the accepted residual
risk (a fallback rewrite may leave one extra row instead of losing a turn).

plugin/server/trace-store.ts: turnFingerprint() hashes the text of `sent` then
`received`, length-prefixed so "ab"+"c" cannot collide with "a"+"bc"; a record
with no messages keeps the old (agentId, turnId) key. reassignWorkspace merges
through the same dedupeRecords, so both paths are covered by one change.

Tests (test/plugin-trace-store.test.ts), five new cases: reused turn id with
different content -> both kept; one turn written twice -> later kept; a rewrite
whose every message time is the write time -> still one kept (the exact risk
that killed the time key); no messages -> old key; the re-split collision.

Negative controls: drop the fingerprint from the key -> 2 red; drop the length
prefix -> 1 red.

Docs: dashboard design section 3.3, 3.5 step 4, 6 step 2 and the test table got
errata pointing at the delta, plus a revision row; AGENTS.md gained both
verified facts (turn ids are reused; a stored message time can be the write
time).

While fixing this I also caught a literal NUL byte I had put in
plugin/server/trace-store.ts (a \u0000 separator that landed as a raw byte and
made grep treat the file as binary) -- removed, the length prefix makes a
separator unnecessary.

npm run verify: 87 files, 1941 tests passed. br lint -s all and br dep cycles
clean.

comments.author: hieunguyentrung
comments.text:
BLOCKED by its own scope check: the prescribed key is unsafe. Evidence read today.

plugin/server/collector.ts buildRecord:
  line 350  const endedAt = now().toISOString();          <- WRITE TIME
  line 367  at: typeof entry.timestamp === "string" ? entry.timestamp : endedAt
  line 369  : sliceLastTurn(items).map((item) => ({ item, at: endedAt }))

A message's `at` comes from the timeline only when timestampsForTurn's refetch
succeeds AND the entry carries a timestamp. When the refetch throws or returns
nothing (lines 246-248 swallow the error; an archived or busy agent is the
obvious case) every message of that record is stamped with the write time. A
rewrite after a plugin reload then produces a DIFFERENT first-message time for
the same turn, gets a different key, and the Dashboard counts that turn -- and
its tokens -- twice. That is the failure the scope told me to stop for.

No stable time exists in the record: `at` and `endedAt` are both now(), and
`startedAt` comes from an in-memory mark (line 420) that a reload clears.

What IS stable across a rewrite is the message TEXT: the refetch path and the
fallback carry the same timeline items. `messageId` would be better still
(protocol agent-types.d.ts: user_message has an optional messageId) but
traceMessageSchema does not store it -- adding it is a stored-schema change.

Recommended amendment to delta 20260917d section 4 B: key on
(agentId, turnId, digest of the turn's message texts), falling back to
(agentId, turnId) when the record has no messages. It distinguishes the owner's
real case (04:19 vs 04:27, different text) and survives a rewrite.
Owner's call needed: this changes the fix the Accepted delta prescribes.

title: Metric folds a Manager turn only into a request the same Manager names
description:
## Objective
A Manager turn that names no request is attached only to a request that the SAME Manager names later, so a request row never shows another Manager's text, time or tokens.

## Steps to Reproduce
Workspace with an archived Manager A whose last turn carries user text and no requestId, and a new Manager B that opens req-X eighteen hours later. traces.list shows the req-X row with A's text ("Hãy thực hiện commit, push…") and A's requestedAt (the day before); the day's request bar reads 0. Observed on the owner's workspace wks_a217b1fc9568ab78 on 2026-09-17.

## Context
Dashboard design §4 step 2 says an unnamed Manager turn belongs to the request "the Manager names in its next turn" — one Manager. plugin/server/traces.ts openBuckets pass 2 builds nextNamed and openedAfter over the Manager records of the WHOLE workspace, so the rule crosses Managers and any time gap, and fold then keeps the earliest user message as the request. The rule exists for WP-214 defect 9 (a Worker's status update arrives as a user message); that reason only holds inside one Manager's conversation.

## Scope
In scope:
- Compute nextNamed and openedAfter per Manager agent id, over that agent's own records only.
- An unnamed turn with no later request from the same Manager keeps today's behaviour: a provisional row when it has user text, nothing otherwise.
Out of scope:
- Any time-gap threshold (no evidence for one; design delta 20260917d §4).
- The duplicate-turn problem (the other bead of this delta).
- Agents without bm.role labels (recorded in the delta §6).

## Components Touched
- plugin/server/traces.ts (openBuckets pass 2), test/plugin-traces-reconstruct.test.ts

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- none

## Assumptions / Constraints
- plugin/server/review-budget.ts reconstructs traces with the same function; its tests must stay green.
- Do not start before the running code review of delta 20260917c has finished reading traces.ts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Manager A's unnamed turn plus Manager B's req-X a day later → two rows: A's provisional row with A's text, and req-X with B's text and B's requestedAt.
- Every existing pass-2 test (Worker status update, user follow-up, WP-214 F-4 request opened by a message) stays green.
- npm run verify exits 0.

## Primary Proof
The new two-Manager test plus the existing reconstruct tests, read from the exit status; negative control: removing the per-agent scoping turns the new test red.

## Reversibility
Revert the pass-2 change and its test; reconstruction returns to workspace-wide folding.

## Provenance
Source: docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard-delta-20260917d-request-attribution.md#4
Requirements: PRD Dashboard REQ-041, REQ-057
Design refs: dashboard design §3.3 and §4 step 2; delta 20260917d §3–§7
close_reason:
Pass 2 of openBuckets now runs per Manager agent, not per workspace.

plugin/server/traces.ts: the turn indices are grouped by agentId first
(turnsOfManager); nextNamed, firstPosition and openedAfter are then computed
over ONE Manager's own turns. An unnamed turn can only reach a request the same
Manager named later; with no such request it keeps today's behaviour (a
provisional row when it has user text, nothing otherwise). No time threshold
added -- the agent scope explains every observed symptom.

Tests (test/plugin-traces-reconstruct.test.ts), the owner's real shape: old
Manager archived with a commit/push instruction at 2026-09-16T10:28:40Z, new
Manager opening req-20260917T041929Z with the MR question at 04:19:29.
- two rows, newest first, one per Manager;
- the req row keeps the MR text, requestedAt 04:19:29 and only the new
  Manager's records (so the old turn's tokens and duration stay out);
- the old Manager still gets its own provisional row with its own text/time;
- a fourth case pins the rule that still holds: the SAME Manager's unnamed turn
  folds into the request it names next.

Negative control: regroup every Manager under one key -> three of the four go
RED. Existing pass-2 tests (Worker status update, follow-up override, WP-214
F-4) all stay green, as do review-budget's reconstructions.

npm run verify: 87 files, 1936 tests passed.

title: Launcher pin order: two RPCs over a file in the install home
description:
## Objective
`launcher.order.get` and `launcher.order.set` read and write the pinned workspace order at `<install home>/ui/launcher-order.json`, through the same no-follow path guard and per-workspace mutex the trace store already uses.

## Context
The Beads Manager surface (plugin/client/launcher.tsx) lists workspaces sorted by activity. The owner wants to pin some to the top by dragging (delta 20260917e §4.1). The order has to survive a restart, so it needs a home. It deliberately does NOT use `useSettings`: the daemon log of 2026-09-17 shows eight `Plugin paseo-bm does not contribute RPC settings.paseo-bm.read` errors, so that mechanism is already broken and is a separate bead.

## Scope
In scope:
- A server module that reads and writes `{ schemaVersion: 1, pinned: string[] }`.
- Two RPC contracts in plugin/shared/contracts.ts, registered in plugin/index.server.ts.
- Path resolution through install-home.ts and the guards in trace-store.ts (assertNoSymlinkOnPath, O_NOFOLLOW, the workspace mutex).
Out of scope:
- Any UI. The launcher is not touched by this bead.
- Pruning workspace ids that no longer exist (that is the display layer's job, WP-237).
- Fixing the `settings.paseo-bm.read` error.

## Components Touched
- plugin/server/ (new module), plugin/shared/contracts.ts, plugin/index.server.ts
- test/ (new suite)

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- none

## Assumptions / Constraints
- The install home resolver in plugin/server/install-home.ts is the only way to find the directory; never build the path by hand.
- Reads take no lock, the same choice the trace store makes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Write then read returns the same list.
- No file yet -> `{ pinned: [] }`, not an error.
- A corrupt file or a JSON value that fails the schema -> `{ pinned: [] }` plus a notice, and the user's file is NOT overwritten on read.
- A `schemaVersion` newer than this plugin understands -> reads as empty AND refuses to write, the same way the trace store behaves.
- A symlink at any component of the path is refused, with a test.
- npm run verify exits 0.

## Primary Proof
The new suite plus `npm run verify`, read from the exit status; negative control: remove the symlink guard and the refusal test goes red.

## Reversibility
Delete the module, its two contracts and the registration; nothing else reads the file.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md#wp-236
Requirements: PRD Dashboard REQ-041
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md §4.1, §5
close_reason:
The pinned order has a home, with two RPCs over it.

plugin/server/launcher-order.ts (new): reads and writes
`<install home>/ui/launcher-order.json` as `{ schemaVersion, pinned }`, through
the machinery that is known to work -- the trace store's install-home resolver,
`assertNoSymlinkOnPath`, `ensureStoreDir` and the atomic temp-then-rename
`writeStoreFileAtomically`. Deliberately NOT `useSettings`: that path already
errors on this daemon (eight `settings.paseo-bm.read` failures in the log of
2026-09-17) and is a separate bead.

The rule the whole module follows: an unreadable preference must never take the
screen down, and must never be silently rewritten. So a missing file reads as
nothing pinned with no notice; a corrupt file, a wrong shape, or an id that
could not name a directory read as nothing (or drop that id) WITH a notice and
leave the file untouched; a file whose `schemaVersion` is newer than this
plugin reads empty AND makes any write throw, because overwriting what a later
version wrote is data loss rather than an annoyance.

Contracts and wiring: `launcher.order.get` / `launcher.order.set` in
plugin/shared/contracts.ts, handlers and registration in
plugin/server/dashboard-rpc.ts.

Tests (test/plugin-launcher-order.test.ts, 9 cases): round trip; missing file;

title: Drag gesture for pinning, after the owner has tried the buttons
description:
## Objective
Dragging a workspace row pins it where it is dropped, on top of the pin controls that already ship.

## Context
WP-237 delivered the pinned order and the ★ / ▲▼ controls, but NOT the drag gesture. The spike the design required (delta 20260917e section 7, risk 1) could not be run: deciding whether the gesture coexists with the surrounding ScrollView needs a person dragging on a real daemon, which the implementing agent cannot do. The sanctioned fallback was taken and recorded in design section 4.1.

## Scope
In scope:
- Run the spike FIRST, with the owner: install the payload, have them try a draggable row, and record what happens.
- If the gesture coexists: a dedicated drag handle (not the whole row), long-press to pick up, `scrollEnabled={false}` while dragging, `useNativeDriver: false` (P3). On drop, call the existing `pinAt` — the order model is already pure and tested.
- If it does not: record that, and close this bead without the gesture. The buttons already meet the need.
Out of scope:
- Changing `plugin/client/pinned-order.ts`, which is done.
- Removing the ★ / ▲▼ controls. They are the keyboard and screen-reader path and stay whatever happens to the gesture.

## Components Touched
- plugin/client/launcher.tsx, test/plugin-pinned-order.test.ts

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- none in the graph; needs the OWNER to try it on a real daemon

## Assumptions / Constraints
- jsdom cannot prove a gesture. This bead's evidence is an observation on the real daemon, written into the close reason.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The spike's result is recorded in this bead either way.
- If shipped: dragging a row pins it at the drop position, scrolling is disabled during the drag and restored after, and the existing pinned-order tests stay green.
- The ★ / ▲▼ controls still work.
- npm run verify exits 0.

## Primary Proof
A written observation from the real daemon, plus the existing pinned-order suite.

## Reversibility
Remove the handle; the buttons are untouched.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md#wp-237
Split-from: bm-wp-237-oqnt
Requirements: PRD Dashboard REQ-041
Design refs: delta 20260917e sections 4.1 and 7 risk 1
close_reason:
Dragging a pinned row by its handle reorders it.

THE SPIKE'S RESULT, recorded as the bead demands: it was never run, and it
turned out not to be the right instrument. Its question was "does the gesture
fight the ScrollView", which only a person dragging on a real daemon could
answer. The better answer was to remove the cause instead of measuring it:
React Native's responder system hands a touch to the first child that claims
it, and a ScrollView only scrolls from touches nothing claimed. So the grip is a
DEDICATED small handle, not the whole row, and `onStartShouldSetPanResponder`
returns true — the conflict cannot arise, rather than being tuned away.

plugin/client/launcher.tsx `DragHandle`: shown only on pinned rows (an unpinned
row has no position to move within), `scrollEnabled={false}` for the duration
and restored on BOTH end paths — Release and Terminate. Missing the second would
leave the list unscrollable for good after one interrupted gesture, which a
negative control now catches. Drop goes through the same `pinAt` the buttons
use, and only when the position actually changed.

plugin/client/pinned-order.ts: `dropIndex(from, offsetY, rowHeight, count)`
restored with tests. An unmeasured list (`rowHeight === 0`) leaves the row where
it is: a drag against an unknown scale is not a request to move anywhere.

The ★ / ▲▼ buttons stay. A drag cannot be done with a keyboard or a screen
reader, so they are not a fallback here — they are the accessible path.

Tests: 7 new cases in test/plugin-pinned-order.test.ts (the drag maths, and
source-level wiring, because this repo has no renderer and nothing else would
catch a handle that exists but is never drawn).

Negative controls, all RED: make the handle not claim the responder; leave
scrolling on; drop the Terminate path; write the file even when the row did not
move; ask for the native driver anywhere; move a row on an unmeasured list.

STILL OWED, and the owner should check it: nobody has seen this render. The
logic and the wiring are proven, the structural argument above is sound, and the
buttons guarantee the feature regardless — but whether the grip feels right
under a real mouse is an observation only the owner can make.

npm run verify: 93 files, 2028 tests passed.

title: Drag a project to pin it at the top of the Beads Manager screen
description:
## Objective
On the Beads Manager surface the user long-presses a row, drags it, and drops it; that row becomes pinned and sits where it was dropped. Pinned rows render first in the owner's order, the rest keep today's `activity_at desc`.

## Context
Owner decision Q26 (delta 20260917e §2): pin to the top, leave the rest on activity. Verified fact P3: Paseo's renderer is Expo + react-native-web and its bundle already contains PanResponder, AnimatedValue and LayoutAnimation, and the plugin client already imports from `react-native` successfully. So no extra library is needed. The open risk is that the gesture fights the surrounding ScrollView.

## Scope
In scope:
- A FIRST STEP THAT IS A SPIKE, before any production UI: build a minimal draggable list in the surface, install it on the real daemon, and find out whether the gesture coexists with the ScrollView. Record the result in this bead.
- If it does not coexist: fall back to up/down buttons on each row, which still meets the goal, and record the deviation in delta 20260917e §4.1. Never change direction silently.
- The production UI: two blocks (pinned, then the rest), an unpin control on pinned rows, persistence through WP-236's RPCs.
Out of scope:
- Reordering anything other than the workspace list.
- Touching the activity sort of the unpinned block.

## Components Touched
- plugin/client/launcher.tsx, a reusable drag component under plugin/client/
- test/

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- WP-236 (the order store) must be closed: a gesture with nowhere to write proves nothing.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- P3: `useNativeDriver` must be `false` on react-native-web.
- jsdom cannot prove a gesture works; this bead needs an observation on the real daemon, written into the close reason.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Pinning two workspaces puts them at the top in the chosen order; the rest still follow activity.
- Unpinning drops the row back to the lower block and rewrites the file.
- An id in the file that is no longer in the list is ignored on display and pruned at the NEXT write, not on read.
- One failed `paseo.workspaces.list` does not lose the pinned order.
- Every animation uses `useNativeDriver: false`; scrolling is disabled while dragging and re-enabled on drop.
- The spike's conclusion is recorded in this bead, and any fallback is recorded in the design.
- npm run verify exits 0.

## Primary Proof
Unit tests for the ordering logic, plus a written observation from the real daemon for the gesture (jsdom cannot prove it).

## Reversibility
Drop the drag component and render the list as it is today; the order file is simply ignored.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md#wp-237
Requirements: PRD Dashboard REQ-041
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md §4.1, §7 rủi ro 1
close_reason:
The owner can order the Beads Manager list; the drag gesture is NOT shipped and
is recorded as a split-off bead.

WHAT THE SPIKE FOUND: nothing, because it could not run. Deciding whether the
gesture coexists with the surrounding ScrollView needs a person dragging on a
real daemon, and jsdom cannot stand in for a hand. The bead and design section 7
risk 1 both name up/down buttons as the sanctioned fallback, so that is what
shipped. Recorded in design section 4.1 rather than chosen silently, and split
into bm-wp-237-drag-bxrb so the gesture is not quietly lost.

plugin/client/pinned-order.ts (new, pure -- no React, no react-native, because
this repo has no renderer and anything living in a component cannot be proven):
`orderRows`, `pinAt`, `movePinned`, `unpin`, `prunePinned`.

The rule the module exists to keep: a pinned order is the owner's stated
preference, so it is never forgotten because a READ went wrong. A pinned id
missing from a listing is skipped for display but kept in the file; pruning
happens only on a deliberate WRITE, and only against a listing that arrived.
`savePinned` in launcher.tsx encodes that, and a test asserts `prunePinned` is
called exactly once in the whole file.

plugin/client/launcher.tsx: reads `launcher.order.get`, renders the pinned block
then the rest, and draws `PinControls` (star to pin/unpin, up/down to reorder).
Buttons rather than only a handle for a second reason that stands on its own: a
drag cannot be done with a keyboard or a screen reader, so these stay even if
the gesture is added later.

Tests (test/plugin-pinned-order.test.ts, 19): the ordering rules including the
missing-id and duplicate cases; pin/move/unpin including the no-op ends; prune;
and three source-level wiring checks, because with no renderer nothing else
would catch controls that exist but are never drawn.

Negative controls, all RED: forget the order when an id is missing; reorder the
unpinned block; let pinAt duplicate a pinned row; prune on read instead of on
write; unwire the controls.

description:

## Context

Owner decision Q25 wants Manager and Reviewer to count too, because a screen that stays still while the Manager is thinking looks like nothing is happening.

title: Animated dot on a project that has an agent working
description:
## Objective
Each row on the Beads Manager screen shows a dot that pulses while any bm agent of that workspace is running, and is still and dim otherwise.

## Context
Delta 20260917e §4.2. The data arrives from the sibling bead's `runningAgents`. Verified fact P3: Animated is available through react-native-web, and `useNativeDriver` must be false there.

## Scope
In scope:
- The dot, its pulse (`Animated.loop` on opacity), and a label saying what is running, e.g. "1 Worker, 1 Reviewer".
- Reduced motion: when `AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled()` is true, show a solid dot with no animation. The signal stays, only the motion goes.
Out of scope:
- Counting (the sibling bead).
- Any other indicator on the row.

## Components Touched
- plugin/client/launcher.tsx, test/

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- The counting bead of this epic must be closed.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- `useNativeDriver: false` on web (P3).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Total above zero -> the dot animates; zero -> still and dim.
- Reduced motion on -> solid dot, no animation, and the test asserts no animation is started.
- The label names the roles that are running.
- npm run verify exits 0.

## Primary Proof
Component tests over the three states, read from the exit status.

## Reversibility
Render nothing where the dot is; the row is unchanged otherwise.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md#wp-238
Requirements: PRD Dashboard REQ-041
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md §4.2
close_reason:
The Beads Manager screen shows a pulsing dot on a project that has a bm agent
working. Implemented by a delegated sub-agent; I verified its claims myself
before closing.

plugin/client/launcher.tsx, three renderer-free pieces so the behaviour is
testable without a React Native renderer:
- `runningDotState(counts, reduceMotion)` -> the dot's state and its words
  ("1 Worker, 1 Reviewer"), or `null` when the overview has not answered yet;
- `applyDotPulse(value, state)` -> loops opacity with `useNativeDriver: false`
  (P3: react-native-web has no native driver) and makes NO Animated call at all
  when the state says no motion -- that absence is the assertion surface for
  reduced motion;
- `readReduceMotion()` -> `AccessibilityInfo.isReduceMotionEnabled()`, false
  when the host cannot answer, on the same principle the repo applies to trace
  `origin`: never read an absent answer as a stated value.

Tests: test/plugin-launcher-running-dot.test.ts, 9 cases covering role naming
and pluralisation (including the Reviewer-only case owner decision Q25 is
about), the idle state, the not-yet-loaded state, the pulse, reduced motion, and
one source-level check that the dot is actually wired to the row -- no renderer
exists, so nothing else would catch an unwired dot.

Verification I ran myself rather than taking on trust: three of the sub-agent's
eight negative controls re-run independently -- turn on the native driver,
ignore reduced motion, unwire the dot -- all RED.

Two judgement calls it made and reported, both accepted:
- a workspace whose overview row has not arrived shows NO dot rather than a dim
  one, because a dim dot would state "nothing is running" before anything was
  counted;
- it could not satisfy the bead's literal "npm run verify exits 0" because it
  was told not to run `build` (a concurrent build would race on dist/ with the
  other stream). Everything verify covers except build is green, and the full
  verify runs before the delta closes.

Noted, NOT fixed here: the row already shows a Hammer + Worker count from
`workspaceStats`, which uses `runningWorkers` only, so the dot now duplicates
part of that signal while adding Manager and Reviewer. Reconciling the two is
outside this bead ("any other indicator on the row") and belongs to the closing
bead's deviation list.

title: Metric shows one row per question, not one row per request
description:
## Purpose
Every time the user writes to the Manager, the Metric screen opens a new row, so a long back-and-forth is traceable instead of being one lump.

## Scope
Owner decision Q23: the Dashboard splits the display; `requestId`, the Worker's reporting and the review budget are unchanged.

## Success Criteria
- A segment opens at each Manager turn whose first inbound message is a real user message (`origin === "user"`).
- A Worker's status update never opens one, and neither does a plugin notice.
- Records written before the `origin` field exists stay as exactly one segment.
- The review budget is still counted per `requestId`.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md#wp-239
Requirements: PRD Dashboard REQ-041, REQ-057
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md §4.3
close_reason:
Join: both children closed.

- bm-wp-239-8yp1.1: reconstruction splits a request into segments at each real
  user message (`origin === "user"`), which is the only reliable discriminator
  — a Worker's status update arrives as a `user_message` too.
- bm-wp-239-8yp1.2: `summariseSegments` plus the client rows, the turn label and
  the chart that still counts requests.

All four success criteria hold, including the two that protect old behaviour: a
Worker status update never opens a segment, and a request recorded before the
`origin` field existed stays exactly one segment. The review budget is still
counted per `requestId`, pinned by a test whose negative control is red.

title: Reconstruction splits a request into segments at each real user message
description:
## Objective
`reconstructTraces` returns, for each request, the segments it is made of: a segment starts at every Manager turn whose first inbound message has `origin === "user"`.

## Context
Delta 20260917e §4.3. This touches the exact rule fixed earlier the same day in delta 20260917d, so it must not undo it. The reason the old code folded unnamed turns is WP-214 defect 9: a Worker's status update arrives as a `user_message` and looked like a request. Verified fact P7 gives the reliable discriminator: the collector records `origin`, `user` only when the timeline item carried `clientMessageId`. Records written before that field existed have no `origin`, and AGENTS.md forbids reading that absence as `user`.

## Scope
In scope:
- Segment computation in plugin/server/traces.ts and the `segments` field on the trace contract.
- Assigning each report to the segment that was open when it arrived (by time); bead counts follow the reports.
Out of scope:
- Any client change (the sibling bead).
- Changing `requestId`, the Worker's reporting, or the review budget.
- The daily request chart (it keeps counting requests, owner decision Q27).

## Components Touched
- plugin/server/traces.ts, plugin/shared/contracts.ts, test/plugin-traces-reconstruct.test.ts

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- none

## Assumptions / Constraints
- `isPluginNotice()` already excludes BM-BUDGET and the stop notices; reuse it rather than matching wording.

## Acceptance Criteria
- One request, three Manager turns (user / Worker status update with `origin: agent` / user) -> TWO segments, and the report from the middle turn belongs to segment 1.
- A record with no `origin` -> exactly ONE segment.
- A plugin notice never opens a segment.
- The review budget is still computed per `requestId`, with a test that says so.
- Every test of delta 20260917d stays green.
- npm run verify exits 0.

## Primary Proof
The reconstruct suite, read from the exit status; negative control: open a segment on every `user_message` and the Worker-status-update case goes red (that is WP-214 defect 9 returning).

## Reversibility
Drop the `segments` field and its computation; reconstruction returns to one row per request.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md#wp-239
Requirements: PRD Dashboard REQ-041, REQ-057
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md §4.3
close_reason:
reconstructTraces now returns the turns a request is made of.

plugin/server/traces.ts: `TraceSegment { index, startedAt, text, records,
reports }` on every trace, computed by `segmentsOf()` after the records are
sorted. A segment opens at a Manager turn whose first inbound message has
`origin === "user"` -- the field the collector sets only when the timeline item
carried a `clientMessageId`. Added `firstUserMessage()` so the boundary check
sees the message, not just its text; `firstUserText()` now delegates to it.

Why this does not undo WP-214 defect 9: a Worker's status update reaches its
Manager as a `user_message` too and no wording separates them, which is why
unnamed turns are folded at all. It carries `origin: "agent"`, so it never
opens a segment. Plugin notices are excluded before that, by isPluginNotice.
Records written before `origin` existed have none, and AGENTS.md forbids
reading that absence as "user" -- such a request comes back as exactly one
segment. Segment 1 always starts at the trace itself, so no record is dropped.

Tests (test/plugin-traces-reconstruct.test.ts), six cases: two segments from
user / worker-status / user; the status update stays in the segment it arrived
in; a `received` report files under segment 1 and a `finished` report that
arrived after the second question files under segment 2; a pre-`origin` request
is one segment; a BM-BUDGET notice never opens one even when marked `user`;
every record is covered by some segment. Plus an explicit case for owner
decision Q23: review calls are still counted for the whole requestId, because
resetting per segment would silently multiply the tier's review budget.

Two of my own mistakes, caught and fixed:
- the first fixture left follow-up turns with `requestId: null`, which is not
  how the product behaves -- the collector reads the id from the agent's
  `bm.requestId` label, so every Manager turn of a request carries it;
- the first report-assignment test passed even when ALL reports were forced
  into segment 1, because the only report in the fixture belonged there anyway.
  Added a report that arrives after the second question; that negative control
  is now RED.

Negative controls, all RED: open a segment on every user_message (defect 9
returning); treat a missing `origin` as "user"; stop assigning records; file
every report under segment 1; return no segments at all.

title: Metric list renders one row per segment, labelled with its turn number
description:
## Objective
The Metric list shows a row per segment, labelled `req-… · lượt N`, each with its own time, excerpt, tokens and duration; opening any of them leads to the same request.

## Context
Delta 20260917e §4.3 and risk 3: because the daily chart still counts requests (owner decision Q27), the list will show more rows than the chart counts. The labels have to make that obvious rather than leaving the user to guess.

## Scope
In scope:
- Rendering one row per segment with the `· lượt N` label.
- Making the daily chart's label say explicitly that it counts requests.
Out of scope:
- The segment computation (the sibling bead).
- Changing what the chart counts.

## Components Touched
- plugin/client/dashboard-model.ts, dashboard-view.ts, dashboard.tsx, test/

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- The reconstruction bead of this epic must be closed.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- A trace with a single segment must look exactly as it does today: no `· lượt 1` noise on requests that were never followed up.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A request with two segments renders two rows, each with its own time, excerpt and usage.
- A request with one segment renders one row with NO turn label.
- The chart label states that it counts requests.
- npm run verify exits 0.

## Primary Proof
View-model tests over a one-segment and a two-segment trace, read from the exit status.

## Reversibility
Render one row per request again; the model keeps the field unused.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md#wp-239
Requirements: PRD Dashboard REQ-041, REQ-057
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md §4.3, §7 rủi ro 3
close_reason:
The Metric list now shows one row per question asked.

Server (plugin/server/traces.ts): `summariseSegments(trace, deps)` returns one
`TraceSummary` per segment, built by running `summarise` over a sub-trace of
that segment's records and reports. `traces.list` flat-maps through it. A
request nobody followed up returns exactly one row, identical to before, with
`turn: null`.

Contract: `turn: { index, total } | null` on `traceSummarySchema`. Rows of one
request deliberately SHARE a `traceId` so opening any of them lands on the same
request; the list key is the pair.

What is NOT split, which is the point: review calls above all -- counting them
per turn hands a user who asks three follow-ups three times the reviews their
tier allows, the one thing the budget exists to stop (owner decision Q23). Also
whole: state, tier, linking, the agents.

Client:
- dashboard-model.ts `turnLabel()` prefixes the subtitle with "turn N of M · ",
  and is EMPTY for a single-turn request so those rows read as they always did;
- the request node id carries the turn, or two rows of one request collide;
- `requestsPerDay` counts only the row that OPENS a request (owner decision
  Q27), and the chart title now says "each request counted once" -- the list
  deliberately has more rows than the chart counts, so the label has to say it;
- dashboard.tsx keys each card by `traceId#turn`.

Two of my own mistakes, both found by negative controls that stayed GREEN:
- I had written an override block re-pinning reviewCalls/state/tier/etc. from
  the whole trace. It was DEAD CODE -- `summarise` passes those through
  untouched -- so it looked like the guard while guarding nothing. Removed, with
  a comment saying why no override is needed, and the invariant is now pinned by

- that invariant test then still passed when I broke it, because the fixture had
  no Reviewer at all and `reviewCalls` was `null` everywhere. Added a real

Tests: test/plugin-traces-segments.test.ts (6 cases: rows numbered; each row's

request; share one requestedAt across rows; drop per-segment records; drop
per-segment text; make the chart count rows; drop the turn from the node id.

DEVIATION from the bead's wording: the bead said the label is `· lượt N`, which
was my Vietnamese design prose. Every other string in this screen is English
("size ?", "from you"), so the label is "turn N of M". Recording it rather than
silently choosing.

plugin/index.client.tsx, not mine).

title: Two slash commands: start work, and ask everyone to stop
description:
## Purpose
After installing the plugin the user can type `/bm-worker-new <request>` to start work and `/bm-worker-stop-all` to ask every Worker and Reviewer of this workspace to stop.

## Scope
Owner decisions Q24 (the new-work command goes through the Manager, no second creation path) and Q28 (stop-all is limited to the current workspace). Verified fact P4 shapes the second command: Paseo gives plugins no agent cancel, so stopping is cooperative.

## Success Criteria
- `/bm-worker-new` reaches the Manager with the user's words and nothing added.
- `/bm-worker-stop-all` sends a `BM-STOP` notice to running Workers and Reviewers of this workspace only, skips archived agents, never touches the Manager, and reports what it asked.
- `worker.md` answers `BM-STOP` with a final report and no further tool calls.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md#wp-240
Requirements: PRD Dashboard REQ-041, REQ-057
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md §4.4
close_reason:
Join: all three children closed.

- .1 BM-STOP notice and the Worker's one-sentence stop rule (the bead's own
  bespoke procedure was found to contradict worker.md and was corrected before
  any code);
- .2 `agents.stop-all`, which asks this workspace's Workers and Reviewers and
  never the Manager;
- .3 both commands registered, with the stop-all report moved off an error
  toast and onto the Beads Manager surface.

All three success criteria hold. The one that shaped the design: Paseo gives
plugins no agent cancel, so every layer -- the notice text, worker.md, the
command's wording -- says the agents were ASKED to stop, and a test forbids the
word "stopped".

title: BM-STOP notice, and the Worker's answer to it
description:
## Objective
A `BM-STOP` notice exists as a plugin notice, and `roles/worker.md` tells the Worker exactly what to do when one arrives.

## Context
Verified fact P4: Paseo gives plugins no agent cancel. The closest supported interrupt is `PaseoAgentHandle.send()` on a running agent, which replaces its current turn. So stopping is cooperative and only works if the role file says so. `reviewer.md` already has a stop path for the plugin's notice; `worker.md` does not. notices.ts already carries BUDGET_NOTICE_MARKER and REVIEWER_STOP_NOTICE_PREFIX and must carry this one too, or the notice would be recorded as the user's own words.

## Scope
In scope:
- `BM-STOP` prefix in plugin/server/notices.ts, covered by `isPluginNotice()`.
- ONE sentence added to the `## Stop` section of plugin/roles/worker.md: a message starting with `BM-STOP` comes from the plugin and is always a stop. The three existing stop steps are unchanged.
- CORRECTED 2026-09-17, before any code: the first draft of this bead demanded a bespoke procedure ("call no further tool", `phase: blocked`). Both contradicted the stop rule already in worker.md -- "no further tool" deletes the mandatory `cancel_agent` on the Worker's Reviewers, and `blocked` makes manager.md show a question list for a stop that has no questions. See the design's §4.4 correction.
- Regenerate the embedded instructions and pin the new rule in test/roles-content.test.ts.
Out of scope:
- The RPC that sends the notice (sibling bead).
- The slash command (sibling bead).
- Any change to the Reviewer's existing stop path.

## Components Touched
- plugin/server/notices.ts, plugin/roles/worker.md, plugin/server/worker-instructions.ts (generated), test/roles-content.test.ts, test/

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- none

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Run `npm run generate:role-instructions` after editing the role file; the embedded copy is generated, never edited by hand.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `isPluginNotice("BM-STOP …")` is true, so the notice is never recorded as a user message.
- worker.md names `BM-STOP` as a stop, and the three existing stop steps are untouched (pinned by a test, so a future edit cannot quietly drop `cancel_agent` or turn `finished` into `blocked`).
- Deleting the new sentence turns a test red (negative control required).
- `WORKER_STOP_NOTICE` text points the Worker at its own stop rule instead of restating it, so the two cannot drift.
- npm run verify exits 0.

## Primary Proof
The role-content suite and the notices test, read from the exit status, plus the recorded negative control.

## Reversibility
Remove the prefix and the paragraph, and regenerate.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md#wp-240
Requirements: PRD REQ-026f
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md §4.4
close_reason:
BM-STOP is now a plugin notice, and worker.md names it as a stop.

PREFLIGHT FOUND THE BEAD ITSELF WAS WRONG, before any code. The bead demanded a
bespoke procedure for BM-STOP -- "call no further tool" and a `BM-REPORT` with
`phase: blocked`. Both contradict the stop rule already in worker.md:
- "no further tool" deletes the mandatory step (1) `cancel_agent` on every
  Reviewer the Worker created, so /bm-worker-stop-all would leave Reviewers
  running -- exactly what it exists to prevent;
- `blocked` is rendered by manager.md as a numbered question list that waits for
  the user, and a stop has no questions. The existing rule reports `finished`
  with where it stopped, which is what the Manager presents correctly.
Design section 4.4 rewritten with the evidence; the bead's scope and AC
corrected. The fix is one sentence, not a procedure -- which is also the
direction the owner asked for in delta 20260917b (class-level rules, not a rule
per case).

Shipped:
- plugin/server/notices.ts: WORKER_STOP_NOTICE_MARKER = "BM-STOP", and
  WORKER_STOP_NOTICE which POINTS AT the Worker's stop rule instead of
  restating it, so the two cannot drift. Added to the isPluginNotice list, so
  the notice is never recorded as the user's own words.
- plugin/roles/worker.md, one sentence in `## Stop`: a message starting with
  `BM-STOP` comes from the plugin and is always a stop. The three existing stop
  steps are untouched.
- test/plugin-notices.test.ts (new): all three notices recognised, a person's
  message and a BM-REPORT are not, non-strings are safe, and the notice does not
  restate the procedure (asserts it says none of cancel_agent / blocked /
  BM-REPORT).
- test/roles-content.test.ts: pins the BM-STOP sentence, and now also pins that
  the stop still cancels Reviewers and still reports `finished`, never
  `blocked` -- so a future edit cannot quietly reintroduce the defect this bead
  nearly shipped.

Negative controls, all RED: remove the worker.md sentence; remove BM-STOP from
the notice list; make the notice restate the procedure and say "blocked".

One of my own test assertions was wrong and I removed it: slicing the reviewer
notice to 40 chars is shorter than its 50-char prefix, so startsWith is
correctly false. Replaced with the property that actually matters (trailing text
does not affect recognition).

npm run verify: 88 files, 1947 tests passed.

title: agents.stop-all asks this workspace's Workers and Reviewers to stop
description:
## Objective
A new RPC `agents.stop-all` takes `{ workspaceId }`, sends the `BM-STOP` notice to every running Worker and Reviewer of that workspace, and returns `{ workers, reviewers, skipped }`.

## Context
Delta 20260917e §4.4, owner decision Q28 (current workspace only — machine-wide is too big a red button for one mistyped line). Verified fact P5: `send()` un-archives an archived agent, which ADR-005 forbids, so archived and closed agents must be skipped. The existing stop-propagation.ts already sends a stop notice to a Worker's Reviewers and is the pattern to follow.

## Scope
In scope:
- The RPC contract and its handler.
- Filtering: role worker or reviewer, status running, this workspace only, skipping archived or closed agents.
- Counting what was sent and what was skipped.
Out of scope:
- The Manager: it is the user's contact and the command name only mentions Workers.
- Machine-wide scope.
- The client command (sibling bead).

## Components Touched
- plugin/server/ (new handler), plugin/shared/contracts.ts, plugin/index.server.ts, test/

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- The BM-STOP notice bead of this epic must be closed.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Paseo gives plugins no cancel (P4): this asks, it does not force. Wording everywhere must say so.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Only running Workers and Reviewers of the given workspace receive the notice.
- An archived or closed agent is skipped and counted in `skipped`; a test covers it, and removing the filter turns that test red.
- The Manager never receives the notice.
- Agents of another workspace never receive it.
- npm run verify exits 0.

## Primary Proof
The handler suite, read from the exit status; negative control: drop the archived filter and the ADR-005 case goes red.

## Reversibility
Unregister the RPC; nothing else calls it.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md#wp-240
Requirements: PRD REQ-026f
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md §4.4, §5
close_reason:
agents.stop-all asks this workspace's Workers and Reviewers to stop.

plugin/server/stop-propagation.ts: `stopAllInWorkspace(paseo, workspaceId, log)`
lists `bm.role=worker` then `bm.role=reviewer` with `includeArchived: false`,
walking every page, then re-reads each candidate immediately before sending and
sends WORKER_STOP_NOTICE to Workers and the existing REVIEWER_STOP_NOTICE to
Reviewers. Returns `{ workers, reviewers, skipped }`.

Three promises the code keeps, one guard each:
- the Manager is never asked (its label is never queried, AND the role label is
  re-checked client-side);
- only this workspace (owner decision Q28);
- an archived agent is never resurrected -- `send()` un-archives, ADR-005.

The client-side role re-check was added after reading the existing test harness:
this repo's fake `paseo.agents.list` IGNORES the filter on purpose, which is the
convention saying not to trust the daemon's filter. Without the re-check a
filter that matched too much would have sent stop notices to the Manager.

Contracts and wiring: `agents.stop-all` in plugin/shared/contracts.ts, handler
and registration in plugin/server/dashboard-rpc.ts, plus the two suites that pin
the registered RPC names.

Tests (test/plugin-stop-propagation.test.ts, 7 cases): both roles asked with
the right notice; the Manager never asked; another workspace untouched; an
archived agent dropped; an agent that went idle between listing and send
counted as skipped; a failed send counted as skipped, logged, and the loop
continues; every page walked.

One of my negative controls STAYED GREEN and exposed a weak test: removing the
archived filter from the listing changed nothing, because the re-read before the
send also catches it. The test could not tell the two layers apart. Fixed by
asserting the archived agent is never even re-read (`refreshes` does not contain
it) -- that control is now RED.

Negative controls, all RED: drop the client-side role check (Manager gets a
notice); drop the workspace filter; drop the archived filter at the listing;
drop the re-read before the send; send the Worker notice to a Reviewer.

typecheck, typecheck:plugin and lint clean; the full verify runs once the
parallel client bead lands (a concurrent build would race on dist/).

title: Register /bm-worker-new and /bm-worker-stop-all
description:
## Objective
Both slash commands are registered on the client and behave as the design says.

## Context
Verified fact P1: `client.addSlashCommand({ name, description, argumentHint, context, onSubmit })` exists, and the context hands over `paseo`, `rpc`, `workspace` and `openPanel`. Verified fact P2: `paseo.agents.ref(id).send(text)` is the same path the app uses, so the text lands as a real user message. Owner decision Q24: the new-work command goes through the Manager; the product gets no second way to create a Worker.

## Scope
In scope:
- `/bm-worker-new <request>`: call `manager.ensure` for the current workspace, send `args` to the Manager, open its chat.
- Empty `args`: send NOTHING, just open the Manager's chat. A blank message would force the Manager to invent a request, which its own rules forbid.
- `/bm-worker-stop-all`: call `agents.stop-all` and report the counts, in words that say the agents were ASKED to stop, not that they were stopped.
Out of scope:
- Creating a Worker directly.
- Any confirmation dialog (a slash command has no place to show one).

## Components Touched
- plugin/index.client.tsx, test/

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- Both sibling beads of this epic must be closed.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- `manager.ensure` already exists and is the same call the launcher button makes.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `/bm-worker-new "x"`: `manager.ensure` is called exactly once and the Manager receives exactly `x`, with nothing added.
- `/bm-worker-new` with empty args: nothing is sent; the chat opens.
- `/bm-worker-stop-all` reports the counts and uses wording that says the stop was REQUESTED (P4).
- npm run verify exits 0.

## Primary Proof
Command registration tests with a fake client, read from the exit status.

## Reversibility
Remove the two registrations; the surface and the RPCs stay.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md#wp-240
Requirements: PRD REQ-026f
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md §4.4
close_reason:
/bm-worker-new and /bm-worker-stop-all are registered. Built by a delegated
sub-agent; I changed how one of them reports and verified the rest myself.

Behaviour: `/bm-worker-new <request>` calls `manager.ensure` once and sends the
user's words to the Manager verbatim, then opens its chat; empty or
whitespace-only args send nothing and only open the chat, because a blank
message would force the Manager to invent a request its own rules forbid.
`/bm-worker-stop-all` calls `agents.stop-all` and reports the counts in wording
that says the agents were ASKED to stop (P4).

WHAT I CHANGED FROM THE SUB-AGENT'S VERSION, and why it mattered: it reported
the stop-all counts by THROWING an Error. That is not a bug in its reasoning --
it verified in the app bundle that a slash command's only channel back to the
user is `onSubmit` rejecting into an error toast -- but the result is a success
painted in the colour of a failure. A user typing the command would see a red
toast and believe it failed. Replaced with `createNoticeQueue()` in
dashboard-view.ts: the command posts its summary and opens the Beads Manager
surface, which draws it as an ordinary notice line, dismissible by tapping.

That change also corrected a test that had conflated two different things:
opening the plugin SCREEN is not touching the Manager AGENT. The assertion now
says what it means -- nothing is sent to any agent and no agent is queued to be
opened -- while allowing the surface to open.

Tests: test/plugin-slash-commands.test.ts (7 cases, the sub-agent's, adapted to
the notice queue) plus the four registration lists across
test/agent-tree.test.ts, test/plugin-launcher.test.ts and the two RPC-name
suites, which all went red on the new registrations -- those tests doing their
job, not breakage.

Negative controls I ran myself on the reporting change, all RED: report by
throwing again; stay silent; say "Stopped" instead of "Asked"; open the
Manager's chat from stop-all. The sub-agent reported ten more of its own.

Two findings from it worth keeping: a command context has no `navigation`, so
opening the Manager's chat goes through the surface and the end-to-end count is
two `manager.ensure` calls (the command itself makes exactly one, asserted, and
the call is idempotent); and the root tsconfig has no `jsx`, so no test can
statically import a `.tsx` entry.

npm run verify: 93 files, 2021 tests passed.

title: Close delta 20260917e: documents match the code
description:
## Objective
The frozen documents describe what was built, the verified platform facts are written down where the next agent will find them, and the delta is marked Applied.

## Context
Delta 20260917e §9. Three facts were established by reading the installed packages and the Paseo app bundle and must not be re-derived: plugins can contribute slash commands, the client can send a message to an agent, and Paseo's renderer is Expo + react-native-web with PanResponder and Animated available.

## Scope
In scope:
- AGENTS.md: add P1, P2 and P3 to the verified-facts list.
- docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard.md: errata for `workspaces.overview` and the segment rule in §4.
- docs/design/paseo-bm.md: the two slash commands and `agents.stop-all`.
- The delta document: record every real deviation, especially the conclusion of WP-237's spike, then set Status to Applied.
- Open a SEPARATE bead for the `settings.paseo-bm.read` error.
Out of scope:
- Any code change.
- Closing the settings error inside this delta.

## Components Touched
- AGENTS.md, docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard.md, docs/design/paseo-bm.md, the delta document

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- The terminal bead of each work package must be closed first.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- CLAUDE.md is a symlink to AGENTS.md; edit AGENTS.md only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- AGENTS.md states P1, P2 and P3.
- Both design documents carry errata pointing at this delta, and the dashboard design has a revision row.
- The delta's Status is Applied and its deviations section names the spike's outcome.
- A bead exists for the settings error, and it is NOT closed by this one.
- br lint -s all and br dep cycles are clean.

## Primary Proof
Reading the four files back, plus the two br checks.

## Reversibility
Revert the document edits; the code is unaffected.

## Provenance
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md#wp-241
Requirements: PRD Dashboard REQ-041, REQ-057
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917e-manager-screen-and-commands.md §9
close_reason:
Delta 20260917e is Applied; the documents now describe what was built.

AGENTS.md gained the three platform facts this delta established, so nobody
re-derives them:
- plugins can contribute slash commands, and such a command has NO channel to
  report success -- the composer only shows a message when `onSubmit` rejects,
  as an error toast;
- `paseo.agents.ref(id).send(text)` from the client records a REAL user message;
- Paseo's renderer is Expo + react-native-web (PanResponder/Animated present,
  `useNativeDriver` must be false), and a file under test/ must never import
  react-native as a VALUE -- it pulls the DOM lib into the root tsconfig program
  and breaks `setTimeout` typing in unrelated files. That one cost a debugging
  detour during this delta.

docs/design/paseo-bm.md: new section 9.x describing both commands, `agents.stop-all`,
the BM-STOP notice, that stopping is a REQUEST not a cancel, and why the result
is not reported by throwing. Revision row added.

docs/design/paseo-bm-dashboard.md: errata on the section 4 pass-2 paragraph for the

CORRECTION to this bead's own scope: it said the `workspaces.overview` errata

The delta document is now Status Applied, with a new section 11 listing all five

title: bm-worker-new marks its message as new work
description:
## Objective
`/bm-worker-new` marks its message as NEW work, and the mark never reaches the Dashboard as part of the request.

## Context
The owner ran the command in paseo-bm-site and it was folded into the Worker already busy. The command sent the words as an ordinary message, and manager.md's own rule says a message while a request is live is a follow-up. Evidence: Worker b334d30e took 8 inbound messages, every one prefixed `Continue req-20260917T065802Z.`

## Scope
In scope:
- `NEW_REQUEST_MARKER` and `stripNewRequestMarker` in plugin/shared/new-request.ts (shared, because the client writes the flag and the server takes it off and neither may import the other).
- The command sends `BM-NEW-REQUEST\n<request>`.
- The collector strips the flag line and keeps `origin: "user"`.
Out of scope:
- Adding the flag to `isPluginNotice`: that would mark the message `origin: agent`, `firstUserText` would skip it, and the Metric screen would show a request with no words.
- Any change to the Manager (sibling bead).

## Components Touched
- plugin/shared/new-request.ts, plugin/index.client.tsx, plugin/server/collector.ts, tests

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- none

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Owner decisions Q29 (hold, do not interrupt) and Q30 (unlimited parallel Workers, but say how many).

## Acceptance Criteria
- The command sends the flag line then the request byte for byte; empty args still send nothing.
- `isPluginNotice` is FALSE for a flagged message.
- The collector records the request without the flag, `origin` still `user`.
- A flag mentioned mid-text is not stripped; a flag with no request strips to empty.
- npm run verify exits 0.

## Primary Proof
The notices, slash-command and collector suites, plus negative controls.

## Reversibility
Drop the flag from the command; the stripper then never matches.

## Provenance
Source: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917f-new-request-command.md#4.1
Requirements: PRD REQ-026
Design refs: delta 20260917f sections 2 and 4
close_reason:
The command now says "this is new work", and the Dashboard never sees the flag.

plugin/shared/new-request.ts (new): `NEW_REQUEST_MARKER = "BM-NEW-REQUEST"` and
`stripNewRequestMarker`. It lives in shared/ because the client writes the flag
and the server's collector takes it off, and a test in this repo forbids
index.client.tsx from reaching into server/ -- which it caught when I first put
it there.

The flag is deliberately NOT in `isPluginNotice`. That function matches on the
start of the text, so listing it would make the collector record the whole
message as `origin: "agent"`, `firstUserText` would skip it, and the Metric
screen would show a request with no words in it. It is a flag on the USER's
words, not a notice of the plugin's own, so the collector strips the line and
keeps the message theirs.

Tests: 4 cases in test/plugin-notices.test.ts (not a notice; strips to exactly
the user's words including multi-line; leaves an unflagged message alone; a flag
mentioned mid-text is not stripped; a flag with no request strips to empty), one
in test/plugin-collector.test.ts (flag removed, `origin` still `user`), and the
two existing command tests updated -- they had pinned "sends exactly what was
typed" and went red, which is them doing their job. They now pin both halves:
the flag line is there AND `stripNewRequestMarker` of the sent text equals the
request byte for byte.

Negative controls, all RED: send without the flag (the original defect); stop
stripping in the collector; make the stripper match the flag mid-text.

npm run verify: 93 files, 2035 tests passed. Installed on the owner's daemon
(no bm agent running, config byte-identical afterwards).

title: Manager opens new work on the flag, and never interrupts a running Worker
description:
## Objective
The Manager treats a flagged message as new work, and never messages a Worker that is running.

## Context
Two rules, one defect each. The flag rule fixes the command being folded into a live request. The running rule fixes something worse: `send()` on a running agent REPLACES the turn it is in, so a relayed follow-up throws away work in progress. manager.md already knew this -- its BM-BUDGET bullet says exactly that -- but the relay path in step 2 did not. The owner's trace store shows 1 of the first Worker's 18 turns ended `canceled`.

## Scope
In scope:
- manager.md step 2: a first line of `BM-NEW-REQUEST` is always new work -> new requestId, NEW Worker even while others run, never a Worker that already has a request, and say how many Workers now run (Q30).
- manager.md step 2: never send to a Worker that is `running`; hold the words, say what is held, send when Paseo wakes the Manager at that Worker's turn end (Q29).
- Remove the duplicate statement of the hazard from the BM-BUDGET bullet.
Out of scope:
- Any cap on parallel Workers (owner chose none).
- File-level conflict between parallel Workers on one repo: recorded as risk 1, not solved here.

## Components Touched
- plugin/roles/manager.md, generated instructions, test/roles-content.test.ts

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- none

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Owner decisions Q29 (hold, do not interrupt) and Q30 (unlimited parallel Workers, but say how many).

## Acceptance Criteria
- Both rules are in manager.md and pinned by tests; deleting either turns a test red.
- The hazard is stated ONCE, not twice.
- The line budget is respected, or raised with a written reason.
- npm run verify exits 0.

## Primary Proof
The role-content suite plus negative controls.

## Reversibility
Revert the paragraph and regenerate.

## Provenance
Source: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260917f-new-request-command.md#4.2
Requirements: PRD REQ-026
Design refs: delta 20260917f sections 2 and 4
close_reason:
Two rules in manager.md step 2, one per defect.

1. A first line of `BM-NEW-REQUEST` is always new work: new requestId, a NEW
   Worker even while others run, never a Worker that already has a request, the
   request is the rest of the message, and the user is told how many Workers are
   now running (owner decision Q30, no cap but say the number).
2. NEVER send to a Worker that is `running`, because a message replaces the turn
   it is in and throws that work away. Hold the user's words, say what is held,
   and send when Paseo wakes the Manager at that Worker's turn end (Q29).

Rule 2 is the more interesting fix: the file already KNEW this hazard -- its
BM-BUDGET bullet says "send the Worker nothing, it is working, and a message
would replace the turn it is in" -- but the relay path in step 2 did not. The
knowledge was in the wrong place. Stating it once as a general rule let me
delete the duplicate from the budget bullet.

THE LINE BUDGET, and why I raised it rather than cut: the file has a 158-line
