title: New Manager starts in the provider's no-prompt mode
description:
## Objective
`manager.ensure` creates a new Beads Manager with `config.modeId` set to the provider's no-prompt mode (Claude `bypassPermissions`, Codex `full-access`) and the label `bm.modeSet=<that mode>`, unless the `bm-manager` profile names its own mode, which then wins.

## Context
The installer registers the `bm-manager` profile without `modeId` (ADR-006), so today every new Manager starts in Claude's `default` mode ("Always Ask") and stops on permission prompts. The owner decided (Q31) that new Managers run without prompts. The `bm.modeSet` label means "paseo-bm already set this Manager's mode": the sibling WP-244 work never touches a Manager that carries it, so a mode the user later picks by hand is respected (Q36).

## Scope
In scope:
- New function `managerModeFor(modes, profileModeId)` in `plugin/server/role-mode.ts`:
  1. `profileModeId` is listed by the provider → that id;
  2. else the first mode whose `colorTier` is `dangerous`;
  3. else `undefined` (leave the provider default) — do NOT fall back to `moderate` or `safe`.
  The plugin never picks a `planning` mode ON ITS OWN (step 2 only takes `dangerous`). A mode the user set on the profile always wins in step 1, EVEN a `planning` one (owner decision Q31: "a mode set by hand on the profile still wins").
- The create branch of `ensureManager` in `plugin/server/manager.ts`: read the provider's modes with the existing `modesFor(paseo, "bm-manager", log, cwd?)` (already raced against `withTimeout`, 5 s, and logs every failure), compute the target with `managerModeFor`, pass it as `config.modeId` and add the label `bm.modeSet=<mode>` next to `bm.role` and `bm.version`.
- Export the label key as a constant (e.g. `MODE_SET_LABEL = "bm.modeSet"`) for WP-244 to reuse.
Out of scope:
- Managers that already exist (WP-244).
- The `before("agent.create")` hook: `ROLE_GETS_MODE.manager` stays `false`; `manager.ensure` is the ONLY place that decides the Manager's mode.
- Worker and Reviewer modes, the installer, the profile, `~/.paseo/config.json`.

## Components Touched
- `plugin/server/role-mode.ts` — `managerModeFor`.
- `plugin/server/manager.ts` — `ManagerPaseo` gains an optional `providers.listModes` (same shape role-mode.ts reads); create branch passes `modeId` and the label.
- `plugin/index.server.ts` — only if a dependency must be passed through.
- `test/rpc-manager-ensure.test.ts` (and the existing role-mode tests, if any) — new cases.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
none

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Modes arrive as `{ id, label?, description?, colorTier? }`; `colorTier` is one of `planning`, `safe`, `moderate`, `dangerous` (read-only probe on the owner's daemon: `bm-manager` → plan[planning], default[safe], acceptEdits[moderate], auto[moderate], bypassPermissions[dangerous]).
- A failed or slow mode lookup must never fail the creation. Then create exactly as today: pass `profile.modeId` if the profile has one, add NO `bm.modeSet` label, log one line. The next open handles that Manager like an old one (WP-244).
- `bm.modeSet` is added only when this code chose the mode.
- Tests use the injected fake Paseo; nothing touches the real daemon.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Profile without `modeId`, provider lists `bypassPermissions`[dangerous] → create called with `modeId: "bypassPermissions"` and label `bm.modeSet: "bypassPermissions"`.
- Profile `modeId: "acceptEdits"` listed by the provider → that mode, label carries it.
- Provider lists no `dangerous` mode → no `modeId` (unless the profile has one), no label, one log line.
- `listModes` rejects or exceeds 5 s → Manager still created as today, no label, one log line.
- No profile mode, provider lists `plan`[planning] first and `bypassPermissions`[dangerous] later → `bypassPermissions` (a `planning` mode is never picked automatically).
- Profile `modeId: "plan"` listed as `planning` → `plan` is used and labelled (the profile wins, Q31).
- Negative control: making `managerModeFor` return `undefined` turns the first case red.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Every acceptance criterion above is met.
- `npm run verify` exits 0.

## Primary Proof
`npm test -- test/rpc-manager-ensure.test.ts` green with the cases above (including the negative control observed red, then restored), followed by `npm run verify` exit 0.

## Reversibility
Revert the edits to `role-mode.ts`, `manager.ts` and the tests. Managers already created with this code keep their mode and label on the user's daemon; the user changes the mode back in Paseo, and the label is harmless.

title: Existing Managers switch to the no-prompt mode once, when the Manager screen opens them
description:
## Goal
A Beads Manager that existed before this change is switched to the provider's no-prompt mode once, the next time the Manager screen opens it, and the user sees why when that could not happen.

title: manager.ensure switches an existing Manager's mode once through the paseo CLI
description:
## Objective
When `manager.ensure` finds a live Manager without the `bm.modeSet` label, it switches that Manager to the target mode with `paseo agent mode` and labels it with `paseo agent update --label`, once; every failure becomes a `modeNotice` string and never prevents returning the Manager.

## Context
The plugin SDK cannot change the mode of an agent that already exists: `PaseoAgentHandle` (`@getpaseo/client`) has no mode setter, `DaemonClient.setAgentMode` is not exposed to plugins, and `before("agent.session_open")` can only change `env`. Paseo CLI 0.8 offers `paseo agent mode <id> <mode> [--json]` and `paseo agent update <id> --label <k=v> [--json]`. The plugin already runs an external binary the same way in `plugin/server/setup-tools.ts` (`findTool` + `execFile`). Owner decisions: switch once per Manager (Q36), skip a Manager that is running (Q37), build this CLI path; any failure is only a notice (Q39).

## Scope
In scope:
- New module `plugin/server/paseo-cli.ts`: locate `paseo` with `findTool("paseo")` from `setup-tools.ts`; run it with `execFile` WITHOUT a shell, 5 s timeout per call; the runner is injectable so tests pass a fake. Before building arguments, check the agent id matches `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$` (never starts with `-`, so the CLI cannot read it as a flag) and the mode id is one the provider listed.
- The found-Manager branch of `ensureManager` (`plugin/server/manager.ts`), for the chosen (newest) Manager only, in this order:
  1. label `bm.modeSet` present → do nothing, `modeNotice: null`;
  2. no target mode (`managerModeFor` from WP-243 returns `undefined`, or modes could not be read) → do nothing (already logged), `modeNotice: null`. The target follows `managerModeFor` exactly: a mode set by hand on the `bm-manager` profile wins, even a `planning` one (Q31); only the automatic pick is limited to `dangerous`;
  3. snapshot `status === "running"` → no CLI call; `modeNotice` says the Manager is busy and its mode will be switched to `<mode>` the next time it is opened;
  4. `currentModeId !== target` → run `paseo agent mode <id> <target> --json`;
  5. run `paseo agent update <id> --label bm.modeSet=<target> --json` (also when step 4 was skipped because the mode was already right);
  6. `paseo` not found, non-zero exit, or timeout at any step → still return the Manager; `modeNotice` names the reason and tells the user to switch the Manager's mode in Paseo. If step 4 succeeded and step 5 failed, the next open repeats step 5 (step 4 then skips itself).
- `ManagerAgentSnapshot` gains `currentModeId?: string | null` (entries of `agents.list` carry it).
- `modeNotice: z.string().nullable()` added to the `managerEnsureRpc` output in `plugin/shared/contracts.ts`, and to `EnsureManagerResult` (null for a newly created Manager).
Out of scope:
- Showing the notice in the UI (sibling bead).
- Worker or Reviewer modes; any retry loop or background job; other live Managers of the workspace (they are only reported, as today).

## Components Touched
- `plugin/server/paseo-cli.ts` (new).
- `plugin/server/manager.ts` — found branch, snapshot type, result type.
- `plugin/shared/contracts.ts` — `managerEnsureRpc` output.
- `plugin/index.server.ts` — pass the runner/paseo lookup if needed.
- `test/rpc-manager-ensure.test.ts`, a new `test/plugin-paseo-cli.test.ts`, and the contract test that covers `manager.ensure`.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- WP-243 bead "New Manager starts in the provider's no-prompt mode" must be closed first: this bead reuses `managerModeFor` and the `bm.modeSet` label constant it adds.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Messages are English, like the rest of the plugin's user-facing text.
- Never change the mode of a Manager that carries `bm.modeSet`: that is how a user's own later choice is respected.
- Never archive, delete or restart anything; never run `paseo daemon …`.
- Tests inject the runner; NO test may execute the real `paseo` binary or reach the real daemon.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Running `paseo` from inside the daemon process can only be proven on the real daemon; that is checked at the owner acceptance bead (WP-249), not here.
- Switching a Claude agent's mode can rebuild its query, which is why a running Manager is skipped.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Label present → the runner is never called.
- No label, `idle`, `currentModeId: "default"` → exactly `["agent","mode",id,"bypassPermissions","--json"]` then `["agent","update",id,"--label","bm.modeSet=bypassPermissions","--json"]`.
- Mode already right → only the `update` call.
- Profile `modeId: "plan"` (listed), Manager in `default` → switched to `plan`, labelled `bm.modeSet=plan`.
- `running` → no call, notice mentions the next open.
- `paseo` not found / exit code 1 / timeout → Manager returned, notice non-null with the reason.
- Id `--help` or a mode the provider did not list → no call.
- Negative control: removing the label check turns the "label present" case red.
- Contract: an output with `modeNotice` still parses with a schema that lacks the field.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Every acceptance criterion above is met.
- `npm run verify` exits 0.

## Primary Proof
`npm test -- test/rpc-manager-ensure.test.ts test/plugin-paseo-cli.test.ts` green (negative control observed red, then restored), then `npm run verify` exit 0.

## Reversibility
Revert the new module and the edits. A Manager already switched on the user's daemon keeps its mode and label; the user switches the mode back in Paseo; the label is harmless.

## Provenance

Cuối cùng, quan trọng nhất, tôi muốn kiểm tra xem với mỗi model thì cơ chế cách nói instruction có cần tối ưu không vì thuâtj toán để nhồi instruction có thể khác nhau"

title: Manager screen shows the mode notice from manager.ensure
description:
## Objective

## Context

Paseo's composer cannot report success, so the plugin's own launcher notices are the only place the user learns why a Manager is still in "Always Ask".

- `plugin/client/launch-manager.ts`: `EnsureManagerOutput` gains `modeNotice?: string | null` (optional, so an older server still type-checks); the `opened` launcher state carries it; `describeLauncherState` adds `{ tone: "warning", text: modeNotice }` when it is non-null.

title: Each recorded turn stores the model, thinking option and mode the agent ran
description:
## Objective
Every trace record written from now on carries an optional `runtime { model, thinkingOptionId, modeId }` with the values the agent actually ran that turn, and one shared function returns a record's effective model (`runtime.model`, else `usage.model`).

## Context
The trace store already records the model of each turn in `usage.model` (taken from `snapshot.model`, the CONFIGURED model), but not the thinking option or the mode, so the Dashboard cannot say what each agent ran on (owner decision Q32, REQ-058). The collector already calls `timeline.refetch` every turn, and its payload's `agent` snapshot carries `runtimeInfo { model, thinkingOptionId, modeId }` (the running values), `effectiveThinkingOptionId`, `thinkingOptionId`, `currentModeId` and `model`. Example from a real Worker: `model` and `runtimeInfo.model` `claude-opus-5`, `currentModeId` and `runtimeInfo.modeId` `bypassPermissions`, both thinking fields `null`.

## Scope
In scope:
- `traceRecordSchema` in `plugin/shared/contracts.ts`: add OPTIONAL `runtime: z.object({ model: string|null, thinkingOptionId: string|null, modeId: string|null }).nullable().optional()`.
- `plugin/server/collector.ts` (`timestampsForTurn` / record building): fill `runtime` from the refetch snapshot, running values first, configuration only as fallback:
  - `model` = `runtimeInfo.model` → else `snapshot.model`;
  - `thinkingOptionId` = `runtimeInfo.thinkingOptionId` → else `effectiveThinkingOptionId` → else `thinkingOptionId`;
  - `modeId` = `runtimeInfo.modeId` → else `currentModeId`.
  "Else" applies when the field is absent, `null`, or not a non-empty string, so a provider-reported `null` never hides a real fallback; if the whole chain is empty the field is `null`.
- When `timeline.refetch` fails, `runtime` is `null` (same as `usage` today).
- One exported helper in `plugin/server/traces.ts`, e.g. `effectiveModel(record)` = `record.runtime?.model ?? record.usage?.model ?? null`, for WP-246 and WP-247 to use.
Out of scope:
- Any change to `usage.model` (keeps its old source so older plugin versions read new records the same way).
- Aggregation and UI (WP-246, WP-247).

## Components Touched
- `plugin/shared/contracts.ts` — `traceRecordSchema`.
- `plugin/server/collector.ts` — snapshot typing and `runtime` extraction.
- `plugin/server/traces.ts` — `effectiveModel` helper.
- `test/plugin-collector.test.ts`, `test/plugin-dashboard-contracts.test.ts`.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
none

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Persisted format rule (contracts.ts): a new record may only ADD optional fields. Keep `v: 1` and `TRACE_STORE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1`; no migration. `z.object` strips unknown keys, so an older plugin reading a new record ignores `runtime` and keeps writing.
- Never throw out of the hook: a malformed snapshot gives `runtime: null`, not an error.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Snapshot whose `runtimeInfo` values DIFFER from `model` / `effectiveThinkingOptionId` / `currentModeId` → `runtime` holds the three `runtimeInfo` values (negative control: inverting the priority turns this red).
- No `runtimeInfo` → `snapshot.model`, `effectiveThinkingOptionId` → `thinkingOptionId`, `currentModeId`; no thinking value anywhere → `null`.
- `runtimeInfo.modeId: null` with `currentModeId: "auto"` → `modeId: "auto"`.
- `refetch` rejects → `runtime: null`, `usage: null`.
- A record with `runtime` parses with a copy of the schema WITHOUT the field; an old record without it parses with the new schema; `v` and the store version are still 1.
- `usage.model` unchanged for the same input.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Every acceptance criterion above is met.
- `npm run verify` exits 0.

## Primary Proof
`npm test -- test/plugin-collector.test.ts test/plugin-dashboard-contracts.test.ts` green (negative control observed red, then restored), then `npm run verify` exit 0.

## Reversibility
Revert the edits. Records already written with `runtime` stay readable after the revert because the schema strips unknown keys; nothing to migrate or delete.

## Provenance

title: Trace reconstruction returns runtime rows per agent and usage by effective model
description:
## Objective
`traces.get` returns, for each agent in `usageByAgent`, a `runtime` list of rows `{ model, thinkingOptionId, modeId, recorded, turns }`, plus `TraceDetail.usageByModel`, and `usageOfTrace` prices tokens grouped by the effective model.

## Context
WP-245 made each new trace record carry `runtime` and added `effectiveModel(record)` = `runtime.model` → `usage.model`. The Dashboard needs these per agent and per model (REQ-058 a–d). The owner accepted (Q38) that cost is grouped by the effective model; today `usageOfTrace` groups by `usage.model`, so the only number that changes is a turn whose profile left the model empty (`usage.model` null, `runtime.model` set): its tokens, "unpriced" today, get priced.

## Scope
In scope:
- `plugin/shared/contracts.ts`: `usageByAgent[]` entries gain `runtime: z.array(z.object({ model: string|null, thinkingOptionId: string|null, modeId: string|null, recorded: boolean, turns: int>=1 }))`; `traceDetail` gains `usageByModel: z.array(z.object({ model: string|null, usage: usageSchema }))`. Both additive.
- `plugin/server/traces.ts`: build the rows. Each turn record of the agent contributes to exactly ONE row:

  | record | model | thinkingOptionId, modeId | recorded |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | has `runtime` | `effectiveModel(record)` | from `runtime` | true |
  | no `runtime`, has `usage.model` | `usage.model` | null | false |
  | neither | null | null | false |

  Rows are distinct tuples `(model, thinkingOptionId, modeId, recorded)` with `turns` counted, ordered by the first turn that produced them. There is no separate "unrecorded" counter.
- `usageByModel`: tokens per effective model (strip a `provider/` prefix the same way `usageOfTrace` does today), priced with the existing price function; model without a price → `costUsd: null`, tokens still shown.
- `usageOfTrace`: group by the effective model instead of `usage.model`.
- `plugin/server/dashboard-rpc.ts` only if the new fields must be threaded through.
Out of scope:
- Rendering (sibling bead); the overview block (WP-247); the price table.

## Components Touched
- `plugin/shared/contracts.ts`, `plugin/server/traces.ts`, possibly `plugin/server/dashboard-rpc.ts`.
- `test/plugin-traces-reconstruct.test.ts`, `test/plugin-dashboard-contracts.test.ts`, `test/rpc-list-describe.test.ts` only if the RPC shape is asserted there.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- WP-245 bead "Each recorded turn stores the model, thinking option and mode the agent ran" must be closed first: it adds `runtime` and `effectiveModel`.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Keep every existing `usageOfTrace` test green except where the effective-model key is the point; if an existing expectation must change, it may only be the empty-profile-model case described above — anything else means the change is wrong.
- The Manager is part of `usageByAgent` (role `manager`); the same rows apply to it.

## Acceptance Criteria
- One Worker with 3 turns `claude-opus-5 / null / bypassPermissions` and 1 turn `claude-opus-5 / high / bypassPermissions` → two rows, `recorded: true`, turns 3 and 1, in that order.
- 2 old turns without `runtime`, `usage.model: "claude-opus-5"` → one row `{ model: "claude-opus-5", thinkingOptionId: null, modeId: null, recorded: false, turns: 2 }`.
- 1 turn with neither → row `{ model: null, …, recorded: false, turns: 1 }`.
- `usageByModel` token sums equal the request's total tokens; the request's `costUsd` equals the sum of the priced parts.
- Empty-profile-model case (`usage.model` null, `runtime.model` `claude-opus-5`) is priced as `claude-opus-5` — red if `usageOfTrace` still groups by `usage.model`.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Every acceptance criterion above is met.
- `npm run verify` exits 0.

## Primary Proof
`npm test -- test/plugin-traces-reconstruct.test.ts test/plugin-dashboard-contracts.test.ts` green including the empty-profile-model case, then `npm run verify` exit 0.

## Reversibility
Revert the edits; stored records are untouched (this bead only reads them).

## Provenance

Requirements: REQ-058 (a)–(d); owner decision Q38
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260918-manager-mode-model-metrics.md §4.3 (table "Một lượt góp vào dòng nào", "Giá theo model hiệu lực")

title: Write the report on how role instructions reach each model
description:
## Objective
Write `docs/design/paseo-bm-research-20260918-instructions-by-model.md` (Vietnamese): a sourced report that answers, for Claude Code / `claude-opus-5` and Codex / `gpt-5.6-sol` (plus one paragraph on OpenCode), whether the way paseo-bm delivers and words its role instructions needs per-model optimisation, ending in a ranked list of recommendations.

## Context
The owner called this the most important part of the request: the algorithm that "stuffs" instructions into the context may differ per model. Already verified in the installed Paseo 0.8 bundle (`/Applications/Paseo.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar`, `@getpaseo/server/dist/server/server/agent/providers/`): Claude receives the role file APPENDED to the `claude_code` preset system prompt (`systemPrompt: { type: "preset", preset: "claude_code", append }`, with `CLAUDE.md` loaded via `settingSources`); Codex receives it as `developerInstructions` at thread start (after a collaboration mode's own `developer_instructions` when one applies); OpenCode as `system`. The daemon's own append prompt follows the role text in all three. Each agent snapshot stores the exact prompt it got in `persistence.metadata.systemPrompt`. Current roles: Manager and Worker on `claude-opus-5`, Reviewer on `gpt-5.6-sol`. The owner's standing preference for agent prompts: a few class-level limits plus positive instructions, not a growing list of bans (delta 20260917c).

## Scope
In scope — answer six questions, each with a separate conclusion per provider:
- R1 Where the role text sits in the context: message role (system / developer), position relative to the tool's preset prompt, repo `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`, skill listings, MCP tool descriptions, the daemon's append.
- R2 How large the role text is relative to the rest, and what comes after it (character counts, token estimates with the method stated).
- R3 What each vendor's current public prompting guidance says about emphasis (CAPITALS, bold NEVER), examples, structure (tables, XML, Markdown), length, conflicting instruction layers, and system vs developer placement — URL and date read for every claim.
- R4 What the existing traces show per model: `BM-REPORT` / `BM-REVIEW` completeness (`incompleteFields`, `unparsedFields`), questions asked, visible limit breaches in the evidence (git, dependency installs, network), behaviour when stopped — with counts and how they were computed.
- R5 Which features of the three current role files are likely to act differently per model.
- R6 Conclusion: is per-model optimisation needed; if so a ranked list, each item with impact, cost, risk, how to measure, and whether it is "one text for all models" or "a per-provider variant".
Out of scope:
- ANY edit to `plugin/roles/*.md`, the hook, or the generated instruction files (owner decision Q33) — recommendations are for the owner to decide later.
- A live measurement run on the daemon; creating agents.

## Components Touched
- `docs/design/paseo-bm-research-20260918-instructions-by-model.md` (new).
- Read only: the Paseo bundle (extract the needed files from `app.asar` into a `mktemp -d` directory with a small script that parses the asar header), agent snapshots via Paseo's `get_agent_status`, the trace store `~/.paseo-bm/traces/*/events-*.jsonl`, `docs/operations/*run*.md`, `plugin/roles/*.md`.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
none

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Network: ONLY read-only fetches of Anthropic's and OpenAI's public prompting documentation (owner decision Q34). No package downloads, no API calls, nothing else online.
- Never read secrets: skip `~/.paseo/config.json` and any provider auth file; read profiles with Paseo's `list_profiles` instead.
- Every claim carries its source (file and line, URL and date, or the trace measurement and its method); inference is labelled as inference.
- Delete the scratch directory when done.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The report has sections R1–R6, each with a conclusion for Claude Code and for Codex, plus the OpenCode paragraph.
- R4 contains numbers computed from the trace store and states the computation.
- R6 is a ranked list with impact, cost, risk, measurement, and "one text / per-provider variant" per item.
- `git status --short plugin/roles` prints nothing; the scratch directory no longer exists.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- Every acceptance criterion above is met and its evidence read back.

## Primary Proof
The report read back section by section against R1–R6, every claim with a source; `git status --short plugin/roles` empty; `ls <scratch dir>` fails.

## Reversibility
Delete the new report file; nothing else changes.

title: Add the BM-QUESTIONS reader and BM-ANSWERS composer in plugin/shared/bm-questions.ts
description:
## Objective
Add `plugin/shared/bm-questions.ts` with `parseQuestions(text)` (reads the last `BM-QUESTIONS` block of a message) and `answersText(requestId, questions, picks)` (writes a `BM-ANSWERS` block), proved by a new test file, plus one test showing `parseReports` is unchanged by a trailing `BM-QUESTIONS` block.

## Context
Workers will put their questions in a `BM-QUESTIONS` block right after `BM-REPORT` in the same message, and answers come back as `BM-ANSWERS`. The chat card (bead for WP-253) needs a pure, bounded reader and composer shared by client code. Model-written input is sloppy, so the reader is forgiving, like the `BM-REPORT` reader in `plugin/shared/bm-report.ts`.

## Scope
In: the new module, `test/plugin-bm-questions.test.ts`, ONE new case in `test/plugin-bm-report.test.ts`.
Out: any change to `plugin/shared/bm-report.ts`, `contracts.ts`, the collector, the trace store, the card, role files.

## Components Touched
- `plugin/shared/bm-questions.ts` (new) — pure: no React, no `server/` import.
- `test/plugin-bm-questions.test.ts` (new).
- `test/plugin-bm-report.test.ts` — one invariance case.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
none

## Assumptions / Constraints
Exact API:
```ts
export interface QuestionOption { key: string; text: string; recommended: boolean }
export interface Question { id: string; text: string; options: QuestionOption[] }
export interface QuestionSet { requestId: string | null; questions: Question[] }
export function parseQuestions(text: string): QuestionSet | null;
export type Pick = { key: string } | { other: string };
export function answersText(requestId: string, questions: readonly Question[], picks: Readonly<Record<string, Pick>>): string;
```
The block as Workers write it:
```
BM-QUESTIONS
requestId: req-20260917T010956Z
Q1: Storage — the request says "save the user list" but not where.
- a: the existing Postgres `users` table: no migration, ready today. (recommended)
- b: a new table: needs a migration, which makes this request Large.
- c: a file on disk: simplest, but two writers can lose data.
Q2: Existing sessions — renaming the session cookie signs everyone out.
- a: keep the old name: nobody is signed out. (recommended)
- b: rename it: everyone signs in again, once.
```
Reader rules:
- Returns the LAST block in the message, or null when there is none.
- Marker: `BM-QUESTIONS` alone on its line; tolerate a leading `>`, `-`, `**…**`, and code fences before/after.
- Question line: `Q<n>` then `:`, `.` or `)`; tolerate `**Q1:**` and `- Q1:`; id normalised to `Q<n>`; `text` = the rest.
- Option line needs a bullet or parentheses: `- a: …`, `- (a) …`, `- a) …`, `(a) …`, `a) …`; key lowercased. Prose starting with `a: ` without bullet/parenthesis is NOT an option.
- `(recommended)` or `[recommended]` (any case) marks the option and is removed from `text`. More than one marked in a question → none recommended.
- A line indented by 2+ spaces that is not an option continues the question/option above; blank lines are skipped.
- The block ends at another marker (`BM-REPORT`, `BM-REVIEW`, `BM-QUESTIONS`, `BM-ANSWERS`), a closing fence, or an unindented prose line.
- Duplicate question id → keep the first; duplicate option key inside a question → keep the first.
- Bounds: first a line-by-line pass over the WHOLE message finds the last marker (one anchored regex per line, no nested quantifiers); then read at most 20 000 characters FROM that marker; at most 10 questions and 8 options each; each text cut at 1000 characters with `…`.
- A question with fewer than 2 options is still returned.
- `requestId:` inside the block is optional (null when absent); strip wrapping backticks/asterisks from its value as `valueOrNull` in `bm-report.ts` does.

Composer output, in question order, one line per question; newlines inside `other` become spaces:
```
BM-ANSWERS
requestId: <requestId>
Q1: a — <the option text exactly as parsed>
Q2: other — <the user's words>
```
Ids not in `questions` are ignored. A question without a pick (or an `other` that is blank after trim) THROWS, so a programming error never sends a partial answer.

## Risks / Gotchas
- Do not modify `plugin/shared/bm-report.ts`: `BM-REPORT` is a consumed contract (Dashboard PRD REQ-050) and a line without `:` like `BM-QUESTIONS` already ends a report block.
- Quadratic regexes on crafted input were a real bug before (40 KB took 1.6 s in review bm-wp-220-nvk.1).

## Acceptance Criteria
- The example block above → 2 questions with 3 and 2 options, `recommended` on `Q1.a` and `Q2.a`, the right `requestId`, no `(recommended)` left in any text.
- One case each for these tolerated shapes: fences, `>` quoting, `**Q1:**`, `- (a)`, `a)`, continuation line.
- One case each for: two recommended (→ none), duplicate id, duplicate key, prose `a: …` not an option, block ending at prose, no block (→ null), two blocks (→ the last).
- A valid `BM-REPORT` longer than 20 000 characters BEFORE the block → the block is read in full.
- 200 KB of `Q1:` / `- a:` lines → at most 10 questions × 8 options, in under 100 ms.
- 200 KB of prose then a block at the end → the block is read, in under 100 ms.
- `answersText` gives exactly the block above for option and `other` picks, turns newlines in `other` into spaces, and throws on a missing pick. Negative control: removing the throw makes the "missing pick" case fail.
- `parseReports(report + "\n" + questionsBlock)` deep-equals `parseReports(report)` (also with both inside one fence), with empty `unparsedFields`.

## Validation / Definition of Done
`npx vitest run test/plugin-bm-questions.test.ts test/plugin-bm-report.test.ts`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:plugin`, `npm run lint` all exit 0.

## Primary Proof
The two test files green, including the long-report case, the timing cases and the negative control.

## Reversibility
Delete `plugin/shared/bm-questions.ts` and `test/plugin-bm-questions.test.ts`, and remove the one added case from `test/plugin-bm-report.test.ts`. Nothing else uses them until WP-253.

## Provenance
Request: req-20260918T021211Z — "template cấu trúc mà Worker hỏi lại … Cách hiển thị cũng đưa vào Card và cho lựa chọn option"
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260918c-question-cards.md#WP-250
Requirements: REQ-059 (a), (e), (h)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260918c-question-cards.md §4.1–§4.3, F2, F8, §6
close_reason: Added plugin/shared/bm-questions.ts (parseQuestions, answersText, MAX_* bounds) and test/plugin-bm-questions.test.ts; one invariance case in test/plugin-bm-report.test.ts. npx vitest run test/plugin-bm-questions.test.ts test/plugin-bm-report.test.ts -> 2 files, 79 tests passed (25 new: example shape, fence/quote/bold/(a)/a)/wrapped/intro variants, non-unique recommendation, duplicate id/key, prose a:, end at prose/marker, null, last of two blocks, <2 options, >20000-char report before block, 200 KB questions <100 ms capped 10x8, 200 KB prose then block <100 ms, 1000-char cut, answersText order/other/ignore/throws). parseReports(report+BM-QUESTIONS) deep-equals parseReports(report), also fenced. Negative control: replacing the missing-pick throw with continue -> 'refuses to write a partial answer' failed (1 failed/24 passed), restored -> 25 passed. npm run typecheck 0, typecheck:plugin 0, npm run lint 0. bm-report.ts untouched. R1.

title: Teach the Worker to ask through a BM-QUESTIONS block and to read BM-ANSWERS
description:
## Objective
Rewrite the "How to ask" part of `plugin/roles/worker.md` so a Worker asks through a `BM-QUESTIONS` block (ids counted across the whole request, every question in the block, `blockers:` only pointing at it) and reads `BM-ANSWERS`; regenerate `plugin/server/worker-instructions.ts`; replace the affected rules in `test/roles-content.test.ts` with rules at least as strict.

## Context
Today every question sits on one long `blockers:` line (42 real reports: median 458 characters, max 2975), so neither the Manager nor the chat card can read them reliably. The owner chose a fixed block right after `BM-REPORT` (decision Q41), with answers coming back as `BM-ANSWERS`. Role instructions are injected when an agent is created, so this changes new Workers only.

## Scope
In: the paragraph starting `**How to ask: at most 5 numbered questions**`, its fenced example and the "What makes those answerable" paragraph in `## Asking`; the `blockers:` line of the `BM-REPORT` template in `## Reporting`; the Worker rules in `test/roles-content.test.ts` that cover them; the generated `plugin/server/worker-instructions.ts`.
Out: the rest of `worker.md` (the three fixed asking moments, the triggers, RULES, Stop), the fields and order of `BM-REPORT`, `manager.md`, `reviewer.md`, the line ceiling in the test.

## Components Touched
- `plugin/roles/worker.md` — `## Asking` (How to ask + example), `## Reporting` (`blockers:` template line only).
- `plugin/server/worker-instructions.ts` — regenerated with `npm run generate:role-instructions` (never hand-edited).
- `test/roles-content.test.ts` — the Worker rules in "asks at fixed moments, in one numbered set, and waits".

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
none. The block format is fixed below; no code is needed.

## Assumptions / Constraints
The text must teach, in English:
- at most 5 questions per turn, each with its options, a recommendation, and what the Worker will do for each answer;
- ids `Q1`, `Q2`, … counted on across the whole request (the second round starts after the last id of the first), so a late answer can never land on a new question;
- write the questions in the chat (the user's language) AND send `blocked`: the `BM-REPORT` followed, in the same message, by a `BM-QUESTIONS` block with EVERY question; `blockers:` then only says e.g. `2 questions: Q1, Q2 — see BM-QUESTIONS` (plus `Suggestion (not done): …` as before);
- one line per question `Q<n>: <topic> — <question>`, one line per option `- <letter>: <option: what it costs, what you will do>`, letters from `a`, at least 2 options, exactly one `(recommended)`; question and option texts in the user's language, the keywords (`BM-QUESTIONS`, `requestId`, `Q<n>`, letters, `(recommended)`) unchanged;
- a `BM-ANSWERS` block is the user's answer: `Q<n>: <letter> — …` picks that option, `Q<n>: other — …` is the user's own words; an answer to an id that is not open (already answered, or from an earlier round) → say so, do not act on it; a question left without an answer stays open and is asked again at the next `blocked`, never defaulted;
- keep: `AskUserQuestion` returns nothing here, `blocked` is the only channel, an unanswered question is never a licence to pick a default, no "unless you say otherwise", "Silence is not an answer", "every option is named".

The example (replaces the numbered `1. … (a) …` example, which is 2 lines longer):
```
BM-QUESTIONS
requestId: req-20260917T010956Z
Q1: Storage — the request says "save the user list" but not where.
- a: the existing Postgres `users` table: no migration, ready today. (recommended)
- b: a new table: needs a migration, which makes this request Large.
- c: a file on disk: simplest, but two writers can lose data.
Q2: Existing sessions — renaming the session cookie signs everyone out.
- a: keep the old name: nobody is signed out. (recommended)
- b: rename it: everyone signs in again, once.
```
`BM-REPORT` template: `blockers: <questions waiting for the user>` becomes `blockers: <what waits for the user; questions go in BM-QUESTIONS>`. The test's verbatim check needs only `blockers:` after `skillsUsed:`.
Constraints: `worker.md` stays under 394 lines (it is 383) and the ceiling is NOT raised; the RULES block stays ≤ 34 lines with exactly 5 limits (untouched here). Leave the existing uncommitted `BM-STOP` line in `## Stop` alone. Everything for agents is English (AGENTS.md).

## Risks / Gotchas
- The test anchors `between(worker, "1. Storage — the request says", "```")` and `/My recommendation: \(a\)/`, `/I am waiting for your answers before I start/` break by design; replace each with an equivalent anchor on the new example (e.g. `between(worker, "Q1: Storage — the request says", "```")` and `/\(recommended\)/`). Do not simply delete them.
- `/EVERY question in \`blockers\`/` becomes a rule that EVERY question goes into `BM-QUESTIONS`.

title: Teach the Manager to group waiting questions per Worker and relay answers as BM-ANSWERS
description:
## Objective
Make `plugin/roles/manager.md` show waiting questions grouped per Worker (letters A, B, … and labels like A6) and relay the user's answers to each Worker as `Continue <requestId>.` plus a `BM-ANSWERS` block holding only that Worker's answers; regenerate `plugin/server/manager-instructions.ts`; cover it in `test/roles-content.test.ts`.

## Context
With several Workers blocked at once, the Manager today repeats one long `blockers:` line per Worker and must guess which of the user's "1a 2b" belongs to which Worker, while rule 2 allows only the user's words verbatim. The owner chose grouping by Worker with letter labels and a fixed answer block, and asking back when an answer fits no single question (decision Q43). Role instructions are injected when an agent is created, so this changes new Managers only.

## Scope
In: rule 2 of `## RULES`; the `blocked` bullet of `## Talking to the user`; the Manager rules in `test/roles-content.test.ts`; possibly the `manager.md` line ceiling in that test (rule below); the generated `plugin/server/manager-instructions.ts`.
Out: any other Manager behaviour, `worker.md`, `reviewer.md`, the card, the RULES line ceiling.

## Components Touched
- `plugin/roles/manager.md` — rule 2; the `**\`blocked\`:**` bullet.
- `plugin/server/manager-instructions.ts` — regenerated with `npm run generate:role-instructions`.
- `test/roles-content.test.ts` — "M2 — relay, not decider…", "reports each Worker phase the way the user needs it", and the file-length `it.each` if the ceiling rule applies.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
none (the block formats are fixed below). Do not work on this at the same time as the Worker-instructions bead: both edit `test/roles-content.test.ts` and regenerate the instruction files.

## Assumptions / Constraints
Worker reports now carry, after `BM-REPORT`, a block like:
```
BM-QUESTIONS
requestId: req-A
Q6: Storage — where?
- a: postgres: no migration. (recommended)
- b: a file: simplest.
```
Workers created before the update still put everything on the `blockers:` line with their own numbering.
The `blocked` bullet must teach:
1. show EVERY question — from `BM-QUESTIONS`, or from `blockers` when the report has no block — each with its options and the Worker's recommendation; the list is shown in full;
2. group by Worker: list EVERY Worker still waiting, give each a letter (A, B, …) in that list with its name and `requestId`, label its questions letter + number (A6 = Worker A's Q6; for an old-style report, the Worker's own number);
3. tell the user they can answer in the Worker's card or here as `A6 a, B1 b`;
4. read the answer against the LATEST list shown; send each Worker only its own answers, and only when it is not `running` (step 2's rule stays): `Continue <requestId>.`, then
```
BM-ANSWERS
requestId: <requestId>
Q6: a — <the option as the Worker wrote it>
Q7: other — <the user's own words>
```
5. an answer that fits no single open question of exactly one Worker → ask the user, send nothing for it; never pick an option for the user;
6. a Worker that reported again after `blocked` has had its answers (maybe in its card): relay nothing more for those questions; "If the user tells you they already answered the Worker, do not relay it again" stays.
Rule 2 gains only a short pointer (answers to a Worker's questions go as the `BM-ANSWERS` block of `blocked`) and must keep the words the M2 test checks: `verbatim`, `` `Continue <requestId>.` ``, "relay, not a decider", "Add no requirement", "first prompt is the exception"/"FIRST prompt … recipe", "user stated a size".
Hard budgets:
- the `## RULES` block is at its ceiling of 29 lines with exactly 5 limits: it must stay ≤ 29 lines and 5 limits; re-wrap (rule 3 has a short line) instead of adding lines; that ceiling is NOT raised;
- `manager.md` is 157 lines, ceiling < 160: write compactly first; only if the compact text still exceeds 159 lines, set the ceiling to (measured line count + 3) and add a comment in the test, like the one for delta 20260917f, naming delta 20260918c-question-cards, the measured count and why nothing more could be cut. `worker.md` and `reviewer.md` ceilings are unchanged. The owner confirms this before implementation starts.
Keep the uncommitted step-2 text (`BM-NEW-REQUEST`, never send to a `running` Worker) unchanged. English only.

## Risks / Gotchas
- `/show EVERY question in \`blockers\`/` breaks by design: replace it with a rule at least as strict (every question, from `BM-QUESTIONS` or from `blockers` when there is none). Keep `/with its options and the Worker's recommendation/` and `/which you show in full/` passing.
- A RULES block over 29 lines fails "the RULES budget" test — that is a real limit, not something to raise.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `manager.md` teaches points 1–6 above and the rule-2 pointer.
- New test rules: grouped by Worker with a letter; label letter + number; the `A6 a, B1 b` form; each Worker gets only its own answers; the `BM-ANSWERS` block; ask back when an answer fits no single question; never pick an option for the user; questions come from `blockers` when there is no block.
- Old Manager rules still pass or are replaced by rules at least as strict; M2 rules pass unchanged.
- RULES block ≤ 29 lines with 5 limits; `manager.md` under its ceiling per the rule above.
- `plugin/server/manager-instructions.ts` equals the regenerated output.

## Validation / Definition of Done
`npm run generate:role-instructions`, then `npx vitest run test/roles-content.test.ts` `test/plugin-bundle-cjs.test.ts` (generated file equals the markdown byte for byte) and `test/plugin-role-labels.test.ts` exit 0; `wc -l plugin/roles/manager.md`.

## Primary Proof
`npx vitest run test/roles-content.test.ts` green, including "the RULES budget" and the file-length check, and `git diff plugin/roles/manager.md` limited to rule 2 and the `blocked` bullet.

## Reversibility
Revert the two paragraphs and the test changes, then `npm run generate:role-instructions`. Managers created meanwhile keep the new instructions until the user opens a new one.

Pre-existing step-2 text untouched. manager.md 171 lines after compaction -> ceiling 160 -> 174 (measured + 3, owner Q46 a) with a comment in the test naming this delta. test/roles-content.test.ts: 'show EVERY question in blockers' replaced by the BM-QUESTIONS/blockers rule; 11 new Manager rules + 1 RULES rule; options/recommendation, already-answered, show in full, M2 rules unchanged. npm run generate:role-instructions; npx vitest run (full) -> 95 files, 2136 tests passed incl. roles-content, plugin-bundle-cjs (generated == markdown), the RULES budget. title: Show a blocked report's questions as an option card in the Manager chat that answers the asking Worker
description:
## Objective
In the Manager's chat, a Worker report that carries a `BM-QUESTIONS` block renders as a card showing every question with selectable options (recommended one marked, none pre-selected), `Use recommendations`, `Other…`, `Clear`, and `Send answers to <Worker>`, which re-reads the Worker's status and sends one `BM-ANSWERS` message straight to the single Worker of that request.

## Context
Chat cards (delta 20260916-chat-cards) already turn a Worker's `BM-REPORT` in the Manager chat into a card with a free-text "Reply to Worker". With several Workers asking at once the owner wants option buttons and a guarantee that an answer reaches the right Worker and question (decisions Q40, Q42, Q44). The card finds the Worker the way it already does (`partiesOf`: exactly one Worker with the report's `requestId`) and sends through `paseo.agents.ref(id).send()`, which records a real user message.

## Scope
In: `plugin/client/chat-cards.ts` and `plugin/client/chat-card.tsx`; `test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts`.
Out: `plugin/shared/contracts.ts`, `plugin/server/chat-rpc.ts`, `chat.peers`, the transformer registration in `plugin/index.client.tsx` (unchanged), cards in Worker/Reviewer chats, parsing old one-line `blockers`, notifying the Manager, keeping "sent" across an app reload.

## Components Touched
- `plugin/client/chat-cards.ts` —
  - `chatCardSchema` gains `questions: z.array(questionSchema).default([])`; `kind`/`version` stay `bm-message`/1;
  - `toChatCard` fills `questions` from `parseQuestions` when the card is a `report` and the block's `requestId` is null or equals the report's (a block for another request is ignored);
  - `summaryOf` → `<tier> · <n> questions waiting` when there are questions;
  - `quickReplies` → none when there are questions;
  - `markdownOf` treats `BM-QUESTIONS` / `BM-ANSWERS` as blocks, with option lines nested under their question;
  - new pure functions `showsQuestions`, `recommendedPicks`, `formComplete`, `answerTarget`, `answeredKey`, `sendAnswers`.
- `plugin/client/chat-card.tsx` — the question section, the buttons, a module-level `Map<answeredKey, { at, summary, to }>`.
- `test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts` — new cases.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
The bead for WP-250 (`plugin/shared/bm-questions.ts`: `parseQuestions`, `answersText`, `Question`, `Pick`) must be closed first; this bead imports them.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- `showsQuestions(card, owner)`: true only when `card.type === "report"`, `card.direction === "received"`, `owner.role === "manager"`, and `card.questions.length > 0`. Every other card renders exactly as today.
- `recommendedPicks(questions, picks)` fills the recommended option into questions without a pick and never overwrites one.
- `formComplete(questions, picks)`: every question has a pick whose key exists, or `{ other }` non-blank after trim.
- `answerTarget(card, owner, peers)` → `{ worker: ChatPeer }` or `{ reason }`. The Worker is `partiesOf(card, owner, peers).from`, with its status from the matching `peers` entry. Reasons:
  - no id → "Cannot tell which Worker asked this: no single Worker has `<requestId>`.";
  - `running` / `initializing` → "<Worker> is working; a message now would replace its turn. Send when it stops.";
  - `closed` → "<Worker> is closed.".

  `idle` and `error` may send.
- `sendAnswers({ card, picks, refreshPeers, send })` is the WHOLE send path, where `refreshPeers(): Promise<{ owner: ChatPeer | null; peers: ChatPeer[] }>` and `send(agentId, text): Promise<void>`. It returns `{ ok: true, to, text }` or `{ ok: false, reason }`:
  - not `formComplete` → `{ ok: false }` without calling anything;
  - otherwise it awaits `refreshPeers()` for fresh status, then applies `answerTarget`;
  - then calls `send(worker.id, answersText(card.requestId, card.questions, picks))` AT MOST once (a null `card.requestId` never gets here: `answerTarget` finds no Worker for it);
  - a thrown error becomes `{ ok: false, reason: errorMessageOf(error) }`.

  The `.tsx` passes `() => peers.refetch()` (mapped to `{ owner, peers }`) and `(id, text) => paseo.agents.ref(id).send(text)`. The repo has no React component tests, so no send logic may live in the `.tsx`.
- Never send to an id read from the message text.
- `answeredKey(agentId, card)` = chat agent id + `requestId` + question ids + a short djb2 hash of `card.text`.
- After a successful send the card shows `Answered at HH:MM → <Worker>: Q1 a, Q2 other` instead of the form, for the rest of the app session. On failure it shows the reason and keeps the picks.
- Layout: each question shows its id and text, the topic (text before the first ` — `) in bold, then its options stacked vertically, each a `Pressable` with `accessibilityRole="button"` and `accessibilityState.selected`, drawn `○ a — …` / `● a — …`. The recommended option carries a `recommended` chip (tone `success`). Last comes `Other…`, which opens a `TextInput` for that question. A line `Answers go to <partyName(worker)> · <requestId>` is shown. The free-text "Reply to Worker" stays.
- Client rules: React Native primitives only, colours from the theme, no `useNativeDriver: true`; a file under `test/` must not import `react-native` as a value (AGENTS.md).

## Risks / Gotchas
- A report text that also contains a `BM-QUESTIONS` block for ANOTHER request must not attach those questions.
- Status in the cached `chat.peers` answer can be 30 s old: that is why `sendAnswers` refreshes first.
- Keep every existing chat-card test expectation for old-style reports unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A blocked report with the block → `questions` filled (ids, options, recommended); a block with another `requestId` → `[]`; an old-style report → `[]`, with summary and quick replies as today.
- `showsQuestions`: true for received + Manager owner; false for Worker, Reviewer, non-paseo-bm owner, and sent cards.
- `answerTarget`:
  - 0 or 2 matching Workers → reason;
  - `running`, `initializing`, `closed` → reason;
  - `idle`, `error` → Worker.
- `recommendedPicks` never overwrites; `formComplete` is false for a missing pick or blank `other`.
- "Use recommendations" + send (2 actions) completes a form whose questions all have a recommendation.
- `sendAnswers` with fake `refreshPeers`/`send`:
  - `send` is called exactly once, with the Worker id from the refresh and text equal to `answersText(...)`;
  - Worker `running` at refresh → no `send`;
  - `send` throws → `{ ok: false }` with its message;
  - incomplete form → neither `refreshPeers` nor `send` is called.
- Negative control: skipping the refresh makes the "`running` at refresh" case fail.
- `markdownOf` renders a `BM-QUESTIONS` block with bold ids and nested options.

## Validation / Definition of Done
`npx vitest run test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts`, `npm run typecheck:plugin`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` exit 0.

## Primary Proof
`test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts` green with the new cases, including the `sendAnswers` cases and the negative control, and all pre-existing cases unchanged.

## Reversibility
Revert `chat-cards.ts`, `chat-card.tsx` and the test additions; the card goes back to today's (the new block then shows as plain text in the expanded message). No stored data changes.

## Provenance
Request: req-20260918T021211Z — "Cách hiển thị cũng đưa vào Card và cho lựa chọn option … trả lời đúng cho Worker đang hỏi"
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260918c-question-cards.md#WP-253
Requirements: REQ-059 (b), (c), (d), (h)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260918c-question-cards.md §4.4, F3–F5, F7, §6
close_reason: chat-cards.ts: questionSchema + ChatCard.questions (default [], kind/version unchanged), toChatCard fills questions from parseQuestions only for reports whose block requestId is null or equal, summary '<n> questions waiting', quickReplies none with questions, markdownOf nests BM-QUESTIONS options; new pure showsQuestions, choosable, topicOf, recommendedPicks, formComplete, answerSummary, answerTarget, sendAnswers (refreshPeers then one send), answeredKey. chat-card.tsx: QuestionForm (vertical option buttons with selected state, recommended chip, Other… input, Use recommendations, Clear, 'Answers go to <Worker> · <req>', Send answers), module-level answered map, wired to peers.refetch and paseo.agents.ref(id).send. npx vitest run test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts -> 36 passed (15 new, 0 existing lines changed per git diff). Negative controls: refresh skipped -> 3 failed incl. 'does not send when the Worker started running'; running guard removed -> 2 failed; restored -> 36 passed. npm run typecheck 0, typecheck:plugin 0, npm run lint 0; bm-questions/bm-report/bundle-cjs suites 184 passed. contracts.ts and chat-rpc.ts untouched. R1 (client UI, no persisted data); visual check left to the owner's real-daemon run.

title: Keep a blocked report card's summary to two lines and cut its waiting-on text at 160 characters
description:
## Objective
The summary line of every `blocked` report card in a chat is at most 2 lines, also while the full message is open, and its `waiting on: …` part is cut at 160 characters, so a long `blockers:` text is no longer repeated on the summary line.

## Context
Follow-up batch b4 of req-20260918T021211Z. The owner sent a screenshot of an old-style blocked card whose summary line repeated the whole 1000-character `blockers:` paragraph above the same text in the opened message. Decisions (PRD delta §1.3): Q49 (c) old-style reports otherwise keep today's card; Q50 (a) this readability fix applies to every blocked report; Q51 (a) plus the owner's one-time permission to reload the plugin after this batch.

## Scope
In: `summaryOf` in `plugin/client/chat-cards.ts` (cut the `waiting on:` part at 160 characters with `…`); the summary `Text` in `plugin/client/chat-card.tsx` (always `numberOfLines={2}`); tests in `test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts`.
Out: option buttons or any parsing of old one-line `blockers` (Q49 c), quick replies, the expanded message, the question card, role files, documents beyond the delta rows already written.

## Components Touched
- plugin/client/chat-cards.ts — summaryOf
- plugin/client/chat-card.tsx — summary Text numberOfLines
- test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
none (the question card of bm-wp-250-question-cards-nv8m.4 is closed).

## Assumptions / Constraints
160 characters is the design value (design delta §4.4, batch b4). Short blockers render exactly as before (the existing expectation "Large · beads 2 created, 1 closed · waiting on: Q1 — keep the old label?" must stay unchanged). React Native primitives only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A report whose `blockers:` is 1000+ characters gives a summary whose `waiting on:` part is at most 160 characters and ends with `…`.
- A short `blockers:` gives the same summary as before (existing test unchanged).
- The summary `Text` in chat-card.tsx has `numberOfLines={2}` whether the message is open or not.
- `npx vitest run test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts`, `npm run typecheck:plugin`, `npm run lint` exit 0.

The chat-card test file, plugin typecheck and lint.

title: Make the Manager stop repeating what a report's card shows (manager.md Talking to the user)
description:
## Objective
Rewrite the "## Talking to the user" section of `plugin/roles/manager.md` so the Manager never repeats what a report's chat card already shows and says in one or two lines only what the card lacks; regenerate `plugin/server/manager-instructions.ts`; replace the affected Manager rules in `test/roles-content.test.ts` with rules at least as strict.

## Context
Every `BM-REPORT` a Worker sends reaches the Manager's chat as a card: phase, tier, beads, the full report one tap away, and a `BM-QUESTIONS` block as option buttons. manager.md still says "show the user EVERY question … with its options", and on 2026-09-18 a Manager printed a card's questions again, twice, right under the card. Owner decision Q1 (a): for every report, repeat nothing the card shows; old-style reports without a `BM-QUESTIONS` block (no buttons) still get their questions listed in full.

## Scope
In:
- the "## Talking to the user" section of manager.md;
- the generated manager-instructions.ts;
- the Manager rules of test/roles-content.test.ts.

Out:
- the `## RULES` block and every other section of manager.md;
- the `BM-BUDGET` bullet and the "ended a turn WITHOUT a new `BM-REPORT`" bullet (unchanged);
- worker.md, reviewer.md and their rules;
- the line ceilings (174 for manager.md, 29 for its RULES block).

## Components Touched
- `plugin/roles/manager.md` — section "## Talking to the user" only.
- `plugin/server/manager-instructions.ts` — regenerated by `npm run generate:role-instructions`, never hand-edited.
- `test/roles-content.test.ts` — the Manager blocks "reports each Worker phase the way the user needs it" and "keeps its replies short, …" (plus the rule `received is acknowledged in one line`, which must keep passing).

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
none.

## Assumptions / Constraints
Exact text changes (design §4.5):
- **Opening paragraph:** replace the sentence "Each carries the request id, the phase, the tier, files changed, beads, open review findings, build and test status, skills used and blockers." with "Each reaches the user as a card — phase, tier, beads, the full report one tap away, and a `BM-QUESTIONS` block as option buttons. Never repeat what the card shows; say in one or two lines only what it does not." The rest of the paragraph stays word for word.
- **`received`:** keep the literal `**\`received\`:** one line` (test-pinned) and "Nothing else is due until it asks or finishes"; the line carries only what the card does not say (for example a tier other than the Manager's guess).
- **`beads-done`:** drop "what documents and beads now exist"; keep "For a **Large** request say the Worker is waiting for the user's confirmation; never say it started implementing before the user answered." (the capital F is test-pinned).
- **`blocked`:** list every Worker still waiting under a letter (A, B, …), one line each `A · <name> · <requestId>: Q6, Q7` — the Worker's own question ids, the owner's Q1 wording — and say the user answers in the Worker's card or here as `A6 a, B1 b` (A6 = Worker A's Q6). The card shows a `BM-QUESTIONS` block's questions and options: never repeat them. A report without that block has no buttons: show its questions from `blockers` in full, with its options and the Worker's recommendation (old reports keep the Worker's numbers). Everything from "Read an answer against your latest list" to "do not relay it again", including the fenced `BM-ANSWERS` example, stays word for word.
- **`finished`:** drop "in a few lines, what changed, the beads, and the check result"; say how many `Suggestion (not done)` items the card lists and ask which, if any, becomes new work — the user decides. The missing-skill sentence, "Do not cancel the Worker for it" and "Leave the Worker idle" stay word for word.
- **"How you talk":** "except the question list of a `blocked` report, which you show in full" → "except the questions of a `blocked` report without a `BM-QUESTIONS` block, which you show in full".
- **Line ceiling:** manager.md must stay under 174 by the test's own count (`text.split("\n").length`; 172 today). A scratch draft of exactly these changes measured 173. Do NOT raise the ceiling and do not drop a safeguard to fit: if it does not fit, stop and send `blocked` to ask the owner.
- `## RULES` stays untouched (≤ 29 lines, exactly 5 limits).
- Another Worker (`req-20260918T035101Z`) may edit worker.md and the Worker rules of the same test file: touch only the Manager rules; run `git status` before starting and stop and ask if the same lines changed.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Replaced test rules (design §4.5 table), each at least as strict as the one it replaces:
  - "every blocked question reaches the user" → two rules: `never repeat them` in the same sentence as `BM-QUESTIONS`; and a report without a `BM-QUESTIONS` block shows its questions from `blockers` in full;
  - "every waiting Worker gets a letter, with its name and request" → `every Worker still waiting under a letter (A, B, …)` plus the verbatim sample line `A · <name> · <requestId>: Q6, Q7`;
  - "suggestions become questions for the user" → `how many \`Suggestion (not done)\` items` together with the user deciding which becomes new work;
  - "a blocked question list is shown in full" → same regex `which you show in full`, renamed "an old-style blocked list is shown in full";
  - new rule: `Never repeat what the card shows`.
- Every other Manager rule keeps its expectation unchanged, including `received is acknowledged in one line`, `A6 = Worker A's Q6`, `answers in the Worker's card or here as \`A6 a, B1 b\``, the verbatim `BM-ANSWERS` block, and `with its options and the Worker's recommendation`.
- manager.md under 174 lines; the RULES budget test is green.
- manager-instructions.ts equals the markdown (`test/plugin-bundle-cjs.test.ts`).

## Validation / Definition of Done
`npm run generate:role-instructions`; `npx vitest run test/roles-content.test.ts test/plugin-bundle-cjs.test.ts` exit 0; `npm run typecheck` exit 0.

## Primary Proof
`npx vitest run test/roles-content.test.ts test/plugin-bundle-cjs.test.ts` green with the replaced Manager rules, plus a watched negative control: putting back the old "show the user EVERY question — from the report's `BM-QUESTIONS` block, else from `blockers` — with its options" sentence in place of the new one makes the "never repeat" rule fail.

## Reversibility
Revert manager.md and the Manager part of the test, then `npm run build` regenerates manager-instructions.ts. Only Managers created afterwards get the old text; no persisted data changes.

## Provenance

Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260918d-card-replies.md#WP-255
Requirements: REQ-059 (f) as amended by docs/product/paseo-bm-prd-delta-20260918d-card-replies.md §5; owner decision Q1 (a)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260918d-card-replies.md §4.5, F3, F4

title: Send every chat card Reply through one status-checked path
description:
## Objective
Make the Reply box's Send on every chat card go through one pure send path, `sendReply`, that re-reads the recipient's status just before sending and sends exactly once, refusing — with a reason shown on the card — when the recipient is running, starting, closed or cannot be identified.

## Context
Today the Reply box calls `paseo.agents.ref(counterpart.id).send(replyText(card, answer))` with the id from a cached `chat.peers` answer (up to 30 s old) and never looks at the recipient's status, so a reply can replace a running turn and throw that work away (design delta 20260918d F2). Only the question card's own "Send answers" button re-reads the status today. Owner decision Q4 (a): Send finds the right recipient and never sends while it is running — "áp cho mọi Reply" (for every Reply). The next bead (`bm-wp-255-card-replies-jt7e.5`) then makes this Reply box the only way to answer questions.

## Scope
In:
- new pure `replyTarget` and `sendReply` in `plugin/client/chat-cards.ts`;
- the Reply box's Send in `plugin/client/chat-card.tsx`;
- their cases in `test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts`.

Out:
- the question section (`QuestionForm`), its "Send answers to <Worker>" button and `formComplete` / `answerTarget` / `sendAnswers`: all stay exactly as they are in this bead (`bm-wp-255-card-replies-jt7e.5` replaces them);
- `replyText`, quick replies, `partiesOf`, `chat.peers`, `plugin/shared/*`, `plugin/server/*`;
- layout.

## Components Touched
`plugin/client/chat-cards.ts`:
- new `replyTarget(card, owner, peers)` → `{ peer: ChatPeer } | { reason: string }`:
  - counterpart = `partiesOf(card, owner, peers).from` for a `received` card, `.to` for a `sent` card; the peer is the `peers` entry with that id;
  - none found → for a `received` report card exactly "Cannot tell which Worker asked this: no single Worker has \`<requestId ?? "this request">\`." (today's `answerTarget` text), otherwise "Cannot tell which <Role> to send this to." (Role from `roleName`);
  - `peer.id === owner?.id` → "This is your own message.";
  - status `running` / `initializing` → "<name> is working; a message now would replace its turn. Send when it stops.";
  - `idle` / `error` → `{ peer }`; any other status → "<name> is <status>.";
  - `<name>` = `partyName({ role: counterpart.role, id: peer.id, title: peer.title })`.
- new `sendReply({ card, text, refreshPeers, send })` → `{ ok: true, to: ChatPeer, text: string } | { ok: false, reason: string }`, with `refreshPeers(): Promise<{ owner: ChatPeer | null; peers: ChatPeer[] }>` and `send(agentId, text): Promise<void>`:
  1. blank `text` → `{ ok: false, reason: "Write a reply first." }`, calling nothing;
  2. `await refreshPeers()`, then `replyTarget` on the fresh data; a reason → `{ ok: false, reason }`;
  3. `send(peer.id, replyText(card, text))` exactly once; the returned `text` is what was sent;
  4. any throw → `{ ok: false, reason: errorMessageOf(failure) }`.

`plugin/client/chat-card.tsx` (`ChatCardView`, the Reply box):
- Send enabled when not sending and `answer.trim() !== ""`;
- calls `sendReply` with `refreshPeers` = `peers.refetch({ throwOnError: true })` mapped to `{ owner: data?.owner ?? null, peers: data?.peers ?? [] }` (the mapping `QuestionForm` already uses) and `send` = `(id, text) => paseo.agents.ref(id).send(text)`;
- success: "Sent to <partyName(to)>.", clear and close the box (as today); failure: show the reason, keep the box text.

`test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts` — new `replyTarget` and `sendReply` cases.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
none.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- The recipient comes only from `chat.peers` via `partiesOf`; never from an id in the message text.
- No send logic in the `.tsx` (the repo has no React component tests). React Native primitives only; a file under `test/` must not import `react-native` as a value (AGENTS.md).
- A running recipient never disables the box: the user may write while it runs; Send refuses at send time.
- Another Worker (`req-20260918T035101Z`) works in the same repository: run `git status` before starting and stop and ask if these files changed under you.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `replyTarget`:
  - report card in the Manager's chat → the one Worker of the request;
  - 0 or 2 Workers with the request → exactly today's "Cannot tell which Worker asked this: no single Worker has \`req-…\`." text;
  - Worker `running` / `initializing` → "Worker · <title> is working; a message now would replace its turn. Send when it stops."; `closed` → "Worker · <title> is closed."; `idle` / `error` → the peer;
  - a review card in a Worker's chat with its Reviewer `running` → refused; a message card in a Worker's chat with the Manager `running` → refused.
- `sendReply`: `send` called exactly once with the id from the refresh and text `replyText(card, text)`; recipient `running` at refresh → no `send`; `send` throws or `refreshPeers` throws → `{ ok: false }` with the error message; blank text → neither `refreshPeers` nor `send` called.
- Negative control, watched failing then restored: `sendReply` using the cached peers instead of `refreshPeers()` → the "running at refresh" case fails.
- Every existing test in `test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts` passes unchanged (including the `answerTarget` / `sendAnswers` / `formComplete` cases, which still exist in this bead).

## Validation / Definition of Done
`npx vitest run test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:plugin`, `npm run lint` exit 0.

## Primary Proof
`test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts` green with the new `replyTarget` / `sendReply` cases and the watched negative control, plus `npm run typecheck:plugin` green for the Reply box wiring.

## Reversibility
Revert the two functions, the Reply box wiring and their tests: the Reply box sends as before. No persisted data.

## Provenance
Request: req-20260918T041426Z — Q4 (a): "Send tìm đúng Worker của request và không gửi khi Worker đang chạy — áp cho mọi Reply"
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260918d-card-replies.md#WP-256
Requirements: REQ-059 (d) as amended by docs/product/paseo-bm-prd-delta-20260918d-card-replies.md §5; owner decision Q4 (a)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260918d-card-replies.md §4.2, §4.3, F2, F5
Split into: this bead (the status-checked send path) and bm-wp-255-card-replies-jt7e.5 (picks in the Reply box), during polishing — two independently reviewable outcomes of WP-256.

Send when it stops.'; idle/error -> peer; other -> '<name> is <status>.') and sendReply({card,text,refreshPeers,send}) (blank -> 'Write a reply first.' calling nothing; refreshPeers then replyTarget on fresh data; send(peer.id, replyText(card,text)) exactly once; throws -> errorMessageOf). chat-card.tsx: the Reply box Send now calls sendReply with peers.refetch({throwOnError:true}) and paseo.agents.ref(id).send; success 'Sent to <name>.', failure shows the reason and keeps the text; QuestionForm/Send answers/formComplete/answerTarget/sendAnswers untouched (next bead). test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts: 8 new cases (report Worker; 0/2 Workers with today's text; running/initializing/closed; review card with Reviewer running and message card with Manager running refused, unknown Manager; one send with refreshed id and replyText; running at refresh -> no send; send/refresh failures; blank box touches nothing); 0 existing lines removed (git diff). npx vitest run test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts -> 45 passed. Negative controls: refresh skipped -> 3 failed incl. 'does not send when the recipient started running'; running guard removed -> 3 failed; restored (cmp identical) -> 45 passed. npm run typecheck 0, typecheck:plugin 0, lint 0. R1 client UI, no persisted data.

title: Lay out the card's questions as readable blocks with full-width option rows
description:
## Objective
Redraw the question section of the chat card per owner decision Q5 (a): each question is a block with a bold heading `Q<n> · <topic>` and the question text in normal (not monospace) type below it; each option is a full-width row, 8px apart, with a radio mark, a bold key, the option text wrapping aligned with its first line, and a `recommended` chip at the end of the row; "Other…" is the last row of the same list; a divider separates questions.

## Context
The owner found the card hard to read and to choose from ("nhìn hơi ríu rít lại khá khó đọc và lựa chọn"). Today the question text uses `styles.mono` and each option is a small bordered box whose whole content is one Text `○ a — …`.

## Scope
In:
- new pure `questionHeading` in `plugin/client/chat-cards.ts`;
- the drawing part of `QuestionForm` in `plugin/client/chat-card.tsx`;
- its test cases.

Out:
- pick and send logic (`bm-wp-255-card-replies-jt7e.2`, `bm-wp-255-card-replies-jt7e.5`; unchanged here);
- the card header, summary line, bead chips, other card types.

## Components Touched
- `plugin/client/chat-cards.ts` — `questionHeading(question): { heading: string; body: string }`, built on `topicOf` (which stays): with a topic → `{ heading: "<id> · <topic>", body: <rest> }`; without → `{ heading: <id>, body: <text> }`.
- `plugin/client/chat-card.tsx` — `QuestionForm` rendering:
  - question block: `View`, `gap: 6`, `paddingVertical: 8`; from the second question on `borderTopWidth: 1` with `theme.colors.border` as the divider;
  - heading: `Text` with `styles.body` and `fontWeight: "600"`;
  - body: `Text` with `styles.body` (NOT `styles.mono`);
  - option list: `View`, `gap: 8`;
  - option row: `Pressable`, `alignSelf: "stretch"`, `flexDirection: "row"`, `alignItems: "flex-start"`, `gap: 8`, `paddingVertical: 8`, `paddingHorizontal: 10`, `borderRadius: 8`, `borderWidth: 1`; selected → `borderColor: toneColor(theme, "info")`, `backgroundColor: theme.colors.surface2`; otherwise `theme.colors.border` and transparent; `accessibilityRole="button"`, `accessibilityState={{ selected, disabled }}`;
  - inside the row: `Text` "○"/"●" (width 14), `Text` key with `fontWeight: "600"` (width 16), `Text` option text with `flex: 1` (wraps aligned), then `Chip { text: "recommended", tone: "success" }` last when recommended;
  - "Other…": the last row of the same list, same row style, mark + "Other…" (no key); when selected its `TextInput` opens right under the row;
  - below all questions: "Use recommendations", "Clear", then the "Answers go to …" line (as left by `bm-wp-255-card-replies-jt7e.5`).
  - A question with fewer than 2 options shows only the "Other…" row.
- `test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts` — `questionHeading` cases.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
`bm-wp-255-card-replies-jt7e.5` (WP-256, "Write the question card's picks into the Reply box …") must be closed first: it turns `QuestionForm` into a draw-only component that receives `picks` and `onChange` from `ChatCardView`; this bead redraws exactly those rows.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- React Native primitives only (`View`, `Text`, `Pressable`, `TextInput`), theme colours, the existing `dashboardStyles`, the existing `Chip`; no new dependency. A file under `test/` must not import `react-native` as a value.
- The layout can only be judged by eye on the owner's daemon; the Worker does not install or reload the plugin there without the owner's explicit permission.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `questionHeading`: id Q6, text "Storage — where does the list live?" → `{ heading: "Q6 · Storage", body: "where does the list live?" }`; id Q1, text "No topic here" → `{ heading: "Q1", body: "No topic here" }`.
- `QuestionForm` no longer uses `styles.mono` for the question text.
- Every option row and the "Other…" row is a `Pressable` with `accessibilityRole="button"` and `accessibilityState.selected`.
- The `recommended` chip is inside the row, after the option text.
- A divider (`borderTopWidth`) separates consecutive questions.

## Validation / Definition of Done
`npx vitest run test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts`, `npm run typecheck:plugin`, `npm run lint` exit 0; read `QuestionForm` back against the list above.

## Primary Proof
`questionHeading` cases green, `npm run typecheck:plugin` green, and the `QuestionForm` diff read back against the layout list.

## Reversibility
Revert the drawing part of chat-card.tsx and `questionHeading` with its test; picks and Send are unaffected.

## Provenance
