title: Write the question card's picks into the Reply box and remove the Send answers button
description:
## Objective
Make the question card write its picks into the Reply box: every pick (tapping an option, "Use recommendations", "Clear", typing in "Other") rewrites a `BM-ANSWERS` block at the very top of the Reply box and opens it, keeping the user's own words; remove the "Send answers to <Worker>" button and `formComplete` / `answerTarget` / `sendAnswers`, so the Reply box's Send (`sendReply`, from `bm-wp-255-card-replies-jt7e.2`) is the only way to answer.

## Context
The owner ticked options in a question card, typed "OK" in "Reply to Worker" and pressed Send; the Worker received only "OK", because the card had two unconnected send paths — `QuestionForm`'s "Send answers" button (sends `answersText`) and the Reply box (sends only the typed text). Owner decision Q4 (a): ticks write into the Reply box, one Send, unanswered questions stay open and the Worker asks them again.

## Scope
In:
- pure functions in `plugin/client/chat-cards.ts`;
- wiring in `plugin/client/chat-card.tsx`;
- `test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts`.

Out:
- `replyTarget` / `sendReply` themselves (done in `bm-wp-255-card-replies-jt7e.2`; only reused here);
- the visual layout of the questions — headings, full-width rows, dividers (`bm-wp-255-card-replies-jt7e.3`);
- `plugin/shared/bm-questions.ts`, `contracts.ts`, `chat-rpc.ts`, `chat.peers`; manager.md, worker.md;
- keeping "answered" across an app reload.

## Components Touched
`plugin/client/chat-cards.ts`:
- new `isAnswered(question, pick)`: true for `{ key }` naming an existing option of a question with ≥ 2 options, or `{ other }` non-blank after trim.
- new `answersDraft(card, picks)`: `answersText(card.requestId, answered, picks)` where `answered` is the questions for which `isAnswered` holds, in question order; `""` when none is answered or `card.requestId` is null. (`answersText` throws only for a question in the list it is given that has no pick, so pass only answered ones; `bm-questions.ts` is not changed.)
- new `withAnswersBlock(text, block)`:
  1. the region is the first line whose trim is exactly `BM-ANSWERS`, plus every directly following line matching `^\s*(requestId|Q\d+)\s*:`;
  2. `rest` = the lines of `text` minus the region and minus the blank lines directly after it, then leading and trailing blank lines dropped (text above and below the region both kept, in order);
  3. result: block and rest → `block + "\n\n" + rest`; block only → `block`; rest only → `rest`; neither → `""`. The block is ALWAYS at the start.
- `answerSummary(questions, picks)`: answered questions only (`Q6 a, Q7 other`), skipping a blank Other.
- new `sentSummary(card, picks, text)`: `answerSummary(...)` when `answersDraft(card, picks)` is non-empty and appears verbatim in `text`; otherwise `null`.
- remove `formComplete`, `answerTarget`, `sendAnswers`.

`plugin/client/chat-card.tsx`:
- `picks` state moves from `QuestionForm` up to `ChatCardView`, next to `answer`; `QuestionForm` receives `picks` and an `onChange(nextPicks)` callback and only draws (keep its current look; `bm-wp-255-card-replies-jt7e.3` restyles it).
- on every picks change: `setPicks(next)`; `setAnswer(withAnswersBlock(answer, answersDraft(card, next)))`; `setReplying(true)`.
- after a successful `sendReply`: if `sentSummary(card, picks, sentBoxText)` is not null, record `{ at, summary, to }` in the module-level "answered" map under `answeredKey(agentId, card)`, so the question section shows "Answered at HH:MM → <Worker>: <summary>".
- remove the "Send answers to <Worker>" button; keep "Use recommendations", "Clear" and the "Answers go to <Worker> · <requestId>" line under the questions.
- when `canReply` is false, the option buttons are disabled and a line shows `replyTarget(card, owner, cachedPeers)`'s reason. A running recipient is NOT a reason to disable.

`test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts`:
- new cases below;
- the `formComplete`, `answerTarget` and `sendAnswers` cases are replaced by cases at least as strict: `formComplete` cases → `isAnswered` / `answersDraft`; `answerTarget` cases → `replyTarget` (same inputs, same reason texts); `sendAnswers` cases → `sendReply` with a box built by `withAnswersBlock` (same inputs; exactly one `send`; `running` at refresh → no send; failures → reason). No case is deleted without its replacement.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
`bm-wp-255-card-replies-jt7e.2` must be closed first: the Reply box's Send must already go through `sendReply` (status re-read), otherwise removing "Send answers" would lose the running-Worker check the question card has today.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Owner decision Q4 (a): Send works with some questions unanswered; they get no line and stay open, and the Worker asks them again. The block always mirrors the picks; manual edits inside it are overwritten on the next pick; words outside it are kept, and words typed above the block move below it.
- The message sent is `replyText(card, box)`: "Reply from the user about \`<requestId>\`:", a blank line, then the box, block first. The `BM-ANSWERS` format is unchanged, so old and new Workers read it.
- No pick logic in the `.tsx`; React Native primitives only; a file under `test/` must not import `react-native` as a value.
- Another Worker (`req-20260918T035101Z`) works in the same repository: run `git status` before starting and stop and ask if these files changed under you.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `isAnswered`: existing key → true; key `z` → false; Other `"   "` → false; a one-option question picked by key → false, by non-blank Other → true.
- `answersDraft`: no picks → `""`; Q6 only → a block with just the Q6 line; `recommendedPicks(questions, {})` → a block with Q6 and Q7 (so "Use recommendations" + Send stays two actions); a card without `requestId` → `""`.
- `withAnswersBlock`: empty box → block; old block replaced, text below kept; text ABOVE the old block ends up below the new block (`"note\n\nBM-ANSWERS…"` → `"BM-ANSWERS…\n\nnote"`); text on both sides → both below the block, in order, no double blank line; empty block → region removed, no leading blank line; box with only text → block + blank line + text; empty block and no region → text unchanged; every case with a non-empty block asserts `result.startsWith(block)`.
- The owner's bug: box = `withAnswersBlock("OK", answersDraft(card, { Q6: { key: "a" } }))` → `sendReply` calls `send` once with `replyText(card, box)`, which contains "Q6: a — the existing table: no migration." and "OK".
- `sentSummary`: block in the sent text → "Q6 a, Q7 other"; block deleted from the text → null; no picks → null. `answerSummary` skips a blank Other.
- Negative controls, each watched failing then restored: `withAnswersBlock` returning only `block` → the "text below kept" case fails; `withAnswersBlock` replacing the region in place → the "text above" case fails.
- `formComplete`, `answerTarget`, `sendAnswers` no longer exist (grep), and "Send answers to" no longer appears in `chat-card.tsx`.
- Existing expectations of `toChatCard`, `summaryOf`, `quickReplies`, `markdownOf`, `showsQuestions`, `partiesOf`, `replyText`, `recommendedPicks`, `answeredKey`, `replyTarget`, `sendReply` unchanged.

## Validation / Definition of Done
`npx vitest run test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:plugin`, `npm run lint` exit 0.

## Primary Proof
`test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts` green with the new cases (the owner's-bug case and the two watched negative controls), the ported cases, and `npm run typecheck:plugin` green for the wiring.

## Reversibility
Revert chat-cards.ts, chat-card.tsx and the test file to their state after `bm-wp-255-card-replies-jt7e.2`: the "Send answers" button and its path come back. No persisted data.

## Provenance
Request: req-20260918T041426Z — "Nên bỏ cái Button "Send answer to Worker … khi tôi tick chọn thì hãy tự concat message vào ô nhập Reply to Worker thì phù hợp hơn" (bug: "đã chọn trong Action Card rồi, nhưng lúc gửi message sang cho Worker không đẩy các option sang")
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260918d-card-replies.md#WP-256
Requirements: REQ-059 (c), (e) as amended by docs/product/paseo-bm-prd-delta-20260918d-card-replies.md §5; owner decision Q4 (a)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260918d-card-replies.md §4.1, §4.3, F1, F7
Split-from: bm-wp-255-card-replies-jt7e.2
close_reason: chat-cards.ts: new isAnswered (existing option of a >=2-option question, or non-blank Other), answersDraft (answersText over answered questions only; '' when none or no requestId), withAnswersBlock (region = first 'BM-ANSWERS' line + following requestId/Qn lines; rest = other lines minus blank lines after the region, trimmed; result block + blank line + rest, block always first), answerSummary now answered-only, sentSummary (summary only when the current draft is inside the sent text); formComplete, answerTarget, sendAnswers removed. chat-card.tsx: picks and the answered record live in ChatCardView; every pick (option, Other typing, Use recommendations, Clear) runs setAnswer(withAnswersBlock(current, answersDraft(card, next))) and opens the Reply box; the Reply Send (sendReply) records 'Answered at HH:MM → <Worker>: <summary>' when sentSummary is not null; QuestionForm is draw-only; 'Send answers to <Worker>' button removed; options, Use recommendations and Clear disabled with replyTarget's reason when canReply is false (a running recipient does not disable). test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts: formComplete cases -> isAnswered/answersDraft cases (same picks, incl. key z, blank Other, recommendations = 2 actions, lone question); answerTarget cases covered by the replyTarget cases of bead .2 (same inputs, same reason texts); sendAnswers cases -> sendReply on the box the picks wrote (one send with exact replyText, running -> no send, send/refresh failures, empty box touches nothing); new withAnswersBlock (7 cases, startsWith(block) on each non-empty block), sentSummary, answerSummary, owner's-bug case (box 'OK' + Q6 a -> one send containing 'Q6: a — the existing table: no migration.' and 'OK'). npx vitest run test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts -> 52 passed. Negative controls: withAnswersBlock returning only block -> 5 failed incl. 'replaces the old block and keeps the words below it' and the owner's-bug case; in-place replacement -> 3 failed incl. 'moves words typed above the old block below the new one'; restored (cmp identical) -> 52 passed. npm run typecheck 0, typecheck:plugin 0, lint 0; grep finds no formComplete/answerTarget/sendAnswers/'Send answers to' in plugin or test. R1 client UI, no persisted data.

title: Persist answer marks in the install home behind answers.marks and answers.mark
description:
## Objective
Persist "Mark as answered" marks in the paseo-bm install home and expose them through two RPCs: `answers.marks` (read) and `answers.mark` (add or remove one mark).

## Context
Owner decision Q16 (a): a mark must survive an app reload, stored "like the launcher order". plugin/server/launcher-order.ts already writes `<install home>/ui/launcher-order.json` safely (symlink guard, atomic write, never repairing on read, refusing to overwrite a newer file); this bead copies that pattern.

## Scope
In: new plugin/server/answer-marks.ts; `answersMarksRpc` / `answersMarkRpc` in plugin/shared/contracts.ts; handlers registered next to `launcher.order.*` in plugin/server/dashboard-rpc.ts; tests; the RPC name lists in test/plugin-bundle-cjs.test.ts and test/rpc-list-describe.test.ts.
Out: any client code (the button is a later bead), launcher-order.ts itself.

## Components Touched
- plugin/server/answer-marks.ts — `ANSWER_MARKS_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1`, `ANSWER_MARKS_FILE_NAME = "answer-marks.json"`, `ANSWER_MARKS_LIMIT = 500`, `answerMarksPath(location)` = `<dirname(tracesDir)>/ui/answer-marks.json` (reuse `UI_DIR_NAME` from launcher-order.ts); `readAnswerMarks(location)` → `{ keys: string[], notices: string[], tooNew: boolean }` (missing file → empty; bad JSON / wrong shape → empty + notice; newer schema → empty + notice + tooNew; invalid keys dropped with a notice; symlink on the path → throws via `assertNoSymlinkOnPath`); `writeAnswerMark(location, key, marked)` → `{ keys, notices, tooNew: false }`: validates the key (string, 1–400 chars, no control characters) else throws `DashboardError("E_TRACE_STORE_UNWRITABLE", …)`; refuses when the file is too new; adds (moved to newest, no duplicate) or removes; keeps the newest 500; `ensureStoreDir` + `writeStoreFileAtomically` like launcher-order. File body `{ schemaVersion: 1, marks: [{ key, at }] }` newest last.
- plugin/shared/contracts.ts — `answersMarksRpc` ("answers.marks", input `{}`) and `answersMarkRpc` ("answers.mark", input `{ key: string (1..400), marked: boolean }`), both output `{ keys: string[], notices: string[] }`.
- plugin/server/dashboard-rpc.ts — `handleAnswerMarksGet(paseo, deps)` / `handleAnswerMarkSet(input, paseo, deps)` via `requireLocation`, registered with `server.handle` beside `launcher.order.*`.
- test/plugin-answer-marks.test.ts — new; the two RPC name lists gain "answers.mark" and "answers.marks".

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
none.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Mirror launcher-order.ts exactly for safety rules; do not edit launcher-order.ts (only import `UI_DIR_NAME`).
- No network, no secrets; the file holds only card keys (agent id | request id | question ids | text hash).
- Run `git status` first; dashboard-rpc.ts and contracts.ts are not modified by the other Worker at planning time — stop and ask if they are.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Round trip: mark two keys → read returns both; unmark one → gone; marking again moves it to newest without duplicating.
- More than 500 marks → the oldest are dropped.
- Missing file → empty, no notice; bad JSON / wrong shape → empty with a notice and the file untouched; schemaVersion 2 → empty, tooNew, and a write throws; a symlinked ui dir → read and write throw; an empty or 401-char or control-character key → write throws.
- Handlers read and write through `requireLocation` (tested with a temp home as the chat.peers test does).
- Both RPCs registered; the RPC-name tests list them.
- vitest on the new and the two list tests, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:plugin`, `npm run lint` exit 0.

## Validation / Definition of Done
Tests, typecheck, typecheck:plugin and lint exit 0.

## Primary Proof
test/plugin-answer-marks.test.ts green, including a watched negative control: removing the too-new refusal makes the "refuses to overwrite a newer file" case fail.

## Reversibility
Delete answer-marks.ts, the two contracts, the registrations and the tests; an existing answer-marks.json is left for the user (the Worker never deletes it).

## Provenance

title: Sync every copy of a card and show a question card answered once its Worker stops waiting
description:
## Objective
Make every copy of a chat card show the same answered state at once, and make a question card in the Manager's chat show "answered" when `chat.waiting` no longer lists its report (the Worker is working, has reported since, or is gone).

## Context
Owner point 1 of batch b6: after answering from the pill's popover, the chat card still looked unanswered. Cause: `ChatCardView` reads the module maps `answered` / `replied` only in its `useState` initialisers, so the chat copy never hears about an answer sent from the popover copy. Owner decision Q17 (a): cards also re-derive the state from `chat.waiting` every 15 s, so it holds wherever the answer came from and after a reload.

## Scope
In: new plugin/client/answer-state.ts; pure `stillWaiting` / `answeredHow` in plugin/client/chat-cards.ts; plugin/client/chat-card.tsx wiring; tests.
Out: the "Mark as answered" button and the marks query (next bead, which fills `marked`); pills (Q18 b); the server.

## Components Touched

description:

title: Add the read-only chat.waiting RPC listing Workers that wait for the user's answer
description:
## Objective
Add the read-only RPC `chat.waiting` that returns, for every paseo-bm Manager, the Workers whose latest report to it is `blocked` with a `BM-QUESTIONS` block and that are idle, each with the report's text.

## Context
Batch b5 (owner decision Q15 b, design delta 20260918d §4.8) shows one composer pill per waiting Worker in the Manager's chat. The client needs a server answer to "who is waiting, with which report". The server already reads an agent's live timeline with `readTimelinePages` (plugin/server/live-timeline.ts) and lists paseo-bm agents with `bmAgentsOf` (plugin/server/dashboard-rpc.ts), as `chat.peers` does.

## Scope
In: `chatWaitingRpc` in plugin/shared/contracts.ts; new plugin/server/chat-waiting.ts with pure `waitingOf` and `handleChatWaiting`; registration in `registerChatRpcs` (plugin/server/chat-rpc.ts); tests; the RPC name lists in test/plugin-bundle-cjs.test.ts and test/rpc-list-describe.test.ts.
Out: the client pills and popover (the pills bead that depends on this one); any change to existing RPCs or to the trace store.

## Components Touched
- plugin/shared/contracts.ts — `chatWaitingRpc = defineRpc({ name: "chat.waiting", input: z.object({}), output: z.object({ waiting: z.array(z.object({ managerId, workspaceId, workerId, workerTitle: string|null, requestId: string, text: string, at: string|null })) }) })`, using the existing `agentIdSchema` / `workspaceIdSchema`.
- plugin/server/chat-waiting.ts — `waitingOf(entries, workers)`:
  - `entries` are one Manager's timeline entries newest first (`{ item, timestamp }` as `readTimelinePages` returns them, reversed per page);
  - consider only `user_message` items whose `clientMessageId` is not a string and whose `text` is a string;
  - the message's report is the last `parseReports(text, ctx)` block whose `requestId` matches `/^req-\d{8}T\d{6}Z$/`; keep the NEWEST report per requestId (later messages of the same request hide older ones, whatever their phase);
  - keep it only when `phase === "blocked"` and `parseQuestions(text)` returns ≥ 1 question with a block `requestId` that is null or equal;
  - the Worker is the ONE entry of `workers` with role `worker`, that requestId and the Manager's workspace; none or several → skip; keep only status `idle` or `error`;
  - output `{ managerId, workspaceId, workerId, workerTitle, requestId, text, at }`.
  `handleChatWaiting(paseo)`: `bmAgentsOf(paseo)`; Worker requestId from the `bm.requestId` label (as `chat.peers`, falling back to `requestIdOfAgent` with trace records when readable); for each Manager not archived and not `closed`, `readTimelinePages(paseo, id, { pages: 1, limit: 200 }, visit)` collecting entries newest first, then `waitingOf`; one Manager failing costs only that Manager.
- plugin/server/chat-rpc.ts — `server.handle(chatWaitingRpc, (_input, context) => handleChatWaiting(sdk(context)))`.
- test/plugin-chat-waiting.test.ts — new.
- test/plugin-bundle-cjs.test.ts, test/rpc-list-describe.test.ts — add "chat.waiting" to their RPC name lists.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
none.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Server code imports only `plugin/shared/*` and `plugin/server/*` (never `plugin/client/*`); `parseReports` is in plugin/shared/bm-report.ts, `parseQuestions` in plugin/shared/bm-questions.ts.
- Read-only: no writes, no messages sent, no network beyond the daemon RPC.
- Check the AgentFacts fields (status, archivedAt/archived, workspaceId, title, requestIdLabel) in plugin/server/traces.ts before use; do not invent fields.
- Another Worker (req-20260918T043115Z) has uncommitted changes elsewhere; run `git status` first; these files are not among them (contracts.ts, chat-rpc.ts unmodified at planning time).

## Acceptance Criteria
- `waitingOf`: blocked + questions + idle Worker → one entry with the report text; Worker running / initializing / closed → none; a newer `received`/`finished` report of the same request → none; blocked without a question block → none; a typed user message (clientMessageId) with a report → ignored; two Workers with the request → none; a question block for another request → none; error status → included.
- `handleChatWaiting` with a fake paseo: two Managers in two workspaces each with one waiting Worker → both; a Manager whose timeline read throws → the other Manager's entries still returned; archived Manager skipped.
- `chat.waiting` registered; the two RPC-name tests list it.
- `npx vitest run test/plugin-chat-waiting.test.ts test/plugin-bundle-cjs.test.ts test/rpc-list-describe.test.ts`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run typecheck:plugin`, `npm run lint` exit 0.

## Validation / Definition of Done
The tests above, typecheck, typecheck:plugin and lint exit 0.

## Primary Proof
test/plugin-chat-waiting.test.ts green, including a watched negative control: dropping the "newest report per request" rule makes the "newer report hides the blocked one" case fail.

## Reversibility
Remove chat-waiting.ts, the contract, the registration and the tests; nothing persisted.

title: Show a composer pill per waiting Worker that opens its question card in a popover
description:
## Objective
Show, in each paseo-bm Manager's chat, one composer pill per Worker waiting for an answer ("<Worker> · <n> questions"), refreshed every 15 s from `chat.waiting`, whose popover draws that Worker's question card so the user can answer it there.

## Context

Paseo 0.8 gives `PluginClientContext.addComposerPill({ id, workspaceId, agentId, button })` with `update`/`remove`, and `button.behavior = { kind: "popover", Content }`; it has no way to scroll the chat to a card, so the popover replaces scrolling. The popover reuses `ChatCardView`, so answering there goes through the card's own Reply path (status re-read, BM-ANSWERS block, Answered chip).

## Scope
In: new plugin/client/waiting-pills.tsx (pure `planPills`, `registerWaitingPills`, popover Content); two lines in plugin/index.client.tsx (import + push the cleanup into the removers list); tests for `planPills`.
Out: the RPC (`chat.waiting`, `bm-wp-256-waiting-pills-mkgt.1`); any other part of index.client.tsx (uncommitted work of Worker req-20260918T043115Z — owner accepted editing on top of it, Q15 b: add only these two lines); scrolling; persistence.

  - `registerWaitingPills(client)`: run once now, then every `WAITING_POLL_MS` (skip a tick while the previous run is pending); `client.rpc(chatWaitingRpc, {})`; apply the plan with `client.addComposerPill({ id, workspaceId, agentId: managerId, button: { title: "Questions from <Worker> about <requestId>", icon: WAITING_PILL_ICON, label, behavior: { kind: "popover", Content } } })`, `registration.update({ ...same fields })`, `registration.remove()`; an RPC failure keeps the current pills; returns a cleanup that clears the timer and removes every pill;
  - popover `Content({ theme, layout, agentId, close })`: builds the card from the entry's text and renders `ChatCardView` with `agentId` = the Manager, `item = { type: "plugin", kind: CHAT_CARD_KIND, version: CHAT_CARD_VERSION, data: card }`, `timestamp = new Date(at ?? Date.now())`.
- plugin/index.client.tsx — `import { registerWaitingPills } from "./client/waiting-pills";` and `registerWaitingPills(client),` appended to the removers array.
- test/plugin-waiting-pills.test.ts — new; must not import `react-native` as a value (import the pure functions from a module that does not import react-native, e.g. split pure logic into plugin/client/waiting-pills-model.ts if needed).

## Dependencies / Prerequisites

## Assumptions / Constraints
- React Native primitives only; theme colours; no new dependency; hooks rules inside Content.
- The popover's providers (usePaseo, useRpc, React Query) are assumed to match the timeline's; not verifiable without the daemon — the owner checks it; the pill alone still says who is waiting.

description:

title: Replace the Reply button with an Answered chip once a reply went out from the card
description:
## Objective
Once a reply went out from a chat card, hide its "Reply to …" button and show a small "Answered" chip directly under the status chip in the card's top-right column; pressing the chip reopens the Reply box.

## Context
Owner point 4 and decision Q14 (a) (PRD delta §1.3). A card only knows what was sent from itself in the open app session, like the existing "answered" memory of the question card (REQ-059d).

## Scope
In: a pure helper in plugin/client/chat-cards.ts, `ChatCardView` in plugin/client/chat-card.tsx, tests.
Out: remembering replies across an app reload; knowing about answers given in another place (the Worker's own chat, the Manager); the header layout itself (done by `bm-wp-257-card-b4-zwx7.1`, which this one depends on).

## Components Touched
- plugin/client/chat-cards.ts — `export function replyControls(canReply: boolean, replied: boolean): { replyButton: boolean; answeredChip: boolean }`: `canReply && !replied` → button only; `canReply && replied` → chip only; `!canReply` → neither.
- plugin/client/chat-card.tsx — module map `replied = new Map<string, Date>()` keyed by `answeredKey(agentId, card)`; state `repliedAt` initialised from it (before the early return); after a successful `sendReply` from the Reply box set both; the Reply button renders only when `replyButton`; the "Answered" chip (`Chip`, tone `success`, text "Answered") renders under the status chip in the right-hand column when `answeredChip`, and `onPress` → `setReplying(true)`.
- test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts — `replyControls` cases.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
`bm-wp-257-card-b4-zwx7.1` ("Redraw the chat card header …") must be closed first: it creates the right-hand column under the status chip where the "Answered" chip goes.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- "Replied" = any successful `sendReply` from this card, with or without a BM-ANSWERS block; the question card's "Answered at HH:MM → …" line stays as it is.
- Session-only, like the answered memory; no persistence.
- React Native primitives only; do not edit ui.tsx, bead-chips.tsx or index.client.tsx. Run `git status` first.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `replyControls` returns exactly the three outcomes above for all four input combinations.
- After a successful send the Reply button is gone and the "Answered" chip is under the status chip; pressing it shows the Reply box with Send and Cancel; a failed send changes nothing.
- `npx vitest run test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts`, `npm run typecheck:plugin`, `npm run lint` exit 0.

## Validation / Definition of Done
The chat-card tests, typecheck:plugin and lint exit 0; the JSX read back.

## Primary Proof

title: Colour each bead row and its status chip by status, and drop bold bead titles
description:
## Objective
Colour every bead row of the Beads screen list and of the "Beads in this chat" panel by status (a light tint over the whole row plus a 4 px bar on the left), give the status chip the same colour everywhere, and draw bead titles in those lists and in the chat-chip detail box without bold.

## Context
The owner scans up to 200 bead rows and wants to see at a glance which are not started, in progress, blocked or closed; bold titles tire the eye (owner decisions Q3 a, Q4 a, Q6 a). Today only a small chip shows status, and its tones (In progress = info, Blocked = warning) differ from the colours the owner chose.

## Scope
In:
- one status → tone table shared by rows and chips;
- the row frame and the title style;
- applying them to the Beads screen list, `ChatBeadsPanel` rows and the `BeadInline` title;
- tests.

Out:
- `plugin/client/chat-card.tsx` and `chat-cards.ts` (another Worker's area; the chips in chat cards change through `statusBadge` alone);
- how beads are bucketed (`statusBucket` stays as is);
- the colours of workspace-row figures in `dashboard-view.ts`;
- the facet chips of the filter bar;
- any header or navigation change (other leaves).

## Components Touched
- `plugin/client/beads-model.ts`:
  - export `type StatusBucket` = the return type of `statusBucket`;
  - `STATUS_TONE: Readonly<Record<StatusBucket, Tone>> = { ready: "info", in_progress: "warning", blocked: "danger", closed: "success" }`;
  - `ROW_TINT_OPACITY = 0.12`;
  - `beadRowLook(bead) → { tone: STATUS_TONE[statusBucket(bead)], muted: bucket === "closed" }`;
  - `statusBadge` keeps its texts (Ready / In progress / Blocked / Closed) and takes its tone from `STATUS_TONE[statusBucket(bead)]`.
- `plugin/client/ui.tsx`:
  - new `TintedCard({ tone, theme, styles, children })`: a `View` with `[styles.card, { overflow: "hidden", borderLeftWidth: 4, borderLeftColor: colour }]`, whose FIRST child is an absolutely filled `View` with `pointerEvents="none"`, `backgroundColor: colour`, `opacity: ROW_TINT_OPACITY`, then `children`; `colour = toneColor(theme, tone)`;
  - new `beadTitleStyle(styles, theme, muted)` → `[styles.sectionTitle, { fontWeight: "400", color: muted ? theme.colors.foregroundMuted : theme.colors.foreground }]`.
- `plugin/client/beads-screen.tsx`: only the list-row block in `BeadsScreen`. The row's `View style={styles.card}` becomes `TintedCard` with `beadRowLook(bead).tone`; the title `Text` uses `beadTitleStyle(styles, theme, look.muted)` instead of `[styles.sectionTitle, { fontWeight: "600" }]`.
- `plugin/client/bead-chips.tsx`:
  - `ChatBeadsPanel` rows: same two changes;
  - `BeadInline` title: `beadTitleStyle` only, no tint.
- `test/plugin-beads-screen.test.ts`: new cases.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
none.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Colours come only from `theme.colors` through `toneColor`. The theme's colour-string format is not promised, so never build an alpha colour string; the overlay's `opacity` does the tint (same pattern as `RoleMark` in `ui.tsx`).
- Keep the list row's existing `Pressable`, expand/collapse and `BeadDetailPanel`: the detail stays inside the tinted frame.
- `test/plugin-launcher.test.ts` loads every client `.tsx` with `vi.mock("react-native")` providing only `ActivityIndicator`, `Pressable`, `ScrollView`, `Text`, `View`. No module-level use of any `react-native` value; use them only inside component bodies.
- No file under `test/` imports `react-native` as a value (AGENTS.md).
- React Native primitives only, no web-only constructs (`className`, `onClick`, `document.`, `window.`), no `server/` import (`test/plugin-structure.test.ts`).
- Another Worker (req-20260918T041426Z) edits `chat-cards.ts` / `chat-card.tsx`. Run `git status` before starting; do not touch those files.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `beadRowLook` gives four distinct tones: `ready` → `info`, `in_progress` → `warning`, `blocked` (both status `blocked` and an open bead that is not ready) → `danger`, `closed` → `success`. `muted` is true only for `closed`.
- For one representative bead per bucket (including an open, not-ready bead), `statusBadge(b).tone === beadRowLook(b).tone`, and `statusBadge(b).text` is unchanged from today (Ready / In progress / Blocked / Closed).
- Negative controls, each observed red and then restored:
  - setting `in_progress` back to `info` fails the tone case;
  - giving `statusBadge` its own tone fails the invariant case.
- The Beads screen list rows and the `ChatBeadsPanel` rows render inside `TintedCard`. Bead titles there and in `BeadInline` use `beadTitleStyle`; no `fontWeight: "600"` remains on a bead title in these two files.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- `npm test -- test/plugin-beads-screen.test.ts test/plugin-chat-beads.test.ts test/plugin-launcher.test.ts test/plugin-structure.test.ts` exits 0.
- `npm run typecheck:plugin` exits 0.
- `npm run typecheck` exits 0.
- `npm run lint` exits 0.

## Primary Proof
`test/plugin-beads-screen.test.ts` green with the new tone and invariant cases and both negative controls seen red, plus `npm run typecheck:plugin` exit 0 for the `.tsx` changes.

none. (Sequenced after the WP-260 leaf only to avoid editing `beads-screen.tsx` at the same time.)

title: Group the Beads list In progress, Blocked, Ready, Closed with an eye toggle that hides closed beads
description:
## Objective
Split the Beads screen list into four groups, In progress → Blocked → Ready → Closed. Each group opens with a divider and a "<label> · <count>" header. Add an eye button at the top of the list that hides closed beads by default and remembers the choice for the app session.

## Context
The owner wants work in progress on top, blocked work right below, each set visibly separated, and closed beads out of the way unless asked for (decisions Q9 a, Q10 a). Today the list is one flat sorted sequence, with a status chip per row.

## Scope
In:
- pure grouping;
- the session-scoped visibility store;
- the list heading row with the eye button;
- group dividers and headers;
- the empty text for "everything matching is closed and hidden";
- tests.

Out:
- the header "✓ done / total" figure and the 14-day chart (another leaf);
- the chat panel (no groups there);
- persisting the eye state across app reloads;
- filters, sort options and facet counts (unchanged; grouping happens after them).

## Components Touched
- `plugin/client/beads-model.ts` (pure, no React):
  - `export const STATUS_GROUP_ORDER: readonly StatusBucket[] = ["in_progress", "blocked", "ready", "closed"]`;
  - `export interface BeadGroup { bucket: StatusBucket; label: string; tone: Tone; total: number; beads: BeadRow[] }`;
  - `export function groupBeads(beads: readonly BeadRow[], options: { showClosed: boolean; limit: number }): { groups: BeadGroup[]; visible: number; closed: number; truncated: number }`:
    - the input is already filtered and sorted, and the order inside each group is kept;
    - groups come in `STATUS_GROUP_ORDER`, empty ones are dropped, and Closed is dropped when `!showClosed`;
    - `label` is the chip text (In progress, Blocked, Ready, Closed) and `tone` is `STATUS_TONE[bucket]`;
    - `visible` = beads in the shown groups before the limit; `closed` = closed beads in the input, whether shown or hidden;
    - the limit is spent across groups in display order; a group left with 0 beads by the limit is not returned; `total` is always the full group size; `truncated` = beads of shown groups cut by the limit.
  - `export const closedBeadsVisibility: { get(): boolean; set(show: boolean): void; subscribe(listener: () => void): () => void }` — one module-level value per loaded client bundle, default `false`; `set` notifies listeners.
- `plugin/client/beads-screen.tsx` (list part only):
  - `const showClosed = useSyncExternalStore(closedBeadsVisibility.subscribe, closedBeadsVisibility.get, closedBeadsVisibility.get)`;
  - `const grouped = groupBeads(shown, { showClosed, limit: LIST_LIMIT })`;
  - the heading row: `<grouped.visible> of <rows.length> beads`, then the eye button — a `Pressable` with `Icon` "EyeOff" when hidden / "Eye" when shown and the text `Closed <grouped.closed>`, `accessibilityRole="button"`, `accessibilityState={{ selected: showClosed }}`, and `accessibilityLabel` `Show closed beads (<n>)` or `Hide closed beads (<n>)`; pressing it calls `closedBeadsVisibility.set(!showClosed)`;
  - per group: a 1 px divider `View` (colour `theme.colors.border`), a header `Text` `<label> · <total>` in `styles.sectionTitle` coloured `toneColor(theme, group.tone)`, then the existing row cards for `group.beads`;
  - when `grouped.visible === 0 && grouped.closed > 0`: `All <closed> matching beads are closed. Show them with the eye button.`;
  - keep "This workspace has no beads yet." and the "Showing the first 200…" text, now driven by `grouped.truncated > 0`.
- `test/plugin-beads-screen.test.ts` — new cases (below).

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
none as an edge. Work it after the title-colour leaf of this epic only because both edit `beads-screen.tsx` and `beads-model.ts`.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- `Icon` comes from `@getpaseo/plugin/client/react-native`. "Eye" and "EyeOff" exist in Paseo 0.8's Lucide set (checked in the app bundle); `Icon` renders nothing for an unknown name.
- `useSyncExternalStore` comes from `react`.
- Sorting stays `sortBeads(filterBeads(rows, filter), sortKey, descending)`, and grouping runs on that result.
- `test/plugin-launcher.test.ts` loads client `.tsx` with `vi.mock("react-native")` providing only `ActivityIndicator`, `Pressable`, `ScrollView`, `Text`, `View`. No module-level use of a `react-native` value.
- No `react-native` value import under `test/`.
- Do not touch `chat-card.tsx` / `chat-cards.ts` / `roles/*.md` (another Worker). Run `git status` first.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `groupBeads` on beads of all four buckets, `showClosed: true`: groups are in the order in_progress, blocked, ready, closed, with labels In progress, Blocked, Ready, Closed and tones warning, danger, info, success. Inside a group the input order is kept.
- An empty bucket gives no group.
- `showClosed: false`: no Closed group, and `closed` still counts the closed beads.
- `limit: 3` over groups of sizes 2, 2, 1: the first group keeps 2 and the second keeps 1. The third, left with 0 beads, is not returned, and its bead counts in `truncated`. `total` values are full, so `truncated` = 2.
- `closedBeadsVisibility.get()` is `false` initially. `set(true)` notifies a subscriber and `get()` returns `true`. The test resets it to `false` afterwards.
- Negative controls, each observed red and then restored:
  - reversing `STATUS_GROUP_ORDER` fails the order case;
  - a default of `true` fails the visibility case.

## Validation / Definition of Done

- `npm run typecheck` exits 0.
- `npm run typecheck:plugin` exits 0.
- `npm run lint` exits 0.

## Primary Proof

title: Add a Beads header button to every open workspace that opens its Beads tab
description:
## Objective
Give every open workspace a "Beads" header button (icon only, `ListChecks`) that opens that workspace's Beads tab (`bm-beads` panel), and keep the buttons in step with the list of open workspaces.

## Context
The Beads tab was reachable only from the desktop "+" menu. On a phone the owner found no "+" at all: Paseo 0.8 mobile shows open tabs only, and its "…" Workspace actions sheet has a fixed item list. Read in the Paseo.app 0.8.0 bundle:
- the workspace header renders `PluginHeaderButtons` on mobile too, and on a narrow screen the first plugin button shows inline;
- `client.addHeaderButton` attaches a button to ONE workspace;
- `client.openPanel(panelId, { workspaceId })` opens a panel there.

The owner chose this button (Q14 a). It shows on desktop too, as a shortcut next to "+".

## Scope
In:
- new module `plugin/client/beads-header-button.ts`;
- its registration in `plugin/index.client.tsx`;
- new test file.

Out:
- the "+" menu and the `bm-beads` panel itself;
- `waiting-pills*` and chat-card files (another Worker);
- any label text on the button (icon only).

## Components Touched
- NEW `plugin/client/beads-header-button.ts` (no JSX):
  - `export const BEADS_HEADER_BUTTON_ID = "bm-beads-open"`;
  - `export const BEADS_HEADER_POLL_MS = 15_000`;
  - `export function beadsHeaderButton(openTab: () => void): PluginButton` → `{ title: "Open the Beads tab: beads and metrics of this workspace", icon: "ListChecks", behavior: { kind: "action", onPress: openTab } }`, with no `label`;
  - `export function planHeaderButtons(shown: ReadonlySet<string>, listed: ReadonlyArray<{ id: string; archivingAt?: string | null }>): { add: string[]; remove: string[] }` — `add` = listed workspaces without `archivingAt` that have no button; `remove` = shown ids no longer listed as open;
  - `export function registerBeadsHeaderButtons(client: PluginClientContext): () => void`:
    - keeps `Map<workspaceId, PluginButtonRegistration>`;
    - `refresh()` is guarded by `pending` and `stopped`; inside `try` it awaits `client.paseo.workspaces.list({})` and applies `planHeaderButtons` to `result.entries`;
    - for each added id it calls `client.addHeaderButton({ id: BEADS_HEADER_BUTTON_ID, workspaceId: id, button: beadsHeaderButton(() => client.openPanel(BEADS_TAB_PANEL_ID, { workspaceId: id })) })`; for each removed id, `registration.remove()`;
    - a failed read keeps the buttons as they are;
    - it runs `refresh()` now, every `BEADS_HEADER_POLL_MS` (timer `unref`), and on every `client.paseo.workspaces.subscribe(...)` event. The subscribe call sits inside `try`, so a client without `paseo` still loads;
    - cleanup sets `stopped`, clears the timer, unsubscribes, and removes every registration.
- `plugin/index.client.tsx` — add `registerBeadsHeaderButtons(client)` to `removers`, right after the `bm-beads` panel.
- NEW `test/plugin-beads-header-button.test.ts`.

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
none (WP-265's epic is closed; the `bm-beads` panel exists since WP-261).

## Assumptions / Constraints
- `BEADS_TAB_PANEL_ID` comes from `./dashboard-view`.
- Types come from `@getpaseo/plugin/client` (`PluginButton`, `PluginButtonRegistration`, `PluginClientContext`).
- `test/plugin-launcher.test.ts` and `test/agent-tree.test.ts` load the client entry with fake clients that have neither `paseo` nor `addHeaderButton`. Their expectations must stay untouched and green, so nothing may call them outside the guarded async refresh.
- No `react-native` value import anywhere in this module or the test.
- Do not touch another Worker's files. Run `git status` first.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `planHeaderButtons(new Set(["a","gone","c"]), [{ id: "a" }, { id: "b" }, { id: "c", archivingAt: "2026-09-19T00:00:00.000Z" }])` gives `{ add: ["b"], remove: ["gone", "c"] }`, and the same list with an empty `shown` gives `{ add: ["a", "b"], remove: [] }`. An archiving workspace is never added, and is removed if it had a button.
- With a fake client listing two open workspaces and one archiving, `registerBeadsHeaderButtons` adds exactly two buttons with id `bm-beads-open`, `icon` "ListChecks", no `label`, and `kind` action.
- Pressing a button calls `openPanel("bm-beads", { workspaceId })` for its own workspace.
- A later list without one workspace calls `remove()` on its button; a list that throws keeps the buttons; cleanup removes all.
- Negative control: `planHeaderButtons` never returning removals fails the removal case (observed red, then restored).
- `test/plugin-launcher.test.ts` and `test/agent-tree.test.ts` pass unchanged.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- `npm test -- test/plugin-beads-header-button.test.ts test/plugin-launcher.test.ts test/agent-tree.test.ts test/plugin-structure.test.ts test/plugin-bundle-cjs.test.ts` exits 0.
- `npm run typecheck` exits 0.
- `npm run typecheck:plugin` exits 0.
- `npm run lint` exits 0.

## Primary Proof
The new header-button tests green (with the negative control seen red), with the existing registration suites green and unchanged.

## Reversibility
Delete the new module and test, and remove the one line in `index.client.tsx`. The buttons disappear when the plugin reloads; no data involved.

title: chat.peers and chat.waiting choose a request's Worker by one rule that ignores archived agents
description:
## Objective
Introduce `soleWorkerOf` and a shared `peersOfWorkspace`, add `archived` to `chat.peers`, and use the one rule in `chat.waiting`, the card's reply target and the card's naming, so a pill and its card always agree on the one live Worker of a request.

## Context
F12: `chat.waiting` skips archived agents but `chat.peers` does not, so after a broken Worker is recreated with the same requestId and archived, a pill shows but its card refuses to send ("Cannot tell which Worker asked this"). Owner decision Q7 a: add `archived` to `chat.peers`; the recipient is the one live Worker; never send to an archived agent (sending unarchives it, ADR-005).

## Scope
In:
- new `plugin/shared/sole-worker.ts`: pure `soleWorkerOf(peers, requestId)` → the single NON-archived `worker` with that requestId, else `null` (none, several, or `requestId` null)
- `plugin/shared/contracts.ts`: `chatPeerSchema` gains `archived: z.boolean()`
- `plugin/server/chat-rpc.ts`: `peersOfWorkspace(all, workspaceId, readRecordsOnce)` returns that workspace's `ChatPeer`s (archived included, flagged), reading the trace store at most once and only when a non-manager agent lacks its `bm.requestId` label; `handleChatPeers` uses it
- `plugin/server/chat-waiting.ts`: `handleChatWaiting` builds its Worker list with `peersOfWorkspace` (only for workspaces with a live Manager, as the F11 leaf already does) and `waitingOf` picks the Worker with `soleWorkerOf`
- `plugin/client/chat-cards.ts`: `replyTarget` uses `soleWorkerOf`; `partiesOf` (naming only) uses `soleWorkerOf`, else the single Worker of that requestId even if archived, so an old card of an archived Worker keeps its name

Out:
- pill appearance and polling (owner kept them, Q18 b of req-20260918T041426Z)
- answer marks (batch b6)
- the `try/catch` around `readTimelinePages` (cleanup leaf)

## Components Touched
- `plugin/shared/sole-worker.ts` (new)
- `plugin/shared/contracts.ts`
- `plugin/server/chat-rpc.ts`
- `plugin/server/chat-waiting.ts`
- `plugin/client/chat-cards.ts`
- `test/plugin-chat-waiting.test.ts`
- `test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts`
- `test/plugin-dashboard-contracts.test.ts`

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
The F11 leaf (chat.waiting reads trace stores only for workspaces with a live Manager) must be closed: its read-count test guards this restructure of the same handler.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Work only after the baseline leaf (WP-270) is closed; never edit files of another request.
- Test conventions: tests load `.tsx` through a non-literal specifier (the root tsconfig has no `jsx`); no file under `test/` imports `react-native` as a value (`import type` is fine); a `.tsx` under `plugin/client/` must not use a `react-native` value at module scope, because `test/plugin-launcher.test.ts` mocks `react-native` with only `ActivityIndicator`, `Pressable`, `ScrollView`, `Text`, `View`.
- Run tests with `npm test -- <files>`, never `npx` (AGENTS.md).
- Write the new test first and watch it fail on the old code; record the negative control in the close reason.

title: A Manager launch requested while another launch is pending runs after it instead of being dropped
description:
## Objective
Make `runPendingRequest` leave a queued launch in its slot while the launcher is pending, and make the Beads Manager surface run it when the pending launch ends.

## Context
F2: `runPendingRequest` calls `requests.take()` before `launcher.launch()`, which returns "busy" while a launch is pending, so a request from the Command Center or `/bm-worker-new` that arrives meanwhile is lost.

## Scope
In:
- `runPendingRequest`: if `launcher.getState().status === "pending"` return `null` BEFORE `take()`
- `ManagerLauncherSurface`: the effect that runs queued launches subscribes to `launchRequests` AND to `managerLauncher`, so the queued request runs when the pending launch ends
- the slot keeps one value, so the newest request wins, as `put` does today

Out:
- the launch controller's own states and messages
- any queue other than `launchRequests`

## Components Touched
- `plugin/client/launch-manager.ts` — `runPendingRequest`

Make the chat card show its first two REAL beads and a "…" chip counting the remaining found beads, instead of cutting the raw id candidates to two before the lookup.

## Context
F10: `chat-card.tsx` slices `beadIdCandidates(card.text)` to 2 before `BeadChips` looks them up; the candidates are only a shape test, so `BM-REPORT`, `BM-QUESTIONS`, `local-first` come first. The card shows 0–1 real chips, a wrong count ("Show all 7 beads"), and a "…" even when no bead exists. REQ-059 (i): more than 2 related beads → 2 chips and a "…" chip.

## Scope
In:
- `plugin/client/chat-cards.ts`: make `visibleBeads` generic over the item type and add `beadChipsView(found: readonly BeadRow[], expanded: boolean): { shown: BeadRow[]; hidden: number }` that applies it to the FOUND beads; `BEAD_CHIPS_SHOWN` stays 2
- `plugin/client/bead-chips.tsx` `BeadChips`: takes all candidates (`ids`, still capped at 100 for the lookup) plus `expanded: boolean` and `onExpand(): void`; after `beads.lookup` it renders `beadChipsView(found, expanded).shown` and, when `hidden > 0`, the "…" chip (moved from `chat-card.tsx`, accessibilityLabel `Show all <found count> beads`); nothing at all when no bead is found
- `plugin/client/chat-card.tsx`: pass every candidate and the expanded state; remove its own "…" block and `visibleBeads` call

Out:
- `ChatBeadsPanel`
- which strings count as candidates (`beadIdCandidates`)

- `plugin/client/chat-cards.ts`
- `plugin/client/bead-chips.tsx`
- `plugin/client/chat-card.tsx`
- `test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts`

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
The baseline leaf (WP-270) must be closed.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Work only after the baseline leaf (WP-270) is closed; never edit files of another request.
- Test conventions: tests load `.tsx` through a non-literal specifier (the root tsconfig has no `jsx`); no file under `test/` imports `react-native` as a value (`import type` is fine); a `.tsx` under `plugin/client/` must not use a `react-native` value at module scope, because `test/plugin-launcher.test.ts` mocks `react-native` with only `ActivityIndicator`, `Pressable`, `ScrollView`, `Text`, `View`.

- Never weaken or delete an existing assertion unless this bead names it.

- Chat-card rule: request req-20260918T041426Z (batch b6) and possibly req-20260918T071130Z changed this code after planning. Re-read the code first; if the finding is already fixed, close this leaf with the code read as evidence ("no longer applies"); a NEW finding is asked of the owner, never added silently.

title: Phase 2a-11: the plugin enforces the coordination conventions between agents
description:

title: Recognise unlabelled bm-* agents by provider in bmAgentsOf, chat.peers and chat.waiting
description:
## Objective
Add `plugin/server/agent-role.ts` (`ROLE_BY_PROVIDER`, `roleOfAgent`, `listAllAgents`) and make `bmAgentsOf` list every agent once across all pages, keep those with a role, and mark each `labelled`; `chat.peers` returns `labelled` on the owner and on every peer.

## Context
Manager f13a4e4e of workspace "Refactor Dependency" was started from Paseo's new-agent flow with the Manager profile and has `labels: {}`. `bmAgentsOf` (plugin/server/dashboard-rpc.ts:293-326) lists only by the `bm.role` label, one page of 200 per role, so `chat.peers` returned `{ owner: null }` and no chat card was drawn (investigation bead bm-llmg).

## Scope
In scope:
- `plugin/server/agent-role.ts` (new):
  - `type BmRole = "manager" | "worker" | "reviewer"`; `interface RoleFact { role: BmRole; labelled: boolean }`;
  - `ROLE_BY_PROVIDER = { "bm-manager": "manager", "bm-worker": "worker", "bm-reviewer": "reviewer" }`, moved out of `plugin/server/role-hook.ts`, which now imports it;
  - `roleOfAgent(agent)`: (1) label `bm.role` is one of the three roles → `{ role, labelled: true }`; (2) else `providerId(agent.provider)` (plugin/server/provider-id.ts, strips `/<model>`) is a key of `ROLE_BY_PROVIDER` → `{ role, labelled: false }`, also when `bm.role` holds an unknown value; (3) else `null`; never throws on malformed input;
  - `listAllAgents(list, { includeArchived })`: moved from `plugin/server/manager.ts` (which imports it back, behaviour unchanged there); calls `agents.list` WITHOUT a labels filter, page limit 200, follows `pageInfo.nextCursor` while `pageInfo.hasMore`; a page without `pageInfo` is the last page.
- `bmAgentsOf`: one `listAllAgents({ includeArchived: true })`; keep entries whose `roleOfAgent` is not null; `AgentFacts.role` is the resolved role; `AgentFacts` gains `labelled: boolean`. `DashboardPaseo.agents.list` accepts an optional `filter.labels` and an optional `pageInfo` in the result.
- `plugin/server/chat-rpc.ts` `peerOf`: adds `labelled`.
- `plugin/shared/contracts.ts` `chatPeerSchema`: `labelled: z.boolean().default(true)`.
- Tests.
Out of scope:
- `manager.ensure` selection, the agent tree, `/bm-worker-stop-all`, the client chip, labelling agents (other beads of this epic).

## Components Touched

- plugin/server/dashboard-rpc.ts — `bmAgentsOf`, `AgentFacts`, `DashboardPaseo`
- plugin/server/chat-rpc.ts — `peerOf`

- test/agent-role.test.ts (new); existing test/plugin-chat-cards.test.ts, test/plugin-chat-waiting.test.ts, dashboard tests that fake `agents.list`

- `chat.waiting` and the Dashboard keep calling `bmAgentsOf` and need no other change.
- TypeScript ESM, Node >= 22; no new dependency; no network.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Send BM-FORMAT to the sender of a block that breaks the template
description:
## Objective
Add `plugin/server/format-check.ts`, registered on `agent.turn_ended`: check the blocks of the ended turn with `checkBlocks`, keep one pending notice per (sender, requestId, kind) for the latest malformed block, and send the `BM-FORMAT` notice to the sender only when it is not running and the block is still the latest.

## Context
Owner decisions Q2 a and Q8 a. Only verified timeline shapes are used: `user_message` without `clientMessageId` (sent by another agent) and `assistant_message`; the raw shape of a `send_agent_prompt` tool call is NOT verified and must not be used.

## Scope
In scope:
- Detection (per ended turn, items read the way plugin/server/collector.ts does: refetch entries of the turn when available, else `sliceLastTurn(event.timeline)`):
  - Manager turn: `user_message`s without `clientMessageId` that are not plugin notices (`isPluginNotice`) → `BM-REPORT` (+ `BM-QUESTIONS`); sender = the ONE Worker of the workspace with that requestId (label `bm.requestId`, else `requestIdOfAgent` from trace records, as `chat.peers` does).
  - Worker turn: same source → `BM-ANSWERS`; sender = the Worker's `paseo.parent-agent-id` if `roleOfAgent` says manager.
  - Reviewer turn: its own `assistant_message`s → `BM-REVIEW`; sender = the Reviewer itself.
  - Not exactly one sender → no notice, one log line.
- Latest only: per (sender, requestId, kind) only the last block of the turn counts; valid → drop pending; malformed → replace pending with its issues and a MARK = `lastUserMessageAt` of the side that checked it (Manager / Worker / the Reviewer itself).
- Re-evaluation at: (1) the turn end where it was checked; (2) the next turn end of the recipient side — Manager for reports, Worker for answers, the Reviewer's parent Worker (`paseo.parent-agent-id`) for reviews; (3) the next turn end of the sender itself — there, if `refresh()` still says running, re-read up to 5 times, 1 s apart.
- Send only if the sender is not `running`/`initializing` (`refresh()`). At the sender's OWN turn end (trigger 3, sender is neither checker nor receiver) also require the checking side's `lastUserMessageAt` to still equal the mark; if it changed, keep the notice for the checking side's next turn end, whose detection replaces or clears it (implementation errata, design §4.7: dropping here lost the notice whenever Paseo's own "Worker finished" message reached the Manager).
- Limits: each block text (hash) notified at most once; each (sender, requestId, kind) at most 2 times; beyond → log `[paseo-bm] <kind> from <id> still breaks the template after 2 notices; not asking again`. All state in memory.
- Notice text exactly:
```
BM-FORMAT requestId: <requestId>
Your last <kind> broke the template:
- <field>: <issue>
Send the whole corrected block again, to the same agent as before, in one message. Change nothing else and do not redo any work; then carry on exactly where you were.
```
  For a Reviewer the last line is `Answer with the whole corrected BM-REVIEW block as your final message; do not review again.`
- `plugin/server/notices.ts`: add `BM-FORMAT` to the plugin-notice prefixes, so the collector records it as the plugin's and `reviewCallsOf` does not count it.
- `plugin/index.server.ts`: register and clean up.
Out of scope:
- Blocking a message before it reaches its recipient (impossible in Paseo). Role instructions (another bead).

## Components Touched
- plugin/server/format-check.ts (new)
- plugin/server/notices.ts
- plugin/index.server.ts
- test/format-check.test.ts (new)

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- Bead bm-wp-277-agent-conventions-pbst.1 (the resolver: `roleOfAgent`, `bmAgentsOf`) and bead bm-wp-277-agent-conventions-pbst.8 (the checker: `checkBlocks`) must be done first.

## Assumptions / Constraints
- `PaseoAgentHandle.send()` on a running agent REPLACES its turn: never send to a running or initializing agent.
- Paseo reuses turn ids inside one agent: never key state on (agentId, turnId).
- Reports: the Manager is woken after every Worker turn (default notifyOnFinish); reviews: the parent Worker is woken when its Reviewer finishes — these guarantee a re-evaluation after the sender is idle. Answers have no such guarantee (known limitation: chip + log).
- TypeScript ESM, Node >= 22; no new dependency; no network.
- plugin/client/** must never import from plugin/server/** (compile error); files under test/ must not import `react-native` as a value (`import type` only).
- Lifecycle hooks and RPC handlers never throw; a failure costs one `console.warn` line starting `[paseo-bm]`.
- The working tree holds uncommitted changes of other requests: edit on top of them, never revert, reformat or stage them.
- Before the first code edit of this bead, list the agents of this workspace; if another `bm-worker` (not you) is `running` or `initializing`, send `blocked` and wait (owner decision Q10 a).

## Acceptance Criteria
- F3: a blocked report missing `(recommended)` → at the Manager's turn end, the idle Worker gets exactly one BM-FORMAT with that issue; after a corrected resend, the next Manager turn end drops the pending notice.
- F4: still wrong after 2 notices → no third notice, the log line.
- Sender running at check → nothing sent; sent at a later turn end once idle; Reviewer still `running` at its own turn end → sent at its parent Worker's next turn end; Manager `running` at a Worker turn end → sent at the Manager's own next turn end; `refresh()` running then idle on re-read → sent.
- A bad `received` followed by a good `blocked` → no notice about `received` (not at the Worker's own turn end because the Manager got a newer message; cleared by the Manager's next detection).
- A `user_message` WITH `clientMessageId` is never checked; a block with no single sender → no notice.
- `isPluginNotice("BM-FORMAT …")` is true; `reviewCallsOf` does not count a BM-FORMAT sent to a Reviewer.
- Nothing throws on malformed events.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- `npm run verify` exits 0 (typecheck, typecheck:plugin, lint, test, build).

## Primary Proof
test/format-check.test.ts with a fake Paseo (agents, refresh, send) and fake timelines.

## Reversibility
Revert the new module and the edits; all state is in memory.

## Provenance
Request: req-20260918T071130Z — "Hãy làm thật chặt về việc thiếu và sai nguyên tắc khi tương tác phối hợp giữa các Agent, việc không tuân thủ convension, template khi truyền đạt thông tin là điệu CỰC KỲ NGUY HIỂM và KHÔNG CHẤP NHẬN"
Source: docs/plans/paseo-bm-implementation-plan-delta-20260918g-agent-conventions.md#WP-280
Requirements: REQ-061 (f)
Design refs: docs/design/paseo-bm-delta-20260918g-agent-conventions.md §4.7, K9, K10, K11, K12, K17
close_reason: plugin/server/format-check.ts on agent.turn_ended: detects (sliceLastTurn items; user_message without clientMessageId and not a plugin notice, or the Reviewer's own assistant_message) the latest BM-REPORT(+its BM-QUESTIONS)/BM-ANSWERS/BM-REVIEW per sender/request/kind via checkBlocks; sender = the one Worker of the request (label or trace records) / the Worker's Manager parent / the Reviewer; pending notice with mark = checker lastUserMessageAt; re-evaluated at the checker's, the receiver's (Reviewer -> parent Worker) and the sender's own turn end; never sends to a running/initializing sender (own turn end: up to 5 re-reads, 1 s apart), never to an archived/closed one; one notice per block hash, max 2 per sender/request/kind; send failure -> log, retried later; notice text as designed. notices.ts: FORMAT_NOTICE_MARKER 'BM-FORMAT' in the plugin-notice prefixes. index.server.ts registers it. Implementation errata recorded in design §4.7, plan and this bead: the mark is only checked at the sender's own turn end and a change there keeps (not drops) the notice, because Paseo's own 'Worker finished' message also moves the mark. test/format-check.test.ts 19/19 (fake Paseo): F3 + corrected resend clears; typed and BM-BUDGET messages skipped; MAX_NOTICES then log; same block once; no single sender -> none; running Worker -> sent at the Manager's next turn end after a 'finished' message; sent at the Worker's own turn end; own-turn re-reads until idle; bad received then good blocked -> no notice; archived -> none; Reviewer told at its turn end, or at the parent Worker's when still running; Worker's own messages and incoming reviews not checked; bad BM-ANSWERS -> Manager told; malformed events never throw; send failure retried; register/cleanup. isPluginNotice(BM-FORMAT) true and reviewCallsOf counts 0. Hook inventories now count 3 turn_ended handlers. npm run verify exit 0 (typecheck, typecheck:plugin, lint, 102 files / 2334 tests, build).

title: Teach the three roles what a BM-FORMAT message is
description:

description:
## Objective
When `modesFor("bm-reviewer")` fails, `runtimeFactsOf("worker")` still returns a `reviewerModeId`: first from the last mode list read successfully in this plugin run, else the static `auto`; every failure, including an unexpected throw, leaves one log line.

## Context

description:
## Objective
Register `on("agent.created")` in a new `plugin/server/agent-labels.ts`: for a `bm-*` agent whose snapshot has no valid `bm.role`, run one `paseo agent update <id> --label bm.role=<role> [--label bm.modeSet=<mode>] --json` through `plugin/server/paseo-cli.ts`, and log the outcome.

## Context
Paseo's `before("agent.create")` hook can change only `{ config, env }`, never labels, so an agent created from Paseo's own new-agent flow with a paseo-bm profile has no labels (owner decision Q1 b). `paseo agent update --label` adds or sets labels and never removes others (checked with `paseo agent update --help`, Paseo 0.8.0).

## Scope
In scope:
- `plugin/server/agent-labels.ts` (new), handler for `agent.created` (`{ agent: { id, workspaceId, parentAgentId, provider, cwd, title } }`, context `{ paseo }`):
  1. `role = ROLE_BY_PROVIDER[providerId(agent.provider)]`; none → return without any call;
  2. `snapshot = await paseo.agents.ref(id).refresh()`; `snapshot.agent.labels["bm.role"]` already one of the three roles → return;
  3. labels to set: `bm.role=<role>`; for `manager` also `bm.modeSet=<mode>` with mode = `runtimeInfo.modeId`, else `currentModeId`; no mode → no `bm.modeSet`;

  Each id is handled at most once per plugin run (in-memory set). The handler never throws.

title: Add the strict BM-* template checker plugin/shared/bm-format.ts
description:
## Objective
Create the pure module `plugin/shared/bm-format.ts` exporting `checkBlocks(message): CheckedBlock[]` that finds every `BM-REPORT`, `BM-QUESTIONS`, `BM-ANSWERS` and `BM-REVIEW` block in a message and returns, per block, the list of template violations.

## Context
Owner decisions Q2 a and Q7 a: the plugin checks every block agents send each other against the templates in plugin/roles/*.md. The existing parsers (plugin/shared/bm-report.ts, bm-questions.ts) are deliberately tolerant and must not change; this checker is separate and strict.

## Scope
In scope:
- Types: `BlockKind`; `FormatIssue { kind; field: string | null; message: string }` (English message, it is sent to agents); `CheckedBlock { kind; requestId: string | null; text; issues }`.
- Block finding: a block starts at a line holding only `BM-REPORT`, `BM-QUESTIONS`, `BM-ANSWERS` or `BM-REVIEW` (a leading `>` or a code fence right before it is allowed); it ends at a blank line, a code fence or the start of another block; `BM-REVIEW` may contain blank lines inside `findings:`; `BM-REVIEW STOPPED` alone is a valid block. Skip template blocks — any value line listing choices with `|` (like `phase: received | beads-done | …`).
- Rules:
  - BM-REPORT: exactly the 12 fields `requestId, phase, tier, filesChanged, beadsCreated, beadsUpdated, beadsClosed, beadsReady, reviewFindingsOpen, buildAndTests, skillsUsed, blockers`, each once, no unknown field, in THIS order; `requestId` matches `^req-\d{8}T\d{6}Z$`; `phase` ∈ received, beads-done, blocked, finished; `tier` matches `^(Small|Medium|Large) \(changed: (no|from (Small|Medium|Large), .+)\)$`; the four bead fields are `none` or comma-separated full bead ids (`BEAD_ID` of bm-report.ts; no `.3` shorthand, no comment text); `skillsUsed` `none` or names `[a-z0-9-]+`; `reviewFindingsOpen` `none` or `b<n>: …` items separated by `;`; `filesChanged`, `buildAndTests`, `blockers` non-empty; `phase: blocked` → the same message carries a `BM-QUESTIONS` block, and `blockers` starts `<n> question(s): Q…, Q… — see BM-QUESTIONS` listing exactly that block's ids.
  - BM-QUESTIONS: `requestId:` present and equal to the report's; 1–5 questions, one line `Q<n>: <text>` each, ids unique and ascending; each question ≥ 2 options, one line `- <letter>: <text>` each, letters consecutive from `a`; exactly one option ending `(recommended)` per question.
  - BM-ANSWERS: valid `requestId:` line; every other line `Q<n>: <letter> — <text>` or `Q<n>: other — <text>`; ids unique; at least one line.
  - BM-REVIEW: fields `requestId, batchId, reviewKind, verdict, checked, findings, notChecked`, each once; `batchId` `^b\d+$`; `reviewKind` ∈ first, re-review; `verdict` ∈ pass, changes-required; `findings: none` or items each with `severity` (blocking | non-blocking), `location`, `reason`, `suggestedFix`; `verdict` is `changes-required` iff at least one finding is blocking.
- `none` compares case-insensitively. At most 20 000 characters are checked; longer → check the start and add `message too long to check`. Never throws.
Out of scope:
- Using the checker in cards or notices (other beads). Changing bm-report.ts / bm-questions.ts or the templates.

## Components Touched
- plugin/shared/bm-format.ts (new)
- test/bm-format.test.ts (new)

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- none

## Assumptions / Constraints
- Pure and environment-neutral: no React, no Node-only API, importable from plugin/client and plugin/server.
- The rules come only from the templates in plugin/roles/worker.md (BM-REPORT, BM-QUESTIONS), manager.md (BM-ANSWERS) and reviewer.md (BM-REVIEW); read them before writing the tests.
- TypeScript ESM, Node >= 22; no new dependency; no network.
- plugin/client/** must never import from plugin/server/** (compile error); files under test/ must not import `react-native` as a value (`import type` only).
- Lifecycle hooks and RPC handlers never throw; a failure costs one `console.warn` line starting `[paseo-bm]`.
- The working tree holds uncommitted changes of other requests: edit on top of them, never revert, reformat or stage them.
- Before the first code edit of this bead, list the agents of this workspace; if another `bm-worker` (not you) is `running` or `initializing`, send `blocked` and wait (owner decision Q10 a).

## Risks / Gotchas
- False positives cost an agent turn: every rule must be derived from the role-file templates, and the real-report fixtures must stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Every rule above has one failing case that yields exactly the expected issue (kind, field).
- These produce NO issue: the BM-REPORT / BM-QUESTIONS examples of worker.md filled with real values; a `blocked` report of five Vietnamese questions with options a–c and one `(recommended)` each (the shape Worker 9467dc77 sent on 2026-09-18); `received`, `finished` and `blocked` reports shaped like this request's own (tier `Small (changed: from Medium, …)`, `beadsCreated: bm-llmg`); a filled BM-REVIEW with `findings: none`; `BM-REVIEW STOPPED`; a BM-ANSWERS block as `answersText` (bm-questions.ts) writes it.
- A template block with `|` choices yields no block.
- Malformed input (empty, huge, binary-ish) never throws.

## Validation / Definition of Done
- `npm run typecheck:plugin`, `npm run lint`, `npx vitest run test/bm-format.test.ts` exit 0.

test/bm-format.test.ts.

title: Stopping a Worker with Paseo's stop does not stop its running Reviewer (REQ-026f)
description:
## Objective
When the user stops a Beads Worker with Paseo's normal stop (app Stop button or paseo stop), every Reviewer that Worker is running stops too, and no child agent keeps running.

## Context
Orchestration acceptance run 4, fixture F-8a (2026-09-15): the runner ran paseo stop on Worker b47f8335 at 14:14:57Z while its Reviewer 528af102 was running. Paseo only interrupted the Worker's turn, so the Worker had no turn to follow its Stop and propagate rule. The Reviewer was not cancelled; it finished its review on its own ~60 s later, and its finish notification woke the Worker again (the Worker then asked the user instead of continuing). Nothing was running at stop + 120 s only because the review was short. REQ-026(f) requires stopping a Worker to stop its Reviewers with no orphan agents. The role-instruction path (F-8b, a stop message) is separate.

## Scope
- Investigate what Paseo 0.8 offers a plugin when an agent is stopped/interrupted (server lifecycle hooks such as before/after agent stop or cancel, agent status events) and whether a plugin may cancel another agent.
- If supported: the paseo-bm plugin cancels running agents labelled bm.role=reviewer whose paseo.parent-agent-id is the stopped Worker; unit tests with a fake server context.
- If not supported: record the limitation in the design (errata) and README troubleshooting, and escalate as a design gap to the owner; do not invent an API.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Install paseo-bm, open Beads Manager, send a Medium request.
2. While a bm-reviewer agent created by the Worker is running, stop the Worker in Paseo.
3. Result: the Reviewer keeps running until its review ends and then wakes the Worker; expected: the Reviewer stops with the Worker.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Either the plugin stops the Worker's running Reviewers when the Worker is stopped, proven by tests and a live re-run of F-8a; or a verified statement that Paseo 0.8 offers no such hook, recorded as design errata and escalated.
- npm run build, typecheck, lint and tests pass for any code change.

## Provenance
Found by: bm-wp-117-9vy.2 orchestration acceptance run 4, F-8a (evidence ~/bm-acceptance/20260915/evidence-run4/F-8a/analysis.txt).
close_reason: Fixed in d754890 (A plugin agent.turn_ended hook sends a fixed stop notice to a stopped bm-worker's running bm-reviewer children; B worker.md/reviewer.md stop rules; E design §2.6 errata + Draft upstream request for a plugin agent cancel). Proof: npm test 1117 passed incl. plugin-stop-propagation (24) and bundle hook registration; typecheck/lint 0; CI 34993295765 success. Live F-8a re-run 5 on r5 payload: paseo stop on Worker 71476063 at 16:13:32Z while Reviewer 9b9ea3bb ran -> plugin sent the notice, Reviewer replied BM-REVIEW STOPPED and went idle ~4 s later (run 4: ~60 s, review completed); Worker woken once, cancelled nothing left, sent finished, asked the user, no further work; stop+120 s and +300 s 0 running, 0 new agents, git unchanged. Evidence ~/bm-acceptance/20260915/evidence-run5/F-8a/summary.txt. Known limitation (errata): interrupt via send, not a hard cancel, until Paseo offers a plugin cancel API.

comments.author: hieunguyentrung
comments.text: Investigation (Paseo 0.8 SDK + daemon, read-only): PARTIALLY SUPPORTED. Plugin can detect a canceled Worker turn via on('agent.turn_ended') outcome.kind='canceled' (lifecycle.d.ts), but PaseoAgentHandle has no cancel (only send/archive/...); cancelAgent exists only on the private DaemonClient; handle.send() to a running agent interrupts via replaceAgentRun but starts a new turn; archive is forbidden (ADR-005, REQ-026f). Cancel reason cannot distinguish user stop from message replace (re-read status: idle vs running). Paseo always sends a 'finished' notification to the parent when a child goes idle, so a stopped Worker is woken once. Options: A) plugin on turn_ended -> send a fixed stop notice to running bm-reviewer children (interrupt + one short turn; relies on reviewer.md); B) worker.md: when woken after a canceled turn, cancel_agent running Reviewers and send finished (real cancel but late); C) Reviewer polls parent (barred from Paseo tools); D) Manager-only (misses user stops); E) document as errata + README + upstream request for agent.cancel. Open design questions: does an interrupt + forced short reply count as 'stopped' under REQ-026f; stop notice wording; status re-read delay; what the woken Worker should do; log/error code; Manager stop same path; upstream ownership.

comments.author: hieunguyentrung
comments.text: Owner decision 2026-09-15: implement A + B + E. A = plugin hook on agent.turn_ended (canceled bm-worker, re-read status; if not running, send a fixed stop notice to running bm-reviewer children); B = worker.md rule: when woken after a canceled turn, cancel_agent any running Reviewers, send finished, do nothing else; reviewer.md recognises the stop notice; E = design errata + upstream request draft for a plugin agent.cancel. Then reinstall, re-run F-8a live, and uninstall/restore config at the end of acceptance.

Installed r5 tarball 16:10Z: plugin auto-reloaded (Plugin ready), payload has stop-propagation.ts, doctor exit 0. Live F-8a re-run (evidence-run5) in progress.

title: worker.md: Manager relay and peer finish notifications are read as a user Stop
description:
## Objective

`plugin/roles/worker.md` (Hard boundaries group 6) tells Worker to treat a turn
that "starts right after an interrupted turn — from a notification that a
Reviewer or another agent finished, or with no new instruction from the user" as
a stop. On a real daemon this matches Manager's ordinary behaviour, so Worker
halts mid-request when nothing stopped it.

## Steps to Reproduce

Observed five times during the WP-214 acceptance run (2026-09-16, real daemon,
`/tmp/bm-acc-20260916/repo`, Manager `06c0c92c`):

1. Send Manager a request; it delegates to a Worker.
2. While the Worker is working, send Manager any follow-up (in the run: a tier
   override). Manager relays it to the Worker with `send_agent_prompt`.
3. The Worker's turn is interrupted by the incoming message, so its next turn
   begins right after an interrupted turn.
4. The Worker reports `phase: finished` with `blockers: "STOPPED …"` and stops,
   with the request undelivered.

Also reproduced by a Reviewer finishing normally: the finish notification opens
the Worker's next turn, which the rule classifies as a stop, so the Worker does
not close the bead it had already implemented and reviewed.

Measured effect: request `req-20260916T064147Z` (one added docstring line)
needed four operator nudges to complete; three of the four stops happened when
the only remaining work was a single `br close` command. Request
`req-20260916T070544Z` stopped after 51k tokens, at the first step.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A message relayed by Manager, or a peer/sub-agent finish notification, does
  not by itself end the request: the Worker continues unless the message says it
  is stopping.
- A real user Stop (Paseo's Stop with no follow-up instruction) is still
  recognised and still triggers group 6 in full: cancel running Reviewers, touch
  nothing else, send `finished`.
- The distinction is stated in `worker.md` in a way that does not depend on
  wording of the incoming message alone.
- A test covers both directions: a relayed instruction continues the work, a
  bare interruption stops it.

## Notes

Out of scope for WP-214: this is the orchestration loop (`roles/worker.md`), not
the Dashboard, and the stop rule is product behaviour the owner approved. Raised
for the owner to decide rather than changed unilaterally.

The Dashboard is what surfaced it: the state column plus the workflow-step table
showed a request reported "finished" whose bead was never closed.

## Provenance

Found by the WP-214 Dashboard acceptance run; recorded in
`docs/operations/paseo-bm-dashboard-run-20260916.md` §3c "Phát hiện 2".
Not split from another bead.
close_reason: Fixed in plugin/roles/worker.md group 6: stop recognition is now a four-row table decided by what the turn brought — a stop message or an empty resume after a cut-off turn is a stop; an instruction (including one Manager relayed, a correction, a tier override or an answer to Worker's own question) and a bare peer finish notification are explicitly NOT stops. The Stop-conditions list and the finish-notification paragraph were made consistent, and the evidence (one real request halted five times, three of them with a single br close left) is kept beside the rule so it is not reasoned away. Verified: worker-instructions.ts regenerated by npm run build; test/roles-content-worker-implement.test.ts has a new bm-wqu case asserting the table order, the two not-a-stop rows and the Manager-relay rationale, plus the updated bm-wq6 cases; npm run typecheck, npm run lint and npm test all clean (1598 passing). Found by the WP-214 acceptance run and recorded in docs/operations/paseo-bm-dashboard-run-20260916.md section 3c.

title: install --help says preview only without --apply, but on a terminal install asks to apply and writes
description:
## Objective
The install help text describes what install actually does without --apply, so a user reading --help is not surprised.

## Context
Found while writing the README (bm-wp-118-4s4.1): install --help prints 'preview only without --apply', but src/commands/install/index.ts computes mayApply = flags.apply || interactive, so on a terminal install shows the plan, asks 'Apply these changes?' and writes on yes. This terminal behaviour is the designed and accepted flow (Phase 1a acceptance M-1: interactive install asks the confirmations). Without a terminal and without --apply it previews and exits 6. The help text is the part that is wrong.

## Scope
- Change the install help/usage text (and uninstall's if it has the same wording and the same behaviour) to say: without --apply, a terminal run shows the plan and asks before writing; a run without a terminal only previews (exit 6).

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Run npx paseo-bm install --help: it says preview only without --apply.
2. Run npx paseo-bm install on a terminal without --apply.
3. Result: it asks 'Apply these changes?' and writes on yes; expected: the help text matches this.

title: README: hướng dẫn cài đặt đúng cho một CLI chạy bằng npx, không phải npm i
description:
## Objective
Người đọc README biết ngay paseo-bm là CLI chạy một lần bằng npx, và không cài nhầm bằng npm i.

## Context
Trang npmjs.com tự sinh ô 'npm i paseo-bm' cho mọi gói, không đọc README và không tuỳ chỉnh được. Với paseo-bm thì lệnh đó sai mục đích: metadata gói có bin paseo-bm -> dist/index.js và main rỗng, nên không có gì để import. Owner đã gặp đúng lỗi này: chạy npm i paseo-bm trong repo khiến dự án tự thêm chính nó vào dependencies. Ngoài ra README đang dẫn npx paseo-bm@next vì lúc viết chưa publish; sau khi phát hành, dist-tag latest cũng trỏ 0.1.0-alpha.0 nên npx paseo-bm cho kết quả như nhau.

## Scope
- README.md: mục Install dẫn thẳng npx paseo-bm, giữ @next như ghi chú để ghim prerelease khi đã có bản ổn định.
- Thêm một dòng ngay đầu README: đây là CLI chạy bằng npx, không cài bằng npm i vào dự án, và nói rõ ô lệnh trên trang npm là mặc định của npm.
- Không đổi package.json, không đổi dist-tag.

## Acceptance Criteria
- README nêu rõ cách chạy đúng và cảnh báo không dùng npm i.
- Mọi lệnh trong README khớp thực tế registry hiện tại (latest và next đều trỏ 0.1.0-alpha.0).
- npm run build, lint và test xanh.

## Provenance
Source: câu hỏi của owner 2026-09-16 sau khi phát hành.
close_reason: Fixed in bd62fda: README now opens with a note that paseo-bm is a CLI run once with npx, exports nothing to import, and that the 'npm i paseo-bm' box on npmjs.com is generated automatically for every package (verified from the registry metadata: bin paseo-bm -> dist/index.js, main null, type module). Install section leads with 'npx paseo-bm' and explains that npx leaves nothing behind; @next kept as the way to pin prereleases once a stable release exists. Removed the two 'npx paseo-bm@latest' references (Updating, E_RECORD_SCHEMA_TOO_NEW) because latest currently resolves to the 0.1.0-alpha.0 prerelease. Every other npx line in the README is a subcommand (install/doctor/uninstall) and was already correct. npm run lint exit 0, npm test 1117 passed.
